children.text: pariśiṣṭam - 1
children.translated_text: Appendix - 1

children.text: namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

children.text: Abhisamayālaṅkārāntaḥ pātināṃ padārthānāṃ saṃkṣepato vivaraṇam
children.translated_text: A concise explanation of the topics contained within the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> (Ornament of Clear Realization)

children.text: sarvākārajñatādyaṣṭau padārthāḥ; cittotpādādayaḥ saptatiśca padārthā abhisamayālaṅkārasyābhidheyā santi / teṣāmiha svarūpaṃ saṃkṣepeṇa prastūyate /
children.translated_text: The eight topics beginning with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects), and the seventy topics beginning with <s>cittotpāda</s> (generation of the awakening mind), are the subjects expounded in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Their essential nature is here briefly presented.

children.text: aṣṭau padārthāḥ
children.translated_text: The eight topics

children.text: sarvākārajñatā, mārgajñatā, sarvajñatā (vastujñatā), sarvākārābhisambodhaḥ, mūrdhābhisamayaḥ, ānupūrvikābhisamayaḥ, ekakṣaṇābhisambodhaḥ, dharmakāyaścetyaṣṭau padārthā abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kārikābhyāṃ pradarśitāḥ / yathā -
children.translated_text: <s>Sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects), <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the paths), <s>sarvajñatā</s> (<s>vastujñatā</s>, knowledge of all [bases]), <s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s> (complete realization of all aspects), <s>mūrdhābhisamaya</s> (peak realization), <s>ānupūrvikābhisamaya</s> (sequential realization), <s>ekakṣaṇābhisambodha</s> (realization in a single moment), and <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth body) — these eight topics are displayed in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through two verses. Namely:

children.text: prajñāpāramitāṣṭābhiḥ padārthaiḥ samudīritā /
children.translated_text: The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) is set forth through eight topics:

children.text: sarvākārajñatā mārgajñatā sarvajñatā tataḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects), <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the paths), and then <s>sarvajñatā</s> (knowledge of all [bases]),

children.text: sarvākārābhisambodho mūrdhaprāpto 'nupūrvikaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sarvākārābhisambodha</s> (complete realization of all aspects), <s>mūrdhaprāpta</s> (peak attainment), <s>ānupūrvika</s> (sequential),

children.text: ekakṣaṇābhisambodho dharmakāyaśca te 'ṣṭadhā //
children.translated_text: <s>Ekakṣaṇābhisambodha</s> (realization in a single moment), and <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth body) — these are the eightfold [topics].

children.text: 1. sarvākārajñatā
children.translated_text: 1. <s>Sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects)

children.text: (ka) lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: (a) Definition

children.text: ekasminneva kṣaṇe yāvatpadārthākārāṇāṃ yathāvat sākṣātkāri paryantajñānaṃ sarvākārajñatāyā lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: The definition of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> is: the ultimate knowledge (<s>paryantajñāna</s>) that directly realizes as many aspects of topics as they are, in a single moment.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
yāvajjñānaṃ yathāvajjñānamiti sarvākārajñatāyā dvau bhedau / yā prajñā aśeṣākārān jānāti sā yāvajjñānam, yā ca yathā padārthānāṃ svarūpaṃ tathā jānātīti yathāvajjñānam /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
<s>Yāvajjñāna</s> (knowledge of the extent) and <s>yathāvajjñāna</s> (knowledge of the mode) are the two divisions of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. The wisdom that knows all aspects without remainder is <s>yāvajjñāna</s>; and that which knows the essential nature of topics just as they are is <s>yathāvajjñāna</s>.

children.text: athavā - cittotpādādihetūnāṃ anāsravaphalānāṃ ca aśeṣākārasākṣātkāri sarvākārajñānamityeko bhedaḥ / buddhabhūmau jāyamānāni dvāviṃśatiḥ anāsravajñānānīti dvitīyo bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the <s>sarvākārajñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects) that directly realizes the totality of aspects of the causes beginning with <s>cittotpāda</s> (generation of the awakening mind) and of the uncontaminated fruits — this is one division. The twenty-two uncontaminated knowledges that arise at the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage) constitute the second division.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
buddhabhūmāveva kevalaṃ sarvākārajñatā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
<s>Sarvākārajñatā</s> exists only at the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage) exclusively.

children.text: 2. mārgajñatā
children.translated_text: 2. <s>Mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the paths)

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
mārgatrayaniḥsvabhāvatvasākṣātkāriṇyā prajñayopāttatve sati āryamāhāyānikābhisamayatvaṃ mārgajñatāyā lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>mārgajñatā</s> is: the nature of an <s>āryamāhāyānika</s> (noble Mahāyāna [practitioner's]) realization, when it is taken up by the wisdom that directly realizes the essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>) of the three paths.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
catvāro 'syā bhedā bhavanti, yathā śrāvakamārgajñatā, pratyekabuddhamārgajñatā, mahāyānamārgajñatā, māhāyānikāryasantatisthasarvaprajñopāyajñatā ceti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are four divisions of this: <s>śrāvakamārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the <s>śrāvaka</s> path), <s>pratyekabuddhamārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> path), <s>mahāyānamārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> path), and the knowledge of all wisdom and means (<s>sarvaprajñopāyajñatā</s>) abiding in the continuum of a noble <s>Mahāyāna</s> [practitioner].

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
mahāyānadarśanamārgamārabhya buddhabhūmiṃ yāvat mārgajñatāyāḥ sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The range of <s>mārgajñatā</s> extends from the <s>mahāyānadarśanamārga</s> (Mahāyāna path of seeing) up to the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage).

children.text: 3. sarvajñatā (vastujñatā)
children.translated_text: 3. <s>Sarvajñatā</s> (<s>vastujñatā</s>, knowledge of all [bases])

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
samastadharmagatapudgalanairātmyasākṣātkāriṇyā prajñayopāttatvena hainayānikajātīyābhisamayasvarūpaṃ āryasantatisthaṃ jñānaṃ mārgajñatāyā lakṣaṇam / hainayānikāryasantatisthaṃ yajjñānaṃ tacchūnyatāyāḥ pudgalanairātmyāparaparyāyāḥ sākṣātkāri, tenopāttatvāt sarvajñatāyā lakṣaṇe hainayānikajātīyeti viśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>mārgajñatā</s> [here referring to <s>sarvajñatā</s>] is: knowledge abiding in the continuum of a noble one (<s>ārya</s>), having the nature of a realization belonging to the <s>Hīnayāna</s> class, taken up by the wisdom that directly realizes the <s>pudgalanairātmya</s> (non-self of persons) pervading all <s>dharmas</s>. The knowledge abiding in the continuum of a <s>Hīnayāna</s> noble one directly realizes <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), which is a synonym of <s>pudgalanairātmya</s>; because it is taken up by that [wisdom], the qualifier 'belonging to the <s>Hīnayāna</s> class' appears in the definition of <s>sarvajñatā</s>.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
phalabhūtāyā jinajananyā dūratvam avidūratvaṃ ceti sarvajñatāyā dvau bhedau /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
Distance (<s>dūratva</s>) and nearness (<s>avidūratva</s>) from the resultant <s>jinajanī</s> (mother of the conquerors) are the two divisions of <s>sarvajñatā</s>.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
śrāvakīyadarśanamārgamārabhya buddhabhūmiparyantaṃ sarvajñatāyāḥ sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The range of <s>sarvajñatā</s> extends from the <s>śrāvaka</s> path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) up to the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage).

children.text: 4. sarvākārābhisambodhaḥ
children.translated_text: 4. <s>Sarvākārābhisambodha</s> (complete realization of all aspects)

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
trisarvajñatākārāṇāṃ bhāvanāmayyā prajñayopāttaḥ sattvayogaḥ sarvākārābhisambodha iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s> is: a <s>sattvayoga</s> (mental engagement of a continuum) taken up by the <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born of meditation) regarding the aspects of the three knowledges (<s>trisarvajñatā</s>).

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
svarūpeṇa viṃśatiḥ prayogāḥ / ākāreṇa trisarvajñatāsambaddhānāṃ trisaptatyuttaraśatasaṃkhyākānāmākārāṇāmabhinirhārakāḥ sattvayogāḥ trisaptatyuttaraśatamasya sarvākārābhisambodhasya bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
By their own nature, there are twenty practices (<s>prayoga</s>). By aspect, the mental engagements that bring about the one hundred and seventy-three aspects connected with the three knowledges — these are the divisions of <s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s>, numbering one hundred and seventy-three.

children.text: satvayogaḥ, mārgapāramitā, bodhisattvamārgaḥ, mahāyānapatipattiḥ, sannāhapratipattirityete paryāyavācinaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sattvayoga</s> (mental engagement of a continuum), <s>mārgapāramitā</s> (perfection of the path), <s>bodhisattvamārga</s> (bodhisattva path), <s>mahāyānapratipatti</s> (Mahāyāna practice), and <s>sannāhapratipatti</s> (practice of donning armor) — these are synonymous terms.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
mahāyānasambhāramārgamārabhya antimakṣaṇasthitabodhisattvāvasthāparyantaṃ sarvākārābhisambodhasya sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The range of <s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s> extends from the <s>mahāyānasambhāramārga</s> (Mahāyāna path of accumulation) up to the stage of the <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding at the final moment.

children.text: 5. mūrdhābhisamayaḥ
children.translated_text: 5. <s>Mūrdhābhisamaya</s> (peak realization)

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
śūnyatālambanayā bhāvanāmayyā prajñayopāttānāṃ taddṛṣṭyā vyavasthāpitānāṃ ca trisarvajñatākārāṇāṃ bhāvanāyāṃ prakarṣaparyantaḥ sattvayogaḥ mūrdhaprayogaḥ iti mūrdhābhisamayasya lakṣaṇam / bodhisattvasya śrutamayyā prajñayopāttānāṃ prayogāṇāmapyatraiva saṃgṛhītatvāllakṣaṇe taddṛṣṭyā vyavasthāpiteti viśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>mūrdhābhisamaya</s> is: the <s>mūrdhaprayoga</s> (peak practice), which is the mental engagement of a continuum at the culminating point of the meditation on the aspects of the three knowledges (<s>trisarvajñatā</s>), taken up by <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born of meditation) with <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) as its object, and of those [aspects] established from the perspective of that [view]. Since even the practices taken up by the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s <s>śrutamayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born of hearing) are included here, the qualifier 'established from the perspective of that [view]' appears in the definition.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
saṃkṣepataḥ prayogamārgīyo mūrdhaprayogaḥ, darśanamārgīyo mūrdhaprayogaḥ, bhāvanāmārgīyo mūrdhaprayogaḥ, ānantaryamūrdhaprayogaśceti catvāro bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
In brief, there are four divisions: the <s>mūrdhaprayoga</s> of the <s>prayogamārga</s> (path of preparation), the <s>mūrdhaprayoga</s> of the <s>darśanamārga</s> (path of seeing), the <s>mūrdhaprayoga</s> of the <s>bhāvanāmārga</s> (path of meditation), and the <s>ānantaryamūrdhaprayoga</s> (uninterrupted peak practice).

children.text: athavā ūṣmamūrdhakṣāntyagradharmākhyāḥ prayogamārgasya catvāraḥ, darśanabhāvanāmārgayo ānantaryamūrdhaprayogāstraya iti sapta mūrdhaprayogā bhavantīti /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the four [stages] of the <s>prayogamārga</s> called <s>ūṣma</s> (heat), <s>mūrdhan</s> (peak), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), and <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma), plus the three <s>ānantaryamūrdhaprayogas</s> of the paths of seeing and meditation — thus there are seven <s>mūrdhaprayogas</s>.

children.text: vistareṇa tu trisaptatyuttaraśataṃ mūrdhaprayogā iti jñeyam /
children.translated_text: In detail, however, it should be known that there are one hundred and seventy-three <s>mūrdhaprayogas</s>.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
mahāyānaprayogamārgīyoṣmaprayogamārabhya antimakṣaṇasthitabodhisattvāvasthāparyantamasya sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The range of this extends from the <s>ūṣmaprayoga</s> (heat practice) of the <s>mahāyānaprayogamārga</s> (Mahāyāna path of preparation) up to the stage of the <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding at the final moment.

children.text: 6. ānupūrvikābhisamayaḥ
children.translated_text: 6. <s>Ānupūrvikābhisamaya</s> (sequential realization)

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
trisarvajñatākārāṇāṃ sthirīkaraṇāya vibhāvanāvyavasthāpitaḥ sattvayoga ānupūrvikaprayoga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>ānupūrvikābhisamaya</s> is: a mental engagement of a continuum established through gradual cultivation (<s>vibhāvanā</s>) for the purpose of stabilizing the aspects of the three knowledges.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
trayodaśāsyānupūrvikābhisamayasya bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are thirteen divisions of this <s>ānupūrvikābhisamaya</s> (sequential realization).

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
mahāyānasambhāramārgamārabhya antimakṣaṇasthitabodhisattvāvasthātaḥ pūrvāvasthāparyantamasya sīmā bhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The range of this extends from the <s>mahāyānasambhāramārga</s> (Mahāyāna path of accumulation) up to the stage prior to the stage of the <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding at the final moment.

children.text: 7. ekakṣaṇābhisambodhaḥ
children.translated_text: 7. <s>Ekakṣaṇābhisambodha</s> (realization in a single moment)

children.text: (ka) lakṣaṇam trisarvajñatākārāṇāṃ svabhyastīkaraṇāya anupūrvabhāvanayotpannaḥ pāryantikaḥ sattvayogaḥ ekakṣaṇābhisambodha iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>ekakṣaṇābhisambodha</s> is: the ultimate mental engagement of a continuum, arisen through sequential cultivation for the purpose of thoroughly familiarizing [oneself] with the aspects of the three knowledges.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
vyāvṛtyā 'sya catvāro bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
By way of exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>), there are four divisions of this.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
caramabhavikabodhisattvāvasthāyāmeva kevalamayaṃ prayogo bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
This practice exists exclusively at the stage of the <s>bodhisattva</s> at the final existence (<s>caramabhavika</s>).

children.text: 8. dharmakāyaḥ
children.translated_text: 8. <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth body)

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
trisarvajñatākārāṇāṃ bhāvanāprakarṣabalenotpannaṃ phalaṃ paryantānāsravaguṇā vā dharmakāya iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>dharmakāya</s> is: the fruit arisen through the power of the culmination of meditation on the aspects of the three knowledges, or [equivalently,] the ultimate uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>) qualities.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
svabhāvakāyaḥ, jñānadharmakāyaḥ, sāmbhogikakāyaḥ, nairmāṇikakāyaśceti catvāro 'sya bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are four divisions of this: <s>svabhāvakāya</s> (essence body), <s>jñānadharmakāya</s> (knowledge truth body), <s>sāmbhogikakāya</s> (enjoyment body), and <s>nairmāṇikakāya</s> (emanation body).

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
buddhabhūmāveva kevalamayaṃ dharmakāyo bhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
This <s>dharmakāya</s> exists exclusively at the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage).

children.text: saptatiḥ padārthāḥ
children.translated_text: The seventy topics

children.text: trisarvajñatopalakṣakāstriṃśad dharmāḥ, caturṇāṃ prayogāṇāmupalakṣakāḥ ṣaṭtriṃśad dharmāḥ, dharmakāyopalakṣakāścatvāra iti saptatiḥ padārthāstriṣu vibhajya pṛthak nirūpyante /
children.translated_text: The thirty <s>dharmas</s> that characterize the three knowledges (<s>trisarvajñatā</s>), the thirty-six <s>dharmas</s> that characterize the four practices (<s>prayoga</s>), and the four that characterize the <s>dharmakāya</s> — [together] the seventy topics are divided into three [groups] and explained separately.

children.text: 1. trisarvajñatopalakṣakāḥ triṃśad dharmāḥ trisarvajñatopalakṣakeṣu triṃśaddharmeṣu sarvākārajñatābodhakā daśa, mārgajñatābodhakā ekādaśa, sarvajñatābodhakā nava ceti triṃśad bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
1. The thirty <s>dharmas</s> characterizing the three knowledges
Among the thirty <s>dharmas</s> characterizing the three knowledges, ten elucidate <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, eleven elucidate <s>mārgajñatā</s>, and nine elucidate <s>sarvajñatā</s> — thus there are thirty.

children.text:
(a) sarvākārajñatopalakṣakā daśa dharmāḥ tatra 1. mahāyānacittotpādaḥ, 2. avavādaḥ, 3. nirvadhāṅgam, 4. mahāyānapratipattyādhāraḥ, 5. mahāyānapratipattyālambanam, 6. mahāyānapratipattisamuddeśaḥ, 7. sannāhapratipattiḥ, 8. prasthānapratipattiḥ, 9. sambhārapratipattiḥ, 10. niryāṇapratipattiriti daśa dharmāḥ sarvākārajñatāmupalakṣayantīti abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kārikābhyāṃ pradarśitāḥ /
yathā -
children.translated_text:
(a) The ten <s>dharmas</s> characterizing <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>
Therein: 1. <s>Mahāyānacittotpāda</s> (generation of the Mahāyāna awakening mind), 2. <s>avavāda</s> (instruction), 3. <s>nirvedhāṅga</s> (factor of penetration), 4. <s>mahāyānapratipattyādhāra</s> (basis of Mahāyāna practice), 5. <s>mahāyānapratipattyālambana</s> (object of Mahāyāna practice), 6. <s>mahāyānapratipattisamuddeśa</s> (purpose of Mahāyāna practice), 7. <s>sannāhapratipatti</s> (practice of donning armor), 8. <s>prasthānapratipatti</s> (practice of setting forth), 9. <s>sambhārapratipatti</s> (practice of accumulation), 10. <s>niryāṇapratipatti</s> (practice of emergence) — these ten <s>dharmas</s> characterize <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, as displayed in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through two verses.
Namely:

children.text: cittotpādo 'vavādaśca nirvedhāṅgaṃ caturvidham /
children.translated_text: <s>Cittotpāda</s> (generation of the awakening mind), <s>avavāda</s> (instruction), and the fourfold <s>nirvedhāṅga</s> (factor of penetration),

children.text: ādhāraḥ pratipatteśca dharmadhātusvabhāvakaḥ //
children.translated_text: the basis (<s>ādhāra</s>) of practice, which is of the nature of <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the expanse of reality),

children.text: ālambanaṃ samuddeśaṃ sannāhaprasthitikriye /
children.translated_text: the object (<s>ālambana</s>), the purpose (<s>samuddeśa</s>), the actions of donning armor (<s>sannāha</s>) and setting forth (<s>prasthiti</s>),

children.text: sambhārāśca saniryāṇāḥ sarvākārajñatā muneḥ //
children.translated_text: and the accumulations (<s>sambhāra</s>) together with emergence (<s>niryāṇa</s>) — [these constitute] the <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects) of the Sage.

children.text: 1. cittotpādaḥ
children.translated_text: 1. <s>Cittotpāda</s> (generation of the awakening mind)

children.text: asya lakṣaṇam, bhedaḥ ālambanam, avadhiśceti catvāri jñātavyāni / abhisamayālaṅkāre tisṛbhiḥ kārikābhiḥ sarva pratipāditam / tathāhi -
children.translated_text: Four things should be known regarding this: its definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), divisions (<s>bheda</s>), object (<s>ālambana</s>), and scope (<s>avadhi</s>). All [of these] are set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through three verses. Namely:

children.text: cittotpādaḥ parārthāya samyaksambodhikāmatā /
children.translated_text: <s>Cittotpāda</s> (generation of the awakening mind) is the desire for perfect complete awakening (<s>samyaksambodhi</s>) for the sake of others.

children.text: samāsavyāsataḥ sā ca yathāsūtraṃ ca cocyate //
children.translated_text: And that is spoken of in brief and in detail, and according to the <s>sūtras</s>.

children.text: bhūhemacandrajvalanairnidhiratnākarārṇavaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Through [the similes of] earth, gold, the moon, fire, a treasury, a jewel-mine, the ocean,

children.text: vajrācalauṣadhīmitraiścintāmaṇyarkagītibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: a <s>vajra</s> (diamond/thunderbolt), a mountain, medicine, a spiritual friend, a wish-fulfilling gem, the sun, and a song,

children.text: nṛpagañjamahāmārgayānaprasravaṇodakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: a king, a storehouse, a great highway, a vehicle, a fountain, and water,

children.text: ānandoktinadīmeghairdvāviṃśatividhaḥ sa ca //
children.translated_text: a joyful sound, a river, and a cloud — it is of twenty-two kinds.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
parārthāya svahetukena chandena samudānītaṃ bodhikāmatāsamprayuktaṃ māhāyānika viśiṣṭaṃ manovijñāna cittotpāda iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The definition [of <s>cittotpāda</s>, the generation of the awakening mind] is: a mental cognition (<s>manovijñāna</s>) that is distinguished as <s>Mahāyāna</s>, associated with the desire for awakening (<s>bodhikāmatā</s>), brought about by aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) that has its own cause, for the benefit of others.

children.text:
(kha) ālambanam
svārthāṃ bodhiṃ parārthaṃ ca parasantatistha nirvāṇamālambya cittotpādaḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text:
(b) Object.
The generation of the awakening mind operates taking as its object one's own awakening and the <s>nirvāṇa</s> existing in others' mental continuums for the benefit of others.

children.text:
(ga) bhedaḥ
bodhipraṇidhisvabhāvaḥ bodhiprasthānasvabhāvaśceti svarūpataścittotpādasya dvau bhedau bhavataḥ /
children.translated_text:
(c) Classification.
The generation of the awakening mind has two divisions in terms of its own nature: that whose nature is the aspiration for awakening (<s>bodhipraṇidhi</s>) and that whose nature is the setting forth toward awakening (<s>bodhiprasthāna</s>).

children.text: samprayuktacaitasikadṛṣṭyā cittotpādasya dvāviṃśatiḥ prabhedā bhavanti, yathā 1. pṛthivīsamaḥ, 2. suvarṇasamaḥ, 3. candrasamaḥ, 4. jvalanasamaḥ, 5. mahānidhisamaḥ, 6. ratnākarasamaḥ, 7. mahārṇavasamaḥ, 8. vajrasamaḥ, 9. parvatasamaḥ, 10. auṣadhisamaḥ, 11. kalyāṇamitrasamaḥ, 12. cintāmaṇisamaḥ, 13. ādityasamaḥ, 14. madhuragītisamaḥ, 15. nṛpasamaḥ, 16. koṣṭhāgārasamaḥ, 17. mahāmārgasama, 18. yānasamaḥ, 19. prasravaṇodakasamaḥ, 20. ānandoktisamaḥ, 21. nadīsamaḥ, 22. meghasamaśceti /
children.translated_text: From the perspective of associated mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>), the generation of the awakening mind has twenty-two subdivisions, namely: 1. like the earth, 2. like gold, 3. like the moon, 4. like fire, 5. like a great treasure, 6. like a jewel mine, 7. like a great ocean...

children.text:
(gha) avadhiḥ
caturvidho bodhisattvānāṃ cittotpādaḥ / tathā hi - ādimokṣiko 'dhimukticaryābhūmau, śuddhādhyāśayikaḥ saptasubhūmiṣu, vaipākiko 'ṣṭamyādiṣu, anāvaraṇiko buddhabhūmau / yathoktaṃ mahāyānasūtrālaṅkāre -
children.translated_text:
(d) Scope.
The generation of the awakening mind of <s>bodhisattvas</s> is of four kinds. Namely: that based on conviction (<s>adhimokṣika</s>) on the stage of the practice of conviction (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>); that of pure superior intention (<s>śuddhādhyāśayika</s>) on the seven pure stages; that of maturation (<s>vaipākika</s>) on the eighth stage and above; and that free from obscurations (<s>anāvaraṇika</s>) on the Buddha-stage. As stated in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>...

children.text: cittotpādo 'dhimokṣo 'sau śuddhādhyāśayiko 'paraḥ /
children.translated_text: The generation of the mind based on conviction, and the other based on pure superior intention,

children.text: vaipākyo bhūmiṣu matastathāvaraṇavarjitaḥ //
children.translated_text: that of maturation is recognized on the stages, and likewise that free from obscurations.

children.text:
2. avavādaḥ
asya lakṣaṇam, bhedaḥ. avadhi, śravaṇaniyamaśceti sarvo viṣayaḥ abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kārikābhyāṃ pratipāditaḥ / tathāhi -
children.translated_text:
2. Instruction (<s>avavāda</s>).
Its definition, classification, scope, and restriction on hearing — the entire subject — is set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in two verses. Namely:

children.text: pratipattau ca satyeṣu buddharatnādiṣu triṣu /
children.translated_text: Regarding the practice, the truths, the three [jewels] — <s>Buddha</s>, jewel, and so on,

children.text: asaktāvapariśrāntau pratipatsamparigrahe //
children.translated_text: non-attachment and non-weariness, and the undertaking of practice,

children.text: cakṣuḥṣu pañcasu jñeyaḥ ṣaṭsvabhijñāguṇeṣu ca /
children.translated_text: the five eyes, the six qualities of superknowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>),

children.text: dṛṅmārge bhāvanākhye cetyavavādo daśātmakaḥ //
children.translated_text: the path of seeing and that called cultivation — the instruction is tenfold.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
mokṣamārgasya abhrāntopadeśaḥ avavāda iti lakṣaṇaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The definition is: instruction (<s>avavāda</s>) is the unerring teaching of the path to liberation.

children.text: athavā - mahāyānacittotpādadvāreṇa prarthitārthaprāptyupāyātmakaḥ abhrāntaviśuddhopadeśaḥ māhāyānīyāvavādalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Alternatively: an unerring, pure teaching whose nature is the means for attaining the desired goal through the door of generating the <s>Mahāyāna</s> awakening mind — this is the definition of <s>Mahāyāna</s> instruction.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
prathamaṃ samprāptaguṇaparipācanārthena aparihāṇimupādāya śikṣaṇāvavādaḥ, tataḥ paścādaprāptaguṇaprāptimupādāya anuśāsanāvavāda iti dvau bhedau / viṣayabhedāt punaḥ avavādo daśadhāḥ jñeyaḥ / tathāhi - pratiapattyākāramadhikṛtya satyadvayasvarūpamanatikramya śikṣaṇaṃ pratipattyavavādaḥ prathamaḥ / pratipatteryadālambanaṃ catvāri āryasatyāni, tadviṣayakopadeśaḥ satyāvavādaḥ dvitīyaḥ / yaścāśrayastrīṇi śaraṇāni tadviṣayakopadeśaḥ ratnatrayāvavādastṛtīyaḥ / yo viśeṣagamanahetuḥ asaktistadviṣaye deśanāvavādaścaturthaḥ / yo 'vyāvṛttigamanahetuḥ apariśrāntiḥ tadviṣayako deśanāvavādaḥ pañcamaḥ / yo 'nanyayānagamanahetuḥ pratipatsamparigrahastadviṣayakāvavādaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ / yo 'parapratyayagāmitvahetuḥ pañca cakṣūṃṣi tadviṣayakaḥ pañcacakṣuravavādaḥ saptamaḥ / yaḥ sava kārajñatāparipūrihetuḥ ṣaḍabhijñāḥ tadviṣayako 'bhijñāvavādaḥ aṣṭamaḥ / parikalpitasvabhāvānāṃ darśanaprahātavyānāṃ kleśānāṃ sabījānāṃ sarvathā samudghātako yo darśanamārgastadviṣayako darśanamārgāvavādo navamaḥ / bhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ sahajāvaraṇānāṃ sabījānāṃ sarvathā samudghātako yo bhāvanāmārgastadviṣayako bhāvanāmārgāvavādo daśamaḥ /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
First, instruction in training (<s>śikṣaṇāvavāda</s>), based on non-regression for the purpose of maturing qualities already attained; then, instruction in admonishment (<s>anuśāsanāvavāda</s>), based on attaining qualities not yet attained — these are the two divisions. According to the division of objects, instruction should be known as tenfold.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
mārgāpraveśamārabhya buddhabhūmiparyantamasya sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope.
Its limit extends from the entry into the path up to the Buddha-stage.

children.text:
(gha) śravaṇaniyamaḥ
mārge 'praviṣṭo 'pi śuddhādhyāśayikaḥ śuddhakarmikaḥ pudgalo māhāyānīyāvavādaṃ śrotuṃ bhavyo bhavati / yaśca mārgapraviṣṭo bodhisattvaḥ sa kalpānāmanekāni buddhebhyo bodhisattvebhyaḥ kalyāṇamitrebhyaḥ avavādaṃ śṛṇoti /
children.translated_text:
(d) Restriction on hearing.
Even one who has not entered the path — a person of pure superior intention and pure conduct — is fit (<s>bhavya</s>) to hear the <s>Mahāyāna</s> instruction. And a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has entered the path, for many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), from Buddhas and <s>bodhisattvas</s>...

children.text:
3. nirvedhāṅgam
caturvidhanirvedhabhāgīyānāmūṣmādīnāṃ lakṣaṇa-bheda-avadhyālambanākārādayaḥ abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kāribhyāṃ pratipāditāḥ / tathādi -
children.translated_text:
3. The aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhāṅga</s>).
The definition, classification, scope, object, and aspects of the four aids to penetration — heat (<s>ūṣman</s>) and so on — are set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in two verses. Namely:

children.text: ālambanata ākārāddhetutvāt samparigrahāt /
children.translated_text: From the standpoint of object, aspect, being a cause, and embracing,

children.text: caturvikalpasaṃyogaṃ yathāsvaṃ bhajatāṃ satām //
children.translated_text: of those good ones who partake of, each in their own way, the connection with the four types of conceptualization,

children.text: śrāvakebhyaḥ sakhaḍgebhyo bodhisattvasya tāyinaḥ /
children.translated_text: compared to <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and the <s>bodhisattva</s> of the Protector,

children.text: mṛdumadhyādhimātrāṇāmuṣmādīnāṃ viśiṣṭatā //
children.translated_text: the distinction of the mild, medium, and intense [degrees] of heat and so on.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
svahetumokṣabhāgīyānantaramutpadyamāno 'bhisamayaḥ prayogamārga iti lakṣaṇam / prayogamārgaḥ, arthābhisamayaḥ, nirvedhāṅgamityanarthāntaram /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The definition is: the realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>) that arises immediately after the accumulation that is one's own cause, [belonging to] the liberation-share (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>), is the path of preparation (<s>prayogamārga</s>). The path of preparation, the realization of the meaning (<s>arthābhisamaya</s>), and the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhāṅga</s>) are synonymous.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
śrāvakādiyānatrayasya trayaḥ prayogamārgā bhavanti / prayogamārgeṣu triṣu pratisvaṃ ūṣma-mūrva-kṣāntyagradharmākhyāścatvāro bhedā bhavanti / itthaṃ dvādaśa bhavanti prayogamārgasya bhedāḥ /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
There are three paths of preparation for the three vehicles of <s>śrāvakas</s> and others. Within each of the three paths of preparation, there are four divisions called heat (<s>ūṣman</s>), summit (<s>mūrdhan</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), and supreme <s>dharma</s> (<s>agradharma</s>). Thus there are twelve divisions of the path of preparation.

children.text:
mahāyānaprayogamārgaḥ
svahetormahāyānasambhāramārgādutpadyamāno māhāyānīyo 'rthābhisamayaḥ mahāyānaprayogamārgaḥ /
children.translated_text:
The <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of preparation:
The <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization of the meaning that arises from one's own cause, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of accumulation, is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of preparation.

children.text: mahāyānaprayogamārgaḥ, mahāyānārthābhisamayaḥ, mahāyānanirvedhabhāgīya iti paryāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of preparation, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization of the meaning, and the <s>Mahāyāna</s> aids to penetration — these are synonyms.

children.text:
mahāyānaprayogamārgabhedāḥ
ūṣma-mūrdha-kṣāntyagradharmākhyāścaturnirvedhabhāgīyāḥ śrāvakanirvedhabhāgīyebhyaḥ pañcabhirviśeṣairviśiṣṭā bhavanti / eteṣu nirvedhabhāgīyeṣu pratyekaṃ mṛdu-madhyādhimātrabhedena tridhā bhavati / evaṃ mahāyānaprayogamārgasya dvādaśa bhedā jāyante /
children.translated_text:
The divisions of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of preparation:
The four aids to penetration called heat, summit, patience, and supreme <s>dharma</s> are distinguished from the <s>śrāvaka</s> aids to penetration by five special qualities. In each of these aids to penetration, there are mild, medium, and intense [degrees]...

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
trividhanairātmyeṣu (pudgalanairātmya-sthūladharmanairātmya-sūkṣmadharmanairātmyeṣu) kimapyekaṃ nairātmyamālambya pravartamānāyā vidarśanāyāḥ prāptimārabhya bhūmiprāptiparyantaṃ prayogamārgasya vyāptirbhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope.
The scope of the path of preparation extends from the attainment of insight (<s>vidarśanā</s>) that operates by taking as its object any one of the three kinds of selflessness — selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>), coarse selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>, and subtle selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> — up to the attainment of the stages (<s>bhūmi</s>).

children.text:
(gha) ālambanākārādayaḥ
hainayānikaprayogamārgānmāhāyānikaprayogamārgaḥ ṣaḍbhirviśeṣerviśiṣṭo bhavati, yathā - ālambanaviśeṣāt, ākāraviśeṣāt, hetutvaviśeṣāt, samparigrahaviśeṣāt, praheyavikalpasaṃyogaviśeṣāt, mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedaviśeṣācca /
children.translated_text:
(d) Object, aspect, and so on.
The <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of preparation is distinguished from the <s>Hīnayāna</s> path of preparation by six special qualities, namely: distinction of object (<s>ālambana</s>), distinction of aspect (<s>ākāra</s>), distinction of being a cause (<s>hetutva</s>), distinction of embracing (<s>samparigraha</s>), distinction of connection with conceptualizations to be abandoned...

children.text: idaṃ ca vaiśiṣṭyam abhisamayālaṅkāre "ālambanamanityādi" - ityataḥ prāramya "sarvathā samparigrahaḥ" - ityantaṃ navabhiḥ kārikābhiḥ suviśadaṃ vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: This distinctiveness is clearly explained in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in nine verses beginning with 'The object is impermanence and so on' and ending with 'the embracing in every way.'

children.text: 4. pratipatterādhāraḥ mahāyānapratipatterādhāraḥ prakṛtigotraṃ bhavati / tasya lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kārikābhyāṃ varṇitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
4. The basis of practice (<s>pratipatterādhāra</s>).
The basis of <s>Mahāyāna</s> practice is the natural lineage (<s>prakṛtigotra</s>). Its definition and so on are described in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in two verses. Namely:

children.text: ṣoḍhādhigamadharmasya pratipakṣaprahāṇayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the quality of realization in sixteen aspects, of the antidote and abandonment,

children.text: tayoḥ paryupayogasya prajñāyāḥ kṛpayā saha //
children.translated_text: of the employment of those two, of wisdom together with compassion,

children.text: śiṣyāsādhāraṇatvasya parārthānukramasya ca /
children.translated_text: of being uncommon to disciples, of the sequential [acts] for the benefit of others,

children.text: jñānasyāyatnavṛtteśca pratiṣṭhā gotramucyate //
children.translated_text: and of knowledge operating effortlessly — the foundation is called the lineage (<s>gotra</s>).

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
sāmānyato yo dharmadhātuḥ pariśodhitaḥ san bodhau pariṇamate, sa gotramiti lakṣaṇam / viśeṣato yo dharmadhātuḥ pariśodhitaḥ san anuttarāyāṃ samyak sambodhau pariṇamate, mahāyānapratipatteścādhāro bhavanti, sa prakṛtigotramiti /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
In general, the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of <s>dharmas</s>) which, when purified, matures into awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) — that is the definition of lineage (<s>gotra</s>). Specifically, the <s>dharmadhātu</s> which, when purified, matures into unsurpassed perfect awakening — that is the basis of <s>Mahāyāna</s> practice...

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
abhidhānadṛṣṭyā prakṛtigotraṃ paripuṣṭagotraṃ ceti dvau bhedau / mahāyānapratipatterāśrayabhūtaṃ prakṛtisthaṃ gotram āśritadharmadṛṣṭyā trayodaśavidha bhavati / idameva prakṛtigotraṃ mahāyānasambhāramārgasyāpyādhāro bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
From the perspective of designation, there are two divisions: the natural lineage (<s>prakṛtigotra</s>) and the developed lineage (<s>paripuṣṭagotra</s>). The natural lineage that serves as the basis of <s>Mahāyāna</s> practice, from the perspective of its dependent <s>dharmas</s>, is of thirteen kinds. This very natural lineage, [as the basis of] <s>Mahāyāna</s>...

children.text: ūṣma-mūrdha-kṣāntyagradharmākhyacaturvidhalaukikanirvedhabhāgīyānāmādhārāścatvāraḥ, lokottaradarśanamārgamasyādhāra ekaḥ, lokottarabhāvanāmārgasyādhāra eka iti ṣaṭ prakṛtigotrāṇi / tataḥ pratipakṣapratipatterādhāraḥ, tataḥ prahāṇapratipatterādhāraḥ, tadanantaraṃ pratipakṣapraheyānupalabdhyā tadutpādanirodhayuktavikalpāpagamasya vimuktimārgasyādhāraḥ, tataḥ prajñākaruṇayorādhāraḥ, śrāvakādyasādhāraṇadharmasyādhāraḥ, parārthānukramasyādhāraḥ, jñānasyāyatnavṛtteścādhāra iti prakṛtisthagotrasya trayodaśabhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: The four mundane <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (factors conducive to penetration) called <s>ūṣma</s> (heat), <s>mūrdhan</s> (peak), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), and <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma) have four bases; the supramundane <s>darśanamārga</s> (path of seeing) has one basis; and the supramundane <s>bhāvanāmārga</s> (path of meditation) has one basis — thus there are six <s>prakṛtigotra</s> (naturally present lineage) [bases]. Then: the basis of the practice of the antidote, then the basis of the practice of abandonment, then — through the non-apprehension of that which is to be abandoned by the antidote — the basis of the <s>vimuktimārga</s> (path of liberation), which involves the departure of conceptualization regarding the arising and cessation of that; then the basis of wisdom and compassion (<s>prajñākaruṇā</s>), the basis of the <s>dharmas</s> uncommon to <s>śrāvakas</s> and the like, the basis of the sequence for the benefit of others, and the basis of knowledge and effortless activity — thus the <s>prakṛtisthagotra</s> (naturally abiding lineage) has thirteen divisions.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
mahāyānasambhāramārgamārabhya antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvāvasthāparyantamasya sīmā bhavati / viśeṣataśca upariṣṭāt sākṣānnirdiṣṭaprayogamārgīyoṣmāvasthātaḥ prārabhya antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvāvasthāparyantamasya vyāptirbhavatīti jñeyam /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The range of this extends from the <s>mahāyānasambhāramārga</s> (Mahāyāna path of accumulation) up to the stage of the <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding at the final moment. In particular, it should be known that its pervasion begins specifically from the <s>ūṣma</s> (heat) stage of the <s>prayogamārga</s> (path of preparation), as directly indicated above, up to the stage of the <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding at the final moment.

children.text: 5. pratipatterālambanam
children.translated_text: 5. The object of practice (<s>pratipatterālambana</s>)

children.text: pratipatterālambanānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ bhedaḥ avadhiśceti trīṇyatra pratipādyante / abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kārikābhyāṃ ālambanasvarūpaṃ pradarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: Three things are set forth here regarding the objects of practice: definition, divisions, and scope. The essential nature of the object is displayed in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through two verses. Namely:

children.text: ālambanaṃ sarvadharmāste punaḥ kuśalādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The object [of practice] is all <s>dharmas</s>; those in turn are the wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>) and the like,

children.text: laukikādhigamākhyāśca ye ca lokottarā matāḥ /
children.translated_text: those called mundane attainment, and those considered supramundane,

children.text: sāsravānāsravā dharmāḥ saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtāśca ye /
children.translated_text: the <s>dharmas</s> that are contaminated (<s>sāsrava</s>) and uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>), and those that are conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>),

children.text: śiṣyasādhāraṇā dharmā ye cāsādhāraṇā muneḥ //
children.translated_text: the <s>dharmas</s> common to disciples (<s>śiṣya</s>) and those uncommon [qualities] of the Sage.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
pratipatterjñeyatvamevālambanatvamiti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of being an object of practice is simply being that which is to be known (<s>jñeya</s>) by the practice.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
ālambanamekādaśavidhaṃ bhavati / tathā hi - kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtāni kāyakarmādīni trīṇi, bālapṛthagjanasambaddhāḥ pañca skandhāḥ, sarvāryajanasaṃgṛhītāni catvāri anāsravadhyānāni, ātmadarśanāpratipakṣatvena pañcopādānaskandhāḥ, ātmadarśanapratipakṣatvena catvāryanāsravāṇi smṛtyupasthānāni, hetupratyayādhīnakāmādidhātusaṃgṛhītā
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
The object is of eleven kinds. Namely: three [types of] bodily action and the like that are wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>), unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>), and indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>); the five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) associated with the ordinary person (<s>bālapṛthagjana</s>); the four uncontaminated <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) comprised within all noble persons (<s>ārya</s>); the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>) as not being the antidote to the view of self (<s>ātmadarśana</s>); the four uncontaminated foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) as being the antidote to the view of self; the conditioned [<s>dharmas</s>]

children.text: bodhipakṣādayaṃ saṃskṛtāḥ (mārgasatyam), kāraṇānapekṣadhātutrayāparyāpannatathatādayo 'saṃskṛtāḥ (nirodhasatyam), sarvāryajanasantānaprabhavacaturdhyānādayo guṇāḥ, samyaksambuddhasantānodayadharmidaśabalānyasādhāraṇānītyekādaśavidhamālambanam /
children.translated_text: such as the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) and the like comprised within the desire-realm and other realms, which are dependent on causes and conditions [i.e., the truth of the path]; the unconditioned [<s>dharmas</s>] such as <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and the like, which are independent of conditions and not comprised within the three realms [i.e., the truth of cessation]; the qualities such as the four <s>dhyānas</s> and the like arising in the continuum of all noble persons; and the uncommon [qualities] such as the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>) and the like, with the <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor) arising in the continuum of a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>) — thus the object is of eleven kinds.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
adhigamānukrameṇa sarvadharmā yathāvadālambyanta iti nāstyālambanānāṃ bhūmyavadhiriti jñeyam /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
Since all <s>dharmas</s> are taken as objects just as they are, according to the sequence of realization, there is no stage-limit for the objects — this should be known.

children.text:
6. pratipattisamuddeśaḥ
asya lakṣaṇaṃ bhedaḥ avadhiriti trīṇi parijñātavyāni, tāni abhisamayālaṅkāre kārikayaikayā 'nayā nirdiṣṭāni / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
6. The purpose of practice (<s>pratipattisamuddeśa</s>)
Three things should be understood here: its definition, divisions, and scope. These are indicated in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> by this single verse. Namely:

children.text: sarvasattvāgratācittaprahāṇādhigamatraye /
children.translated_text: The purpose, characterized by the three greatnesses of supreme mind among all beings (<s>sarvasattvāgratācitta</s>),

children.text: tribhirmahattvairuddeśo vijñeyo 'rya svayambhuvām //
children.translated_text: abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>), and realization (<s>adhigama</s>), should be known as the noble [purpose] of the Self-Arisen Ones.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
pratipattau pratiṣṭhitasya bodhisattvasya svalakṣyameva pratipattisamuddeśa iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of the purpose of practice (<s>pratipattisamuddeśa</s>) is: the very aim (<s>svalakṣya</s>) of the <s>bodhisattva</s> who is established in the practice.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
sarvasattvāgratācittamahattvam, prahāṇamahattvam, adhigamamahattvaṃ ceti trayo 'syabhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are three divisions of this: the greatness of the mind supreme among all beings (<s>sarvasattvāgratācittamahatva</s>), the greatness of abandonment (<s>prahāṇamahatva</s>), and the greatness of realization (<s>adhigamamahatva</s>).

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
buddhabhūmāveva kevalamayaṃ samuddeśo niṣpanno bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
This purpose (<s>samuddeśa</s>) is fully accomplished exclusively at the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage).

children.text:
7. sannāhapratipattiḥ
asyā lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayetthamupavarṇitam / yathā
children.translated_text:
7. <s>Sannāhapratipatti</s> (practice of donning armor)
The definition and the like of this are described in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> by a single verse, as follows:

children.text: dānādau ṣaḍvidhe teṣāṃ pratyekaṃ saṃgraheṇa yā /
children.translated_text: That which, with respect to the sixfold [perfections] beginning with <s>dāna</s> (giving) and the like, for each one individually, gathers [the others] —

children.text: sannāhapratipattiḥ sā ṣaḍbhiḥ ṣaṭkairyathoditāḥ //
children.translated_text: that is the <s>sannāhapratipatti</s> (practice of donning armor), [consisting of] six sets of six, as stated.

children.text:
pratipatterlakṣaṇam
mahāyānacittotpādamāśritya anuttarasamyaksaṃmbodhiniṣpattaye yā trisarvajñatāviṣaye sāmānyena śukladharmādhiṣṭhānā, sarvākārābhisambodhādau caturvidhe 'bhisamaye pratyabhisamayaṃ ṣaṭpāramitādhiṣṭhānā ca kriyā, sā mahāyānapratipatterlakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
Definition of practice
The definition of <s>mahāyānapratipatti</s> (Mahāyāna practice) is: an activity (<s>kriyā</s>) that, based on the <s>mahāyānacittotpāda</s> (generation of the Mahāyāna awakening mind), for the accomplishment of <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect complete awakening), is generally grounded in wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (<s>śukladharma</s>) regarding the domain of the three knowledges, and is grounded in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) for each of the four types of realization beginning with <s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s> (complete realization of all aspects).

children.text:
pratipattibhedaḥ
iyaṃ mahāyānapratipattiścaturvidhā bhavati, yathā - sannāhapratipattiḥ, prasthānapratipattiḥ, sambhārapratipattiḥ, niryāṇapratipattiśceti /
children.translated_text:
Divisions of practice
This <s>mahāyānapratipatti</s> (Mahāyāna practice) is fourfold: <s>sannāhapratipatti</s> (practice of donning armor), <s>prasthānapratipatti</s> (practice of setting forth), <s>sambhārapratipatti</s> (practice of accumulation), and <s>niryāṇapratipatti</s> (practice of emergence).

children.text:
(ka) sannāhapratipatterlakṣaṇam
ṣaṭpāramitāsu pratipāramitāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāsaṃgrāhikayā prajñayopāttaḥ sattvayogaḥ sannāhapratipatterlakṣaṇam / sannāhapratipattiḥ bodhisattvamārga ityanarthāntaram /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition of <s>sannāhapratipatti</s>
The definition of <s>sannāhapratipatti</s> (practice of donning armor) is: a mental engagement of a continuum (<s>sattvayoga</s>), for each <s>pāramitā</s> among the six <s>pāramitās</s>, taken up by the wisdom that gathers all six <s>pāramitās</s> [within each one]. <s>Sannāhapratipatti</s> and <s>bodhisattvamārga</s> (<s>bodhisattva</s> path) are synonymous.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
dānapāramitāsannāhapratipattimārabhya prajñāpāramitāsannāhapratipattiṃ yāvat ṣaḍ bhedā bhavanti / dāne 'pi dānaṃ śīlamityādiṣaṭpāramitā bhavanti / evaṃ ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu ṣaṭ ṣaṭkānīti kṛtvā vistareṇa ṣaṭtriṃśad bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are six divisions, from the <s>sannāhapratipatti</s> of the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) up to the <s>sannāhapratipatti</s> of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). Within giving too there are the six <s>pāramitās</s> [such as] giving, morality, and so on. Thus, making six sets of six among the six <s>pāramitās</s>, in detail there are thirty-six divisions.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
sambhāramārgīyabodhisattvamārabhya antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvaparyantamasyāḥ sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The range of this extends from the <s>bodhisattva</s> on the <s>sambhāramārga</s> (path of accumulation) up to the <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding at the final moment.

children.text:
8. prasthānapratipattiḥ
asyāḥ svarūpam abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kārikābhyāmupavarṇitam / tathā hi
children.translated_text:
8. <s>Prasthānapratipatti</s> (practice of setting forth)
The essential nature of this is described in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through two verses. Namely:

children.text: dhyānārūpyeṣu dānādau mārge maitryādikeṣu ca /
children.translated_text: In the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) and the formless [attainments] (<s>ārūpya</s>), in the sixfold [perfections] beginning with <s>dāna</s> (giving), in the path, in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the like,

children.text: gatopalambhayoge ca trimaṇḍalaviśuddhiṣu //
children.translated_text: in the conjunction of going and apprehension, and in the threefold purity (<s>trimaṇḍalaviśuddhi</s>),

children.text: uddeśe ṣaṭsvabhijñāsu sarvākārajñatānaye /
children.translated_text: in the purpose (<s>uddeśa</s>), in the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), and in the approach to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects) —

children.text: prasthānapratipajjñeyā mahāyānādhirohiṇī //
children.translated_text: the <s>prasthānapratipatti</s> (practice of setting forth) should be known as that which ascends to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
bhāvanāpradhānayā pratipattyā mahāyāne hetvātmake phalātmake vā dharme prasthitikriyā prasthānapratipatterlakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>prasthānapratipatti</s> (practice of setting forth) is: the activity of setting forth and progressing in a causal or resultant <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, through a practice predominantly characterized by meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>).

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
seyaṃ prasthānapratipattirnavavidhā jñeyā, tathā hi - dhyānārūpyasamāpattiṣu prasthānam, dānādiṣaṭpāramitāsu prasthānam, āryamārgeṣu prasthānam, caturapramāṇeṣu prasthānam, anupalambhayoge prasthānam, trimaṇḍalaviśuddhiṣu prasthānam, sarvasattvāgratāditrividhoddeśeṣu prasthānam, ṣaḍbhijñāsu prasthānam, sarvākārajñatāyāṃ prasthānamiti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
This <s>prasthānapratipatti</s> should be known as ninefold: setting forth in the <s>dhyāna</s> and formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), setting forth in the six <s>pāramitās</s> beginning with <s>dāna</s> (giving), setting forth in the noble paths, setting forth in the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), setting forth in the yoga of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>), setting forth in the threefold purity (<s>trimaṇḍalaviśuddhi</s>), setting forth in the threefold purpose beginning with supremacy among all beings, setting forth in the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), and setting forth in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
adhimukticaryābhūmikaprayogamārgīyoṣmāvasthāta ārabhya antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvaparyantamasyāḥ sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The range of this extends from the <s>ūṣma</s> (heat) stage of the <s>prayogamārga</s> (path of preparation) at the level of <s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s> (stage of conviction-conduct) up to the <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding at the final moment.

children.text:
9. sambhārapratipattiḥ
asthāḥ pratipatterlakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kārikābhyāṃ samyak pratipāditam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
9. <s>Sambhārapratipatti</s> (practice of accumulation)
All aspects of this practice — its definition and the like — are properly set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through two verses. Namely:

children.text: dayā dānādikaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ śamathaḥ savidarśanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Compassion (<s>dayā</s>), the sixfold [perfections] beginning with <s>dāna</s> (giving), <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) together with <s>vidarśanā</s> (insight),

children.text: yuganaddhaśca yo mārgaṃ upāye yacca kauśalam //
children.translated_text: and the <s>yuganaddha</s> (union [of śamatha and vipaśyanā]) path, and that which is skill in means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>),

children.text: jñānaṃ puṇyaṃ ca mārgaśca dhāraṇī bhūmayo daśa /
children.translated_text: knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), merit (<s>puṇya</s>), the path (<s>mārga</s>), <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention), the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages),

children.text: pratipakṣaśca vijñeyaḥ sambhārapratipatkramaḥ //
children.translated_text: and the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) — this should be known as the sequence of the <s>sambhārapratipatti</s> (practice of accumulation).

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
ātmanaḥ phalabhūtāṃ mahābodhiṃ yā sākṣāt pradadāti tādṛśī kriyā sambhārapratipattiriti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>sambhārapratipatti</s> (practice of accumulation) is: that activity which directly bestows great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>) as its own fruit.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaṃ
asyāḥ sambhārapratipatteḥ saptadaśa bhedā bhavanti / yathā mahākaruṇāsambhāraḥ, dānasambhāraḥ, śīlasambhāraḥ, kṣāntisambhāraḥ, vīryasambhāraḥ, dhyānasambhāraḥ, prajñāsambhāraḥ, śamathasambhāraḥ, vidarśanāsambhāraḥ, yuganaddhasambhāraḥ, upāyakauśalasambhāraḥ, jñānasambhāraḥ, puṇyasambhāraḥ, mārgasambhāraḥ, dhāraṇīsambhāraḥ, bhūmisambhāraḥ, pratipakṣasambhāraśceti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are seventeen divisions of this <s>sambhārapratipatti</s>: the accumulation of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), the accumulation of giving (<s>dāna</s>), the accumulation of morality (<s>śīla</s>), the accumulation of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), the accumulation of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), the accumulation of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), the accumulation of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), the accumulation of calm abiding (<s>śamatha</s>), the accumulation of insight (<s>vidarśanā</s>), the accumulation of union (<s>yuganaddha</s>), the accumulation of skill in means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>), the accumulation of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), the accumulation of merit (<s>puṇya</s>), the accumulation of the path (<s>mārga</s>), the accumulation of <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention), the accumulation of the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), and the accumulation of the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>).

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
sambhāramātraṃ tvādikarmikabhūmāvapi bhavati / kintu ye mahābodhiprāpaktvena sākṣānnirdiṣṭāste sambhārāḥ prayogamārgīyāgradharmāvasthāta ārabhya antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvāvasthāparyantaṃ bhavanti / āditaḥ pañcadaśa sambhārapratipattayaḥ prayogamārgīyāgradharmāvasthāparyantaṃ bhavanti / ṣoḍaśo bhūmisambhāraḥ saptadaśaśca pratipakṣasambhāro daśasu bhūmiṣu bhavataḥ /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
Accumulation in a general sense exists even at the stage of a beginner. However, those accumulations that are directly indicated as bringing about great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>) extend from the <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma) stage of the <s>prayogamārga</s> (path of preparation) up to the stage of the <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding at the final moment. The first fifteen accumulation practices extend up to the <s>agradharma</s> stage of the <s>prayogamārga</s>. The sixteenth — the <s>bhūmi</s> accumulation — and the seventeenth — the antidote accumulation — exist on the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages).

children.text:
10. niryāṇapratipattiḥ
asyāḥ svarūpam abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kārikābhyāṃ samyak pradarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
10. <s>Niryāṇapratipatti</s> (practice of emergence)
The essential nature of this is properly displayed in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through two verses. Namely:

children.text: uddeśe samatāyāṃ ca sattvārthe yatnavarjaṃne /
children.translated_text: In the purpose (<s>uddeśa</s>), in equality (<s>samatā</s>), in the benefit of beings (<s>sattvārtha</s>), in the abandonment of effort (<s>yatnavarjana</s>),

children.text: atyantāya ca niryāṇaṃ niryāṇaṃ prāptilakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: and for the sake of the absolute (<s>atyanta</s>) — emergence (<s>niryāṇa</s>) characterized by attainment (<s>prāpti</s>);

children.text: sarvākārajñatāyāṃ ca niryāṇaṃ mārgagocaram /
children.translated_text: and emergence in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects), and emergence in the domain of the path —

children.text: niryāṇapratipajjñeyā seyamaṣṭavidhātmikā //
children.translated_text: this <s>niryāṇapratipatti</s> (practice of emergence) should be known as eightfold in nature.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
ekāntena sarvajñatāyāṃ niryāṇakaraḥ śauddhabhūmikaḥ sattvayogaḥ niryāṇapratipattiriti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>niryāṇapratipatti</s> (practice of emergence) is: a mental engagement of a continuum belonging to the pure stages (<s>śuddhabhūmika</s>), which exclusively brings about emergence into <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience).

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
niryāṇapratipattiḥ seyamaṣṭavidhātmikā bhavati / tadyathā - trividhasamuddeśe niryāṇam, samatāyāṃ niryāṇam, sattvārthe niryāṇam, anābhoganiryāṇam, atyantaniryāṇam, prāptiniryāṇam, sarvākārajñātāniryāṇam, mārganiryāṇamiti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
This <s>niryāṇapratipatti</s> (practice of emergence) is eightfold in nature. Namely: emergence in the threefold purpose (<s>samuddeśa</s>), emergence in equality (<s>samatā</s>), emergence for the benefit of sentient beings, effortless emergence (<s>anābhoganiryāṇa</s>), ultimate emergence (<s>atyantaniryāṇa</s>), emergence of attainment (<s>prāptiniryāṇa</s>), emergence of the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñātāniryāṇa</s>), and emergence of the path (<s>mārganiryāṇa</s>).

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
tisṛṣu śuddhabhūmiṣvevāsyā vyāptirbhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
Its range extends only across the three pure stages (<s>śuddhabhūmi</s>).

children.text: // iti sarvākārajñatopalakṣakā daśa dharmāḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [these are] the ten <s>dharmas</s> that characterize <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects).

children.text: (ā) mārgajñatopalakṣakā ekādaśa dharmāḥ
children.translated_text: (B) The eleven <s>dharmas</s> characterizing <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the paths)

children.text: 1. dhyāmīkaraṇatādīni mārgajñatāṅgāni, 2. śrāvakamārgaḥ, 3. pratyekabuddhamārgaḥ, 4. bodhisattvamārgaḥ, 5. bhāvanāmārgakāritram, 6. bhāvanāmārgādhimuktiḥ, 7. bhāvanāmārgādhimuktasya stutiḥ stobha praśaṃsā ca, 8. pariṇāmanā, 9. anumodanā, 10. abhinirhāraḥ, 11. atyantaviśuddhiśceti ekādaśa dharmā mārgajñatāmupalakṣayantīti abhisamayālaṅkāre tisṛbhiḥ kārikābhirupadarśitāḥ / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: 1. <s>Dhyāmīkaraṇatā</s> and other <s>mārgajñatā</s> factors, 2. the <s>śrāvaka</s> path, 3. the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> path, 4. the <s>bodhisattva</s> path, 5. the activities of the <s>bhāvanāmārga</s> (path of meditation), 6. the aspiration of the <s>bhāvanāmārga</s>, 7. praise, eulogy, and commendation of one endowed with the aspiration of the <s>bhāvanāmārga</s>, 8. <s>pariṇāmanā</s> (dedication of merit), 9. <s>anumodanā</s> (rejoicing), 10. <s>abhinirhāra</s> (actualization), and 11. <s>atyantaviśuddhi</s> (ultimate purification) — these eleven <s>dharmas</s> characterize <s>mārgajñatā</s>, as displayed in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through three verses. Namely:

children.text: dhyāmīkaraṇatādīni śiṣyakhaḍgapathau ca yau /
children.translated_text: <s>Dhyāmīkaraṇatā</s> and the rest, and the two paths of disciples (<s>śiṣya</s>) and solitary realizers (<s>khaḍga</s>),

children.text: mahānuśaṃso dṛṅmārgaṃ aihikāmutrikairguṇaiḥ //
children.translated_text: the great benefit (<s>mahānuśaṃsa</s>), the path of seeing (<s>dṛṅmārga</s>), with qualities pertaining to this life and the next,

children.text: kāritramadhimuktiśca stutastobhitaśaṃsitāḥ /
children.translated_text: activities and aspiration, and praise, eulogy, and commendation,

children.text: pariṇāme 'numode ca manaskārāvanuttamau //
children.translated_text: dedication (<s>pariṇāma</s>) and rejoicing (<s>anumoda</s>), and the two supreme mental engagements (<s>manaskāra</s>),

children.text: nirhāraḥ śuddhiratyantamityayaṃ bhāvanāpathaḥ /
children.translated_text: actualization (<s>nirhāra</s>) and ultimate purification (<s>śuddhi</s>) — this is the path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāpatha</s>),

children.text: vijñānāṃ bodhisattvānāmiti mārgajñatoditā //
children.translated_text: to be known as the consciousness of <s>bodhisattvas</s> — thus <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the paths) is set forth.

children.text:
1. dhyāmīkaraṇatādīni
dhyāmīkaraṇatādīnāṃ mārgajñatāṅgānāṃ lakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayopavarṇitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
1. <s>Dhyāmīkaraṇatā</s> and the rest
The definition and so forth of the <s>mārgajñatā</s> factors beginning with <s>dhyāmīkaraṇatā</s> are all described in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through one verse. Namely:

children.text: dhyāmīkaraṇatā bhābhirdevānāṃ yogyatāṃ prati /
children.translated_text: <s>Dhyāmīkaraṇatā</s> (the quality of bringing radiance), with its lights, regarding the fitness of the gods,

children.text: viṣayo niyato vyāptiḥ svabhāvastasya karma ca //
children.translated_text: its specific object, its range (<s>vyāpti</s>), its essential nature, and its function —

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
mārgajñatāparipūrakā avayavībhūtā guṇā eva mārgajñatāṅgānīti lakṣaṇam /
athavā - mārgajñatāparipūrakāḥ asyāmavasthāyāṃ sākṣānnirdiṣṭāḥ sattvasantatisthaguṇā mārgajñatāṅgānīti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>mārgajñatā</s> factors is: qualities that have become component parts (<s>avayavībhūta</s>) which complete <s>mārgajñatā</s>.
Alternatively, the definition of <s>mārgajñatā</s> factors is: qualities abiding in the continuum of a sentient being that are directly indicated at this stage and that complete <s>mārgajñatā</s>.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
pañca mārgajñatāṅgāni dhyāmīkaraṇatādīni bhavanti, tadyathā - ādhāraḥ aparokṣāhaṅkārarāhityam, sahakāripratyayaścittotpādaḥ, sahetukā vyāptiḥ, saṃsārātyajanaṃ svabhāvaḥ, aparigṛhītasattvaparigrahaṇamiti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are five <s>mārgajñatā</s> factors beginning with <s>dhyāmīkaraṇatā</s>, namely: the basis (<s>ādhāra</s>), which is freedom from the conceit of direct perception; the cooperative condition (<s>sahakāripratyaya</s>), which is the generation of the awakening mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>); the range (<s>vyāpti</s>) together with its cause; the essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), which is non-abandonment of <s>saṃsāra</s>; and the embracing of sentient beings who are not [otherwise] embraced.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
sāmānyato mārgāpraveśamādāya buddhabhūmiparyantaṃ sīmā bhavati / sākṣānnirdiṣṭāṅgānāṃ dṛṣṭyā sambhāramārgamārabhya antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvāvasthāparyantaṃ sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
In general, taking entry into the path as the starting point, the boundary extends up to the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage). From the perspective of the directly indicated factors, the boundary extends from the <s>sambhāramārga</s> (path of accumulation) up to the stage of the <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding at the final moment.

children.text:
2. śrāvakamārgaḥ
śrāvakamārgādhigamasya lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre agholikhitayaikayā kārikayā samyagupadarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
2. The <s>śrāvaka</s> path
The definition and so forth of the realization of the <s>śrāvaka</s> path are clearly set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through one verse as written below. Namely:

children.text: caturṇāmāryasatyānāmākārānupalambhataḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the non-apprehension of the aspects of the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>),

children.text: śrāvakāṇāmayaṃ mārgo jñeyo mārgajñatānaye //
children.translated_text: this is to be known as the path of the <s>śrāvakas</s> according to the system of <s>mārgajñatā</s>.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
śrāvakajātīyavineyajanānugrahārthaṃ duḥkhādicaturāryasatyeṣu kimapyekamālambya anityādiṣoḍaśākāreṣvanyatamasya sākṣātkāradṛṣṭyā vyavasthāpitaḥ śrāvakādhigamajātīyo māhāyānikāryābhisamayaḥ śrāvakamārgajña mārgajñānamiti /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
For the purpose of benefiting trainees of the <s>śrāvaka</s> class, taking any one of the four noble truths beginning with suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) as its support, and established through the perspective of direct realization of any one of the sixteen aspects such as impermanence (<s>anitya</s>) — a Mahāyāna noble realization belonging to the class of <s>śrāvaka</s> attainment is the <s>śrāvakamārgajña mārgajñāna</s> (path-knowledge that knows the <s>śrāvaka</s> path).

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
ākāradṛṣṭyā ṣoḍaśavidhaḥ, mārgadṛṣṭyā tu darśanabhāvanā 'śaikṣamārgabhedena trividhaḥ /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
From the perspective of aspects, it is sixteenfold; from the perspective of the path, it is threefold through the division into the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>), the path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), and the path of no-more-learning (<s>aśaikṣamārga</s>).

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
darśanamārgamārabhya buddhabhūmiparyantamasya sīmā bhavati / keṣāṃcana matena mahāyānasambhāramārgamārabhya buddhabhūmiparyantamavadhiriti /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
Its boundary extends from the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) up to the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage). According to some, the scope extends from the Mahāyāna path of accumulation (<s>sambhāramārga</s>) up to the <s>buddhabhūmi</s>.

children.text:
3. pratyekabuddhamārgaḥ
pratyekabuddhādhigamasya lakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvamabhisamayālaṅkāre tisṛbhiḥ kārikābhiḥ pratipāditam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
3. The <s>pratyekabuddha</s> path
The definition and so forth of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> realization are all set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through three verses. Namely:

children.text: paropadeśavaiyarthya svayambodhāt svayambhuvām /
children.translated_text: Due to the futility of others' instruction and self-awakening, of the self-arisen ones (<s>svayambhū</s>),

children.text: gambhīratā ca jñānasya khaḍgānāmabhidhīyate //
children.translated_text: the profundity of knowledge is declared for the rhinoceros-like (<s>khaḍga</s>) [solitary realizers].

children.text: suśrūṣā yasya yasyārthe yatra yatra yathā yathā /
children.translated_text: Whoever listens attentively, for whatever purpose, wherever and however,

children.text: sa so 'rthaḥ khyātyaśabdo 'pi tatra tatra tathā tathā //
children.translated_text: that very meaning becomes manifest to them, even without words, in that very place and in that very manner.

children.text: grāhyārthakalpanāhānād grāhakasyāprahāṇataḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the abandonment of conceptual construction regarding the apprehended object, and through the non-abandonment of the apprehender,

children.text: ādhārataśca vijñeyaḥ khaḍgamārgasya saṃgrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: and from the perspective of the basis — thus the summary of the rhinoceros-like path (<s>khaḍgamārga</s>) should be known.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
pratyekabuddhagotrīyavineyajanānugrahārthaṃ dvādaśāyatanānyālambya bāhyagrāhyārthaśūnyatāsākṣātkārijñānadṛṣṭyā vyavasthāpitaḥ pratyekabuddhādhigamajātīyo māhāyānikāryābhisamayaḥ pratyekabuddhamārgamārgajñaṃ mārgajñānamiti /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
For the purpose of benefiting trainees of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> class, taking the twelve sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) as its support, and established through the perspective of the wisdom that directly realizes the emptiness of external apprehended objects (<s>bāhyagrāhyārthaśūnyatā</s>) — a Mahāyāna noble realization belonging to the class of <s>pratyekabuddha</s> attainment is the <s>pratyekabuddhamārgamārgajña mārgajñāna</s> (path-knowledge that knows the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> path).

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
darśanamārgaḥ, bhāvanāmārgaḥ, aśaikṣamārga iti trayo 'sya bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are three divisions of this: the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>), the path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), and the path of no-more-learning (<s>aśaikṣamārga</s>).

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
mahāyānadarśanamārgamārasya buddhabhūmiparyantamasya sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The boundary of this extends from the Mahāyāna path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) up to the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage).

children.text:
4. mahāyānadarśanamārgaḥ
mahānuśaṃsasya darśanāmārgasya lakṣaṇam, bhedaḥ, avadhiśceti trīṇi parijñātavyānyatra saṃkṣepato nirūpyante / abhisamayālaṅkāre tatsvarūpaṃ pañcabhiḥ kārikābhirupadarśitam /
children.translated_text:
4. The Mahāyāna path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>)
Regarding the path of seeing that possesses great benefit (<s>mahānuśaṃsa</s>), three things should be understood here: its definition, divisions, and scope. These are explained here in brief. Its essential nature is displayed in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through five verses.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
bhavaśamāntadvayanirodhalakṣaṇaḥ satyābhisamayo mahāyānadarśanamārga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of the Mahāyāna path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) is: the realization of truth (<s>satyābhisamaya</s>) characterized by the cessation of the two [extremes] of existence (<s>bhava</s>) and quiescence (<s>śama</s>).

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
samāhitajñānaṃ pṛṣṭhalabdhajñānaṃ ceti dvau darśanamārgasya bhedau /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are two divisions of the path of seeing: meditative equipoise knowledge (<s>samāhitajñāna</s>) and subsequent attainment knowledge (<s>pṛṣṭhalabdhajñāna</s>).

children.text: jñānadṛṣṭyā trīṇi jñānāni darśanamārgaḥ / prathamaṃ yad darśanamārgabhūtaṃ śrāvakamārgaṃ jānāti, dvitīyaṃ yat pratyekabuddhamārgaṃ jānāti / tṛtīyaṃ yanmahāyānamārgaṃ jānātīti trayo bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: From the perspective of knowledge, there are three knowledges constituting the path of seeing: the first knows the <s>śrāvaka</s> path that constitutes the path of seeing, the second knows the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> path, and the third knows the Mahāyāna path — thus there are three divisions.

children.text: ālambanadṛṣṭyā vyāvṛttidṛṣṭyā cāṣṭau kṣāntayaḥ, aṣṭau ca jñānānīti ṣoḍaśa bhedā avasātavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: From the perspective of objects and exclusions, there are sixteen divisions to be determined: eight <s>kṣāntis</s> (acceptances) and eight <s>jñānas</s> (knowledges).

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
prathamāyāmeva bodhisattvabhūmāvasya vyāptirbhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
Its range extends only across the first <s>bodhisattva</s> stage (<s>bhūmi</s>).

children.text:
5. bhāvanāmārgakāritram
bhāvanāmārgakāritrāṇāṃ lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā spaṣṭamupadarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
5. Activities of the path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārgakāritra</s>)
The definition and so forth of the activities of the path of meditation are clearly displayed in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through one verse. Namely:

children.text: sarvato damanaṃ nāma sarvataḥ kleśanirjayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The taming called 'universal taming' (<s>sarvato damana</s>), the conquest of all afflictions (<s>kleśanirjaya</s>),

children.text: upakramāviṣahyatvaṃ bodhirādhārapūjyatā //
children.translated_text: invulnerability to attack, awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), and the worthiness of worship as a support —

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
dṛṣṭatattvabhāvanābalena prāptānuśaṃsā bhāvanāmārgakāritrasya lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of the activities of the path of meditation is: the benefits attained through the power of meditating on realized reality (<s>dṛṣṭatattva</s>).

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
asya ṣaḍ bhedā bhavanti, yathā - ātmotkarṣaniṣedhāt damanakāritram, sarvajananamanakāritram, rāgādikleśābhibhavakāritram, parakṛtāghātavirodhopanipātād upakramāviṣahyatvakāritram, samyak saṃbodhipratipattikāritram, prajñāpāramitādhāraviṣayapūjyatākāritramiti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are six divisions of this, namely: the taming activity through the prohibition of self-aggrandizement, the activity of pleasing all people, the activity of overcoming afflictions such as passion (<s>rāga</s>), the activity of invulnerability to attacks and hostile assaults by others, the activity of the practice of perfect complete awakening (<s>samyaksambodhi</s>), and the activity of being worthy of worship as having the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as its domain and support.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
prathamāṃ bhūmimārabhya daśamīṃ bhūmiṃ yāvadasya sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
Its boundary extends from the first stage (<s>bhūmi</s>) up to the tenth stage (<s>bhūmi</s>).

children.text: bhāvanāmārgaṃḥ asya lakṣaṇam, bhedaḥ avadhiśceti trīṇyatrocyante /
children.translated_text: The path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>): its definition, divisions, and scope — these three are stated here.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
māhāyāniko 'nvabhisamayaḥ mahāyānabhāvanāmarga iti lakṣaṇam /
anvabhisamayaḥ bhāvanāmārga iti paryāyavācinau /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of the Mahāyāna path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) is: a Mahāyāna subsequent realization (<s>anvabhisamaya</s>).
<s>Anvabhisamaya</s> (subsequent realization) and <s>bhāvanāmārga</s> (path of meditation) are synonymous terms.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
sāsravo bhāvanāmārgaḥ, anāsravo bhāvanāmārgaśceti dvau bhedau / tatra sāsravaḥ savikalpabhāvanāmārgaḥ anāsravaśca nirvikalpa iti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are two divisions: the contaminated (<s>sāsrava</s>) path of meditation and the uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>) path of meditation. Among these, the contaminated is the conceptual (<s>savikalpa</s>) path of meditation, and the uncontaminated is the non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>) path.

children.text: tatra sāsravo 'dhimuktipariṇāmanānumodanāmanaskāralakṣaṇastrividhaḥ / anāsravaḥ punarabhinirhāraḥ atyantaviśuddhisvabhāvaśceti dvividhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Among these, the contaminated is threefold, characterized by aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>), dedication (<s>pariṇāmanā</s>), rejoicing (<s>anumodanā</s>), and mental engagement (<s>manaskāra</s>). The uncontaminated, in turn, is twofold: actualization (<s>abhinirhāra</s>) and ultimate purification (<s>atyantaviśuddhi</s>) in nature.

children.text:
6. bhāvanāmārgādhimuktiḥ
adhimuktibhāvanāmārgasya lakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kārikābhyāṃ spaṣṭamādarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
6. Aspiration of the path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārgādhimukti</s>)
The definition and so forth of the aspiration-path of meditation are all clearly shown in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through two verses. Namely:

children.text: adhimuktistridhā jñeyā svārthā ca svaparārthikā /
children.translated_text: Aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>) should be known as threefold: for one's own benefit, for both one's own and others' benefit,

children.text: parārthikaivetyeṣā ca pratyekaṃ trividheṣyate //
children.translated_text: and for others' benefit alone — and each of these is held to be threefold.

children.text: mṛdvī madhyādhimātrā ca mṛdumṛdvādibhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: Mild, middling, and supreme — through the subdivision of mild-mild and so forth,

children.text: sā punastrividhetyevaṃ saptaviṃśatidhā matā //
children.translated_text: each is again threefold — thus it is considered to be twenty-sevenfold.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
svārtha-svaparārtha-parārthākarabhūtāyāṃ jinajananyām abhisampratyayavaśena vyavasthāpito māhāyāniko 'nvabhisamayo 'dhimuktyākhyabhāvanāmārgaḥ savikalpa iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of the aspiration-named path of meditation (<s>adhimuktyākhyabhāvanāmārga</s>) is: a Mahāyāna subsequent realization, conceptual in nature (<s>savikalpa</s>), established through the force of conviction (<s>abhisampratyaya</s>) in the mother of the conquerors (<s>jinajanī</s>) [i.e., the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] that has the form of one's own benefit, the benefit of both self and others, and the benefit of others.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
adhimuktiḥ svārthā svaparārthā parārthā ceti mūlabhedena trividhā / trividhā 'pi satī mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedena pratyekaṃ medāt trikatribhirnavadhā bhavati / tadyathā mṛdvī madhyā 'dhimātrā ca svārthādhimuktiḥ; evaṃ svaparārthādhimuktiḥ parārthādhimuktiśceti / evameṣā 'pi navaprakārā 'dhimuktiḥ mṛdumṛdvādiprakārabhedena pratyekaṃ vibhidyamānā navabhistribhiḥ saptaviṃśatiprakārā bhavati / tadyathā - mṛdumṛduḥ, mṛdumadhyaḥ, mṛdvadhimātraḥ, madhyamṛduḥ, madhyamadhyaḥ, madhyādhimātraḥ; adhimātramṛduḥ, adhimātramadhyaḥ, adhimātrādhimātra iti svārthādhimukternavaprakārāḥ / tathā svaparārthādhimukteḥ parārthādhimukteśca veditavyāḥ /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
Conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>) is of three kinds as a basic division: for one's own benefit, for both one's own and others' benefit, and for others' benefit. Each of the three, being further divided into mild, medium, and intense [degrees], becomes ninefold through three sets of three. Namely...

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
prathamāṃ bhūmimārabhya daśamīṃ bhūmiṃ yāvad asyāḥ sīmā bhavati / dvitīyāṃ bhūmimārabhyaṃ daśamabhūmiparyantamiti kecit /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope.
Its limit extends from the first stage (<s>bhūmi</s>) through the tenth stage. Some say from the second stage through the tenth stage.

children.text:
7. bhāvanāmārgādhimuktasya stutiḥ stobhaḥ praśaṃsā ca
bhāvanāmārgādhimuktasya bodhisattvasya stutyādīnāṃ lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayopavarṇitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
7. Praise, eulogy, and commendation of one who has conviction on the path of cultivation.
The definition and so on of praise and the rest for the <s>bodhisattva</s> who has conviction on the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) are described in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in one verse. Namely:

children.text: stutiḥ stobhaḥ praśaṃsā ca prajñāpāramitāṃ prati /
children.translated_text: Praise, eulogy, and commendation regarding the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom),

children.text: adhimokṣasya mātrāṇāṃ navakaistribhiriṣyate //
children.translated_text: of the measures of conviction, are held [to be] by the three sets of nine.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
purvoktatrividhādhimuktiprajñāpāramitāṃ prati pravṛttasya tadbhāvakabodhisattvasyotsāhavardhanārthaṃ tadadhimokṣasya kriyamāṇāḥ stutyādayo yathābhūtārthādhigamalakṣaṇā nārthavādarūpā iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The praise and so on that are directed toward the <s>bodhisattva</s> who cultivates the aforementioned threefold conviction regarding the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, performed for the purpose of increasing his enthusiasm — these have the character of the realization of the meaning as it truly is...

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
pūrvavat saptaviṃśatireva prabhedāḥ /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
As before, there are exactly twenty-seven subdivisions.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
adhimuktibhāvanāmārgavat /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope.
Same as that of the conviction on the path of cultivation.

children.text:
8. bhāvanāmārgapariṇāmanā
asyāḥ pariṇāmanāyāḥ lakṣaṇabhedādisarvaṃ svarūpam abhisamayālaṅkāre tisṛbhiḥ kārikābhiḥ spaṣṭamupadarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
8. Dedication on the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārgapariṇāmanā</s>).
The entire nature of this dedication — its definition, classification, and so on — is clearly shown in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in three verses. Namely:

children.text: viśeṣaḥ pariṇāmastu tasya kāritramuttamam /
children.translated_text: Dedication is special, and its supreme function;

children.text: nopalambhākṛtiścāsāvaviparyāsalakṣaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: it is of the form of non-apprehension, and has the character of non-perversion.

children.text: vivikto buddhapuṇyaughasvabhāvasmṛtigocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: It is isolated, has the nature of the stream of Buddha's merit, and its domain is mindfulness;

children.text: sopāyaścānimittaśca buddhairabhyanumoditaḥ //
children.translated_text: it is accompanied by means (<s>upāya</s>), signless, and approved by the Buddhas.

children.text: traidhātukāprapannaśca pariṇāmo 'parastridhā /
children.translated_text: Not extending to the three realms, dedication is further threefold:

children.text: mṛdurmadhyo 'dhimātraśca mahāpuṇyodayātmakaḥ //
