children.translated_text: mild, medium, and intense, having the nature of the arising of great merit.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
yo māhāyānikaḥ savikalpo 'nvabhisamayaḥ svaparakuśalapuṇyakriyāvastu anuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau pariṇāmayati, sa pariṇāmanākhyo mahāyānabhāvanāmārga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The <s>Mahāyāna</s> conceptual subsequent realization (<s>anvabhisamaya</s>) that dedicates one's own and others' meritorious and virtuous bases of action (<s>kuśalapuṇyakriyāvastu</s>) toward unsurpassed perfect awakening — that [realization] called 'dedication' is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of cultivation. This is its definition.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
ayaṃ bhāvanāmārgo dvādaśavidho bhavati, tadyathā - viśeṣapariṇāmanāmanaskāraḥ, anupalambhākārapariṇāmanāmanaskāraḥ, aviparyāsalakṣaṇaḥ pariṇāmanāmanaskāraḥ, viviktapariṇāmanāmanaskāraḥ, buddhapuṇyaughasvabhāvānusmṛtipariṇāmanāmanaskāraḥ, upāyakauśalapariṇāmanāmanaskāraḥ, amimittapariṇāmanāmanaskāraḥ, buddhānujñāta (anumodita)-pariṇāmanāmanaskāraḥ, traidhātukāparyāpannapariṇāmanāmanaskāraḥ, mahāpuṇyodayātmako mṛdupariṇāmanāmanaskāraḥ, mahāpuṇyodayātmako madhyapariṇāmanāmanaskāraḥ, mahāpuṇyodayātmako 'dhimātrapariṇāmanāmanaskāra iti dvādaśa bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
This path of cultivation is of twelve kinds, namely: the mental engagement of special dedication, the mental engagement of dedication in the form of non-apprehension, the mental engagement of dedication having the character of non-perversion, the [mental engagement of] isolated dedication...

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
prathamāṃ pramuditā bhūmimārabhya yāvad daśamīṃ bhūmimasya pariṇāmanāmanaskārasya sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope.
The limit of this mental engagement of dedication extends from the first <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) stage through the tenth stage.

children.text:
9. bhāvanāmārgīyānumodanā
anumodanāmanaskārasya lakṣaṇabhedādayo 'bhisamayālaṅkāre ekayaiva kārikayetthamupavarṇitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
9. Rejoicing on the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārgīyānumodanā</s>).
The definition, classification, and so on of the mental engagement of rejoicing are described in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in one verse thus. Namely:

children.text: upāyānupalambhābhyāṃ śubhamūlānumodanā /
children.translated_text: Through means (<s>upāya</s>) and non-apprehension, the rejoicing in roots of virtue

children.text: anumode manaskārabhāvaneha vidhīyate //
children.translated_text: is taught here as mental engagement of rejoicing on the cultivation [path].

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
yo māhāyānikaḥ savikalpo 'nvabhisamayaḥ sva-parakuśalapuṇyakriyāvastūni anumodate, sa anumodanākhyo mahāyānabhāvanāmārga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The <s>Mahāyāna</s> conceptual subsequent realization that rejoices in one's own and others' meritorious and virtuous bases of action — that [realization] called 'rejoicing' is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of cultivation. This is its definition.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
anumodanāmanaskārasya dvau bhedau bhavataḥ, yathā-svakuśalapuṇyakriyāvastvanumodanam, parakuśalapuṇyakriyāvastvanumodanaṃ iti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
The mental engagement of rejoicing has two divisions, namely: rejoicing in one's own meritorious and virtuous bases of action, and rejoicing in others' meritorious and virtuous bases of action.

children.text: athavā - saṃvṛtiviṣayī anumodanāmanaskāraḥ paramārthaviṣayī anumodanāmanaskāraśceti /
children.translated_text: Alternatively: the mental engagement of rejoicing that has conventional [truth] as its object, and the mental engagement of rejoicing that has ultimate [truth] as its object.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
adhimuktipariṇāmanānumodanāmanaskārāṇāṃ trayāṇāṃ bhūmyavadhiḥ samāna eva /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope.
The stage-scope of the three — conviction, dedication, and rejoicing mental engagements — is the same.

children.text:
10. abhinirhāraḥ
anāsravasya abhinirhārabhāvanāmārgasya lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā pratipāditam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
10. Accomplishment (<s>abhinirhāra</s>).
The definition and so on of the uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>) path of cultivation of accomplishment are set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in one verse. Namely:

children.text: svabhāva-śreṣṭhatā tasya sarvasyānabhisaṃskṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: Its own-nature, supremacy, the non-formation of everything,

children.text: nopalambhena dharmāṇāmarpaṇā ca mahārthatā //
children.translated_text: the dedication of <s>dharmas</s> through non-apprehension — and [this is] of great significance.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
māhāyāniko 'nāsravo 'nvabhisamayaḥ, yaḥ paryaṃntādhigamakṛtyaṃ vyavasthāpayati, sa abhinirhārākhyo mahāyānabhāvanāmārga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The <s>Mahāyāna</s> uncontaminated subsequent realization that establishes the function of the final realization — that [realization] called 'accomplishment' is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of cultivation. This is its definition.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
asya pañca bhedā bhavanti, tadyathā - rūpādisarvadharmāviparītadarśanaṃ svabhāvaḥ, nānyathā buddhatvasamprāptiriti bhāvanāmārgasya śreṣṭhatā, sarvadharmaviśeṣānutpādanena adhigamaprayogo 'nabhisaṃskāraḥ, sarvadharmāṇāṃ paramārthato 'nupalambhatayā arpaṇā, buddhatvamahārthasādhanānmahārthateti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
This has five divisions, namely: own-nature, which is the undistorted perception of all <s>dharmas</s> such as form and so on; supremacy, meaning that Buddhahood is not attained otherwise than through the path of cultivation; non-production of all distinctions among <s>dharmas</s>...

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
prathamāṃ bhūmimārabhya daśamīṃ bhūmiṃ yāvadasyābhinirhārasya sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope.
The limit of this accomplishment extends from the first stage through the tenth stage.

children.text:
11. atyantaviśuddhiḥ
atyantaviśuddhyākhyasya anāsravabhāvanāmārgasya lakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre tisṛbhiḥ kārikābhiḥ suspaṣṭaṃ pratipāditam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
11. Complete purity (<s>atyantaviśuddhi</s>).
The entire definition and so on of the uncontaminated path of cultivation called complete purity is very clearly set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in three verses. Namely:

children.text: phalaśuddhiśca rūpādiśuddhireva tayordvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Purity of the fruit and purity of form and so on; because the severance

children.text: abhinnācchinnatā yasmāditi śuddhirudīritā //
children.translated_text: of both [defilements and objects of knowledge] is undifferentiated — this purity is proclaimed.

children.text: kleśajñeyatrimārgasya śiṣyakhaḍgajinaurasām /
children.translated_text: Through the elimination of the affliction, cognitive, and triple-path [obscurations]

children.text: hānād viśuddhirātyantikī tu buddhasya sarvadā //
children.translated_text: of disciples, solitary realizers, and the <s>Jina</s>'s [spiritual] sons — the complete purity of the <s>Buddha</s> is always [present].

children.text: mṛdumṛdvādiko mārgaḥ śuddhirnavasu bhūmiṣu /
children.translated_text: The path beginning with mild-mild is the purity on the nine stages,

children.text: adhimātrādhimātrādermalasya pratipakṣataḥ //
children.translated_text: as the antidote to defilements beginning with the intense-intense.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
māhāyāniko 'nāsravo 'nvabhisamayaḥ, yo 'ntimaprahāṇasya kṛtyaṃ vyavasthāpayati, sa atyantaviśuddhyākhyo mahāyānabhāvanāmārga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The <s>Mahāyāna</s> uncontaminated subsequent realization that establishes the function of the final abandonment — that [realization] called 'complete purity' is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of cultivation. This is its definition.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
bhāvanāmārgaprahātavyānāṃ navānāṃ vipakṣāṇāṃ pratipakṣabhūtā mṛdumṛdvādayo nava bhāvanāmārgā evāsya atyantaviśuddhibhāvanāmārgasya bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
The nine paths of cultivation beginning with mild-mild, which are the antidotes to the nine adverse factors to be abandoned on the path of cultivation — these are the divisions of this path of cultivation of complete purity.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
prathamāṃ bhūmimārabhya daśamabhūmiparyantamasya bhāvanāmārgasya sīmā bhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope.
The limit of this path of cultivation extends from the first stage through the tenth stage.

children.text: // iti mārgajñatopalakṣakā ekādaśa dharmāḥ //
children.translated_text: // Thus the eleven <s>dharmas</s> that characterize the knowledge of paths (<s>mārgajñatā</s>). //

children.text: (i) sarvajñatopalakṣakā nava dharmāḥ
children.translated_text: (III) The nine <s>dharmas</s> that characterize omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>):

children.text: 1. prajñayā na bhave sthānam, 2. kṛpayā na śame sthitiḥ, 3. anupāyena jinajananyā dūratvam, 4. upāyena avidūratā, 5. vipakṣaḥ, 6. pratipakṣaḥ, prayogaḥ, 8. samatā, 9. darśanamārgaśceti nava dharmāḥ sarvajñatopalakṣakā iti abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kārikābhyāṃ samyaguktāḥ / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: 1. Non-abiding in existence through wisdom, 2. Non-abiding in quiescence through compassion, 3. Distance from the Mother of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) through lack of means, 4. Non-distance through means, 5. Adverse factor, 6. Antidote, 7. Practice, 8. Equality, 9. Path of seeing...

children.text: prajñayā na bhave sthānaṃ kṛpayā na śame sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Non-abiding in existence through wisdom, non-abiding in quiescence through compassion,

children.text: anupāyena dūratvam upāyenāvidūratā //
children.translated_text: distance through lack of means, non-distance through means,

children.text: vipakṣapratipakṣau ca prayogaḥ samatā 'sya ca /
children.translated_text: adverse factor and antidote, practice, and its equality,

children.text: dṛṅmārgaḥ śrāvakādīnāmiti sarvajñateṣyate //
children.translated_text: and the path of seeing of <s>śrāvakas</s> and others — [this] is held to be omniscience.

children.text:
1. prajñatā na bhave sthānam
2. kṛpayā na śame sthitiḥ
children.translated_text:
1. Non-abiding in existence through wisdom.
2. Non-abiding in quiescence through compassion.

children.text: ubhayorlakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā pratipāditam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: The definition and so on of both are set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in one verse. Namely:

children.text: nāpare na pare tīre nāntarāle tayoḥ sthitā /
children.translated_text: Not on this shore, not on the far shore, and not standing between the two,

children.text: adhvanāṃ samatājñānāt prajñāpāramitā matā //
children.translated_text: through the knowledge of the equality of the [three] times — [this] is considered the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom).

children.text: tatra ubhayoḥ lakṣaṇādīni pṛthak pṛthagatrābhidhīyante /
children.translated_text: Therein, the definitions and so on of both are stated separately here.

children.text: prajñayā na bhave sthānam
children.translated_text: Non-abiding in existence through wisdom:

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
anityādiṣoḍaśākārāṇāṃ sākṣātkāriṇī hīnayānajātīyā mahākaruṇāgarbhā māhāyānikaryasantatisthā prajñā asyāḥ sarvajñatāyā lakṣaṇam / iyaṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ prajñāpāramitā prajñayā saṃsārādīnavadarśanāt na saṃsāre bhavānte sthitā /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) that directly realizes the sixteen aspects such as impermanence and so on, that is of the <s>Hīnayāna</s> type [in form but], has the womb of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), and exists in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> noble [being's] mental continuum — [this] is the definition of this omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>). And this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>...

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
darśanamārgaḥ bhāvanāmārgaḥ aśaikṣamārgaśceti trayo bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
The path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>), the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), and the path of no-more-learning (<s>aśaikṣamārga</s>) — these are the three divisions.

children.text: duḥkhādicaturāryasatyasambaddhānityādiṣoḍaśākārāṇāṃ sākṣātkārī mahāyānabhāvanāmārgo 'syāḥ sarvajñatāyāḥ prajñatā na bhave sthānamitilakṣaṇātmikāyā upalakṣakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of cultivation that directly realizes the sixteen aspects such as impermanence and so forth, connected with the four noble truths of suffering and the like, is the indicator of this <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), whose defining characteristic is the <s>prajñatā</s> (wisdom) of the nature 'there is no abiding in existence.'

children.text: kṛpayā na śame sthitiḥ
children.translated_text: Through compassion, no abiding in cessation.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
mahākaruṇayā saṃvṛtyapekṣaśamāntavyāvartako māhāyāniko 'bhisamayo 'syāḥ sarvajñatāyā lakṣaṇam / iyaṃ ca prajñāpāramitā kṛpayā sattvārthakaraṇāt na nirvāṇe śamānte sthitā / māhāyānikabhāvanāmārgīyāryapudgalasantatisthā mahākaruṇā asyāḥ kṛpayā na śame sthitiritimārgajñatāyā upalakṣikā /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>) that, through great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), turns away from the extreme of cessation (<s>śamānta</s>) from the conventional perspective — that is the defining characteristic of this <s>sarvajñatā</s>. And this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, through compassion and acting for the benefit of beings, does not abide in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the extreme of cessation. The great compassion residing in the continuum of noble <s>Mahāyāna</s> persons on the path of cultivation is its characteristic.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
māhāyānikasyāryasya sattvālambanā dharmālambanā nirālambanā ceti tisro mahākaruṇāḥ, bodhicittotpādādayaśca bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
For a <s>Mahāyāna</s> noble one, there are three [types of] great compassion: that which takes sentient beings as its object (<s>sattvālambana</s>), that which takes <s>dharmas</s> as its object (<s>dharmālambana</s>), and that which is objectless (<s>nirālambana</s>). The arising of the thought of awakening (<s>bodhicittotpāda</s>) and so forth are also divisions.

children.text: traiyadhvikadharmāṇāmanutpādākāreṇa tulyatāvabodhāt yā śrāvakādyagocaratvena viprakṛṣṭā bodhisattvānāṃ prajñāpāramitā, sā punarnāpare tīre saṃsāre, na pare tīre nirvāṇe vyavasthitā / nāpi saṃsāranirvāṇamubhayamantareṇa vastuno 'sattvāt madhye 'pi sthitā, prajñākaruṇayoḥ samyak prativedhena saṃsāranirvāṇobhayopalambhaviyogāt /
children.translated_text: The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s> which, through the understanding of equality in the aspect of non-origination of <s>dharmas</s> of the three times, is far removed [from the ordinary] by being beyond the range of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and the like — that does not abide on the near shore of <s>saṃsāra</s>, nor on the far shore of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Nor does it abide in the middle apart from both <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, since no [such middle] entity exists.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
prathamāṃ pramuditābhūmimārabhya buddhabhūmiparyantamubhayoḥ sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Limit.
From the first <s>bhūmi</s> (ground), <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful), up to the <s>Buddha</s>-ground — that is the boundary of both [prajñā and karuṇā].

children.text:
3. anupāyena dūratvam
asya lakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre kārikārdhena spaṣṭamullikhitam tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
3. Distance through lack of means (<s>anupāyena dūratva</s>).
All of its characteristics and the like have been clearly delineated in a half-verse in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Thus:

children.text: anupāyena dūraṃ sā sanimittopalabhbhataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Through lack of means, it [the Mother] is distant, because of apprehension with signs.'

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
śrāvakādīnām adhvasamatājñānābhāvāt anityādyākārāṇāṃ sākṣātkāri jñānaṃ sanimittopalambhayogena kṛpāprajñāvaikalyāt dūrībhūtaṃ jinajananyā iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
Because <s>Śrāvakas</s> and the like lack the knowledge of the equality of the three times, their knowledge that directly realizes aspects such as impermanence and the like, through its connection with apprehension based on signs, and through its deficiency in compassion and wisdom, has become distant from the Mother of the <s>Jinas</s> — this is the definition.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
śrāvakasantatisthaṃ anityādyākārajñānaṃ pratyekabuddhasantatisthaṃ cānityādyākārajñānamiti bhedadvayam /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
The knowledge of aspects such as impermanence and the like residing in the continuum of a <s>Śrāvaka</s>, and the knowledge of aspects such as impermanence and the like residing in the continuum of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> — these are the two divisions.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
darśanamārgamārabhya arhattvāvasthāparyantamasya sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Limit.
From the path of seeing up to the stage of <s>arhatship</s> — that is its boundary.

children.text:
4. upāyena avidūratā
asya lakṣaṇādīnāṃ pratipādanam abhisamayālaṅkāre kārikārdhena samyak kṛtam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
4. Nearness through means (<s>upāyena avidūratā</s>).
The presentation of its characteristics and the like has been properly accomplished in a half-verse in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Thus:

children.text: upāyakauśalenāsyāḥ samyagāsannatoditā //
children.translated_text: 'Through skillful means, its proper nearness has been stated.'

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
mahākaruṇayā śūnyatāsākṣātkāriṇyā prajñayā copāttaṃ māhāyānikaryāṇāṃ hīnayānajātīyam anityādyākārajñānam asya lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The knowledge of aspects such as impermanence and the like, which belongs to the <s>Hīnayāna</s> class but is taken up by <s>Mahāyāna</s> noble ones through great compassion and the wisdom that directly realizes emptiness — this is its definition.

children.text: "bodhisattvādīnāṃ tu utsāritabhāvābhiniveśabhrāntinimittānāṃ rūpādisarvadharmaparijñānameva tatsamatāparijñānamityataḥ samyagāsannībhāvo māturiti jñeyam /"
children.translated_text: 'For <s>bodhisattvas</s> and the like, however, since the delusory causes of attachment to the [inherent] existence [of entities] have been removed, the thorough knowledge of all <s>dharmas</s> such as form and the like is itself the thorough knowledge of their equality. Therefore, this should be understood as the proper nearness to the Mother.'

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
māhāyāniko darśanamārgaḥ, bhāvanāmārgaḥ, aśaikṣamārgaśceti trayo bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
The <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of seeing, the path of cultivation, and the path of no-more-learning — these are the three divisions.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
mahāyānadarśanamārgamārabhya buddhabhūmiparyantaṃ sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Limit.
From the <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of seeing up to the <s>Buddha</s>-ground — that is its boundary.

children.text:
5. vipakṣaḥ
asya lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayāṃ kārikayā suspaṣṭaṃ pratipāditam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
5. The adversary (<s>vipakṣa</s>).
All of its characteristics and the like have been very clearly presented in one verse in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Thus:

children.text: rūpādiskandhaśūnyatve dharmeṣu tryadhvageṣu ca /
children.translated_text: 'Regarding the emptiness of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) such as form and the like, and regarding <s>dharmas</s> of the three times,

children.text: dānādau bodhipakṣeṣu caryāsaṃjñā vipakṣatā //
children.translated_text: and regarding giving and the like and the factors conducive to awakening — the notion of [inherent] practice is the adversary.'

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
mahākaruṇā śūnyatāprajñābhyāṃ viyuktā bhāvolambhasvabhāvā hainayānikī vastujñateti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
Great compassion that is separated from the wisdom of emptiness, whose nature is apprehension of [inherent] existence, [and] the knowledge of reality (<s>vastujñatā</s>) belonging to the <s>Hīnayāna</s> — this is the definition.

children.text: "sarveṣāṃ rūpādīnāṃ traiyadhvikānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ sāsravānāsravobhayasthānīyānāmanupalambhasvarūpāṇāṃ sarvatra bhāvopalambhatayā te paraparikalpitātmādiśūnyatvena dṛṣṭāḥ / anuṣṭhānasaṃjñā tu eteṣāṃ pratipakṣabhūtāpi viparyāsapravṛttatvena heyatvāt vipakṣo bhavati /"
children.translated_text: 'All <s>dharmas</s> such as form and the like, including those of the three times, whether in the category of the contaminated, the uncontaminated, or both — though their essential nature is non-apprehension — are everywhere viewed through the apprehension of [inherent] existence as empty of the self and the like as conceived by others. However, even the notion of practice, though it is the antidote to these, is to be abandoned because it operates in a perverted manner; hence it is the adversary.'

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ (ga) avadhiḥ
asya bhedo 'vadhiścetyubhau 'anupāyena dūratvam ' ityasmin prakareṇa yathā pradarśitau, tadvat jñeyāditi /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification. (c) Limit.
Both the classification and limit of this should be understood in the same way as demonstrated under the topic 'distance through lack of means.'

children.text:
6. pratipakṣaḥ
asya lakṣaṇabhedādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre tisṛbhiḥ kārikābhiḥ savistaramupadarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
6. The antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>).
All of its characteristics, classifications, and the like have been extensively shown in three verses in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Thus:

children.text: dānādiṣvanahaṃkāraḥ paraṣāṃ tanniyojanam /
children.translated_text: 'Non-ego-grasping regarding giving and the like, directing others to that,

children.text: saṅgakoṭīniṣedho 'yaṃ sūkṣmaḥ saṅgo jinādiṣu //
children.translated_text: the prohibition of the category of attachment — this is the subtle attachment to the <s>Jinas</s> and the like.'

children.text: tadgāmbhīryaṃ prakṛtyaiva vivekād dharmapaddhateḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Its profundity, by its very nature, through the separation of the path of <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: ekaprakṛtikaṃ jñānaṃ dharmāṇāṃ saṅgavarjanam //
children.translated_text: knowledge of a single nature of <s>dharmas</s> — the abandonment of attachment.'

children.text: dṛṣṭādipratiṣedhena tasyā durbodhatoditā /
children.translated_text: 'Through the prohibition of views and the like, its difficult-to-comprehend nature has been stated.'

children.text: rūpādibhiravijñānāt tadacintyatvamiṣyate //

(ka) lakṣaṇam
mahākaruṇopāyena śūnyatāsākṣātkāriṇyā prajñayā copāttā māhāyānikāryasantatisthā vastujñatā pratipakṣalakṣaṇātmikā /

(kha) bhedo 'vadhiśca
ubhāvapi pūrva 'upāyena avidūratā ' ityasmin prasaṅge yathāvarṇitau tathā jñātavyau /

viśeṣaḥ
jinajananyā dūratvam avidūratvamiti vastujñatāyāḥ (sarvajñatāyāḥ) dvau bhedau / hīnayānāpuraḥsarāyāḥ phalabhūtajinajananyāḥ avidūratā, upāyakauśalena avidūratā, pratipakṣaḥ, māhāyānīyavastujñatā ceti catvāraḥ paryāyāḥ /
phalabhūtajinajananyā dūratvama, anupāyena dūratvam, nimittopalambhagrāhapratibaddhatā, vipakṣaḥ, hīnayānavastujñatā ceti paryāyavācinaḥ.
yathānirdiṣṭa eva śrāvakabodhisatvādīnāṃ vipakṣapratipakṣayorayaṃ vibhāgo 'vasātavyaḥ / tathā coktam -
evaṃ kṛtvā yathoktau vai jñeyaḥ sarvajñatānaye /
ayaṃ vibhāgo niḥśeṣo vipakṣapratipakṣayoḥ //

api ca -
"śrāvakādīnāmevaṃ māturdūrībhāvenānuṣṭhānaṃ pratipakṣo 'pi san vastūpalambhaviparyāsapravṛttatvena bodhisattvānāṃ tyājyatvād vipakṣa iti" /

7. prayogaḥ
asya lakṣaṇabhedādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre sārdhadvayena kārikāgranthena savistaraṃ pratipāditam / tathā hi -
rūpādau tadanityādau tadapūriprapūrayoḥ /
tadasaṅgatve caryāyāḥ prayogaḥ pratiṣedhataḥ //
avikāro na kartā ca prayogo duṣkarastridhā /
yathābhavyaṃ phalaprāpteravandhyo 'bhimataśca saḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Because of the attainment of results as appropriate, it is not barren and is approved.'

children.text: aparapratyayo yaśca saptadhā khyātivedakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And [the knowledge] that is independent of others, sevenfold, is the proclaimer of understanding.'

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
sāṃvṛtike vastusvarūpe tadviśeṣe ca viparyāsapravṛttasya upalambhābhiniveśasya pratipakṣabhūto hīnayānajātīyaḥ sattvayogaḥ prayoga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The practice (<s>prayoga</s>) of the <s>Hīnayāna</s> class, which is the engagement of beings [in the path], being the antidote to the attachment to apprehension that operates in a perverted manner regarding the conventional nature of things and their specific [characteristics] — this is the definition.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
prayogaḥ daśavidho bhavati / tadyathā - rūpādiṣu satyābhiniveśapratiṣedhaḥ, tadviśeṣeṣvanityādiṣu satyābhiniveśapratiṣedhaḥ, kalpitarūpeṣu aparipūriḥ, dharmatārūpeṣu prapūriḥ, pāramitāsu paramārthato 'parihāṇivṛddhī (avikāratvam), paramārthato 'kartṛtvam, trisarvajñātmakānāṃ yathākramamuddeśaprayogakāritrāṇāṃ duṣkaratā, yathābhavyaphalaprāptyā avandhyatā, mahānuśaṃsāyāṃ bodhau aparapratyayatvam, svapnopamapariṇāmādisaptavidhakhyātijñānamiti daśa bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
The practice is tenfold: the prohibition of attachment to reality regarding form and the like; the prohibition of attachment to reality regarding their specific [aspects] such as impermanence and the like; the incompleteness regarding conceptually imputed forms; the completeness regarding the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality) forms; regarding the <s>pāramitās</s>, the absence of deterioration and increase ultimately (i.e., changelessness); the ultimate

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
sambhāramārgamārabhya antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvāvasthāparyantamasya sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Limit.
From the path of accumulation (<s>sambhāramārga</s>) up to the state of the <s>bodhisattva</s> at the final moment — that is its boundary.

children.text:
8. samatā
asyāḥ svarūpam abhisamayālaṅkāre kārikārdhena samādarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
8. Equality (<s>samatā</s>).
Its essential nature has been equally shown in a half-verse in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Thus:

children.text: caturdhā 'mananā tasya rūpādau samatā matā /
children.translated_text: 'The fourfold non-mentation regarding form and the like is considered the equality of that [omniscience].'

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
uparyuktadaśavidhavastujñatāprayogākārāṇāṃ jñātṛjñeyadharmāṇām amananā samatāyā lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The non-mentation (<s>amananā</s>) regarding the <s>dharmas</s> of the knower and the knowable, [which constitute] the aspects of the tenfold practice of the knowledge of reality mentioned above — this is the definition of equality.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
pūrvokteṣu daśavidhaprayogeṣu pratisvaṃ catasraḥ amananā bhavantīti catvāriṃśadasyāḥ samatāyāḥ prabhedā bhavanti / uktaṃ cālokaṭīkāyām -
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
Regarding each of the ten types of practice mentioned above, there are four [types of] non-mentation. Thus, there are forty subdivisions of this equality. As stated in the <s>Ālokaṭīkā</s>:

children.text: "tadevaṃ rūpādipadārthamananā-nīlādinimittamananā-'rūpaṃ dvidhā viṃśatidhe '-tyādiprapañcamananā-nirvedhabhāgīyādyadhigamamananānāṃ pratiṣedhena jñātṛjñeyadharmānupalabdhiścaturvidhoktā vijñeyā /"
children.translated_text: 'Thus, through the prohibition of non-mentation regarding the categories of form and the like, non-mentation regarding the signs such as blue and the like, non-mentation regarding the elaboration of "form is twofold, twentyfold" and so forth, and non-mentation regarding the realization of the factors conducive to penetration and the like — the fourfold non-apprehension of the <s>dharmas</s> of the knower and the knowable should be understood.'

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
sambhāramārgamārabhya antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvāvasthāparyantamasyāḥ samatāyāḥ sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text: (c) Limit (<s>avadhi</s>). The boundary of this equanimity (<s>samatā</s>) extends from the path of accumulation (<s>sambhāramārga</s>) up to the state of a <s>bodhisattva</s> at the final moment.

children.text:
9. darśanamārgaḥ
asya lakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre pañcabhiḥ kārikābhiḥ pratipāditam /
children.translated_text: 9. The path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>). All its characteristics and so forth are set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in five verses.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
dvātriṃśatsamāropaśūnyaḥ satyābhisamayo darśanamārga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: (a) Definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). The realization of the [four noble] truths (<s>satyābhisamaya</s>) that is empty of the thirty-two superimpositions (<s>samāropa</s>) is the definition of the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>).

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
trayāṇāṃ yānānāṃ trayāṇāṃ darśamārgāṇāṃ vyāvṛttibhedena ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇā evāsya ṣoḍaśa bhedā bhavantīti /
children.translated_text: (b) Division (<s>bheda</s>). Through the distinction of exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) of the three paths of seeing of the three vehicles, the sixteen moments (<s>kṣaṇa</s>) are indeed its sixteen divisions.

children.text: // iti sarvajñatopalakṣakā nava dharmāḥ //
children.translated_text: // Thus [end] the nine <s>dharmas</s> that characterize omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>). //

children.text: 2. Catuḥprayogopalakṣakāḥ ṣaṭtriṃśad dharmāḥ
children.translated_text: 2. The thirty-six <s>dharmas</s> that characterize the four applications (<s>catuḥprayoga</s>).

children.text: tatra sarvākārābhisambodhopalakṣakā ekādaśa dharmāḥ, mūrdhābhisamayopalakṣakā aṣṭau dharmāḥ, ānupūrvikābhisamayopakṣakāstrayodaśa dharmāḥ, ekakṣaṇābhisambodhopalakṣakāścatvāra iti ṣaṭtriṃśad bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Among these, eleven <s>dharmas</s> characterize the complete realization of all aspects (<s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s>), eight <s>dharmas</s> characterize the peak realization (<s>mūrdhābhisamaya</s>), thirteen <s>dharmas</s> characterize the sequential realization (<s>ānupūrvikābhisamaya</s>), and four characterize the realization in a single moment (<s>ekakṣaṇābhisambodha</s>) — [together they] make thirty-six.

children.text: (a) sarvākārābhisambodhopalakṣakā ekādaśa dharmāḥ
children.translated_text: (a) The eleven <s>dharmas</s> characterizing the complete realization of all aspects (<s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s>).

children.text: 1. ākārāḥ, 2. prayogāḥ, 3. guṇāḥ, 4. doṣāḥ, 5. lakṣaṇāni, 6. mokṣabhāgīyam, 7. nirvedhabhāgīyam, 8. avaivartiko gaṇaḥ, 9. bhavaśāntyoḥ samatā, 10. anuttarā kṣetraśuddhiḥ, 11. upāyakauśalamityekādaśa dharmāḥ sarvākārābhisambodhamupalakṣayantīti abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kārikābhyāmupadarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: 1. Aspects (<s>ākāra</s>), 2. Applications (<s>prayoga</s>), 3. Qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), 4. Faults (<s>doṣa</s>), 5. Characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), 6. Factors conducive to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>), 7. Factors conducive to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>), 8. The assembly of the irreversible (<s>avaivartika gaṇa</s>), 9. Equanimity of existence and peace (<s>bhavaśāntyoḥ samatā</s>), 10. Unsurpassed purification of the [Buddha-]field (<s>anuttarā kṣetraśuddhi</s>), 11. Skillful means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>) — these eleven <s>dharmas</s> characterize the complete realization of all aspects, as shown in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in two verses. Namely:

children.text: ākārāḥ saprayogāśca guṇā doṣāḥ salakṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Aspects with applications, qualities, faults with characteristics,

children.text: mokṣanirvedhabhāgīye śaikṣo 'vaivartiko gaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: factors conducive to liberation and penetration, the assembly of trainees who are irreversible, //

children.text: samatā bhavaśāntyośca kṣetraśuddhiranuttarā /
children.translated_text: equanimity of existence and peace, and unsurpassed purification of the [Buddha-]field —

children.text: sarvākārābhisambodha eṣa sopāyakauśalaḥ //
children.translated_text: this is the complete realization of all aspects, together with skillful means. //

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
trisarvajñatāsambaddhānāṃ trisaptatyuttaraikaśatākārāṇāṃ bhāvanāmayyā prajñayopāttatvena vyavasthāpitaḥ satvayogaḥ sarvākārābhisambodha iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: (a) Definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). The being's yoga (<s>sattvayoga</s>), established as being taken up by the wisdom born of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>) with regard to the one hundred and seventy-three aspects connected with the three omnisciences (<s>trisarvajñatā</s>), is the definition of the complete realization of all aspects (<s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s>).

children.text:
(kha) paryāyāḥ
bodhisattvamārgaḥ, pāramitāmārgaḥ, sattvayogaḥ, ākārajñatāprayogaḥ, mārgajñatāprayogaḥ, sannāhapratipattirityanarthāntaram /
children.translated_text: (b) Synonyms (<s>paryāya</s>). The <s>bodhisattva</s> path, the <s>pāramitā</s> path, the being's yoga, the application of the knowledge of aspects (<s>ākārajñatāprayoga</s>), the application of the knowledge of paths (<s>mārgajñatāprayoga</s>), and the practice of armor (<s>sannāhapratipatti</s>) — these are synonymous.

children.text:
(ga) bhedaḥ
ākāradṛṣṭyā trisaptatyuttaraśatam, prayogadṛṣṭyā viṃśatiḥ bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: (c) Division (<s>bheda</s>). From the perspective of aspects (<s>ākāra</s>), there are one hundred and seventy-three divisions; from the perspective of applications (<s>prayoga</s>), there are twenty divisions.

children.text:
(gha) avadhiḥ
mahāyānasambhāramārgamārabhya antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvāvasthāparyantamasya sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text: (d) Limit (<s>avadhi</s>). The boundary of this extends from the <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of accumulation (<s>sambhāramārga</s>) up to the state of a <s>bodhisattva</s> at the final moment.

children.text:
1. ākārāḥ
ākārāṇāṃ lakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre pañcabhiḥ kārikābhiḥ savistaraṃ samyagupavarṇitam /
children.translated_text: 1. Aspects (<s>ākāra</s>). All the characteristics and so forth of the aspects are described in full detail and correctly in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in five verses.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
sarvākāramārgavastujñānasaṃgraheṇa trisarvajñatākārāṇāṃ bhāvanāmayaṃ prayogavaiśiṣṭyam ākārāṇāṃ lakṣaṇamiti /
children.translated_text: (a) Definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). The special quality of application (<s>prayogavaiśiṣṭya</s>) that is born of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>) upon the aspects of the three omnisciences, through the comprehensive knowledge of all aspects, paths, and grounds (<s>sarvākāramārgavastujñāna</s>), is the definition of the aspects.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
trisaptatyuttaraśatamākārāṇāṃ bhedā bhavanti / tathā hi - sarvajñatāyāḥ saptaviṃśatiḥ, mārgajñatāyāḥ ṣaṭtriṃśat, sarvākārajñatāyā daśottaraśatamiti trisaptatyuttaraśataṃ bhedāḥ /
children.translated_text: (b) Division (<s>bheda</s>). There are one hundred and seventy-three divisions of aspects. Namely: twenty-seven for omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), thirty-six for the knowledge of paths (<s>mārgajñatā</s>), and one hundred and ten for the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) — [totaling] one hundred and seventy-three divisions.

children.text: caturāryasatyeṣu prathamataḥ trayāṇāṃ satyānāṃ pratyekaṃ catvāra iti dvādaśa, mārgasatyasya caturthasya pañcadaśa ceti sarvajñatāyāḥ (vastujñatāyāḥ) saptaviṃśatirākārāḥ / tathā coktam abhisamayālaṅkāre -
children.translated_text: Of the four noble truths, first, four aspects each for the first three truths make twelve; and fifteen for the fourth, the truth of the path — [thus] twenty-seven aspects of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s> / <s>vastujñatā</s>). As stated in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>:

children.text: asadākāramārabhya yāvanniścalatākṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: Beginning with the aspect of non-existence (<s>asadākāra</s>), up to the aspect of immovability (<s>niścalatā</s>),

children.text: catvāraḥ pratisatyaṃ te mārge pañcadaśa smṛtāḥ //
children.translated_text: four per truth, and fifteen for the [truth of the] path are remembered. //

children.text: samudayasatyasya aṣṭau, mārgasatyasya sapta, duḥkhasatyasya pañca, nirodhasatyasya ṣoḍaśa ceti mārgajñatāyāḥ ṣaṭtriṃśad ākārā bhavanti / tathā coktam abhisamayālaṅkāre -
children.translated_text: Eight for the truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>), seven for the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>), five for the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>), and sixteen for the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>) — thus there are thirty-six aspects of the knowledge of paths (<s>mārgajñatā</s>). As stated in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>:

children.text: hetau mārge ca duḥkhe ca nirodhe ca yathākramam /
children.translated_text: In the [truth of] cause, in the [truth of] path, in the [truth of] suffering, and in the [truth of] cessation, in order,

children.text: aṣṭau te sapta pañceti ṣoḍaśeti ca kīrtitāḥ //
children.translated_text: they are proclaimed as eight, seven, five, and sixteen. //

children.text: śaikṣaśrāvakāṇāṃ saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣyā vastujñatāyā ākārāḥ, bodhisattvānāṃ mārgajñatāyāḥ catustriṃśat, buddhānāṃ sarvākārajñatāyā asādhāraṇā ekonacatvāriṃśacceti sarvākārajñatāyā daśottaraśatam ākārā bhavanti / tathā coktam abhisamayālaṅkāre -
children.translated_text: For trainee <s>śrāvakas</s>, the thirty-seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>) are the aspects of the knowledge of grounds (<s>vastujñatā</s>); for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, thirty-four [aspects] of the knowledge of paths (<s>mārgajñatā</s>); for <s>Buddhas</s>, thirty-nine uncommon [aspects] (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) of the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) — [thus] one hundred and ten aspects of the knowledge of all aspects. As stated in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>:

children.text: smṛtyupasthānamārabhya buddhatvākārapaścimāḥ /
children.translated_text: Beginning with the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), ending with the aspects of Buddhahood,

children.text: śiṣyāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ buddhānāṃ ca yathākramam //
children.translated_text: for disciples, for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and for <s>Buddhas</s> respectively, //

children.text: saptatriṃśaccatustriṃśattriśannava ca te matāḥ /
children.translated_text: they are considered to be thirty-seven, thirty-four, and thirty-nine;

children.text: trisarvajñatvabhedena mārgasatyānurodhataḥ //
children.translated_text: according to the division of the three omnisciences, in conformity with the truth of the path. //

children.text: jñānākārebhyaḥ pūrvam arthākārāḥ parijñātavyā iti prathamataḥ trisaptatyuttaraśatam arthākārā upadarśitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the aspects of meaning (<s>arthākāra</s>) should be understood before the aspects of knowledge (<s>jñānākāra</s>), the one hundred and seventy-three aspects of meaning are presented first.

children.text:
2. prayogāḥ
prayogāṇāṃ lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre catasṛbhiḥ kārikābhiḥ savistaraṃ suspaṣṭamupavarṇitam /
children.translated_text: 2. Applications (<s>prayoga</s>). All the characteristics and so forth of the applications are described fully and very clearly in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in four verses.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
jñātṛjñeyayoḥ vastumārgākārāṇāṃ ca śamathavipaśyanāyuganaddhabhāvanāsvarūpaṃ niḥsvabhāvatāniṣprapañcātmakaṃ jñānamevātra sākṣānnirdiṣṭasya prayogasya lakṣaṇamiti /
children.translated_text: (a) Definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>). The knowledge that is of the nature of the paired cultivation of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) (<s>yuganaddhabhāvanā</s>) regarding the aspects of grounds, paths, the knower, and the knowable — knowledge that is of the nature of essencelessness and freedom from conceptual elaboration (<s>niḥsvabhāvatāniṣprapañcātmaka</s>) — is the definition of the application directly indicated here.

children.text: athavā - trisarvajñatānāṃ yāvadākārāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāyuganaddhabhāvanāmayyā prajñayopāttaḥ sattvayoga evātra nirdiṣṭaprayogasya lakṣaṇam / yato hi 'kṛcchrāccireṇa prativodhataḥ ' ityanena nirdiṣṭaḥ sambhāramārgīyaḥ prayogo 'tra saṃgṛhīto bhavati /
children.translated_text: Alternatively: the being's yoga (<s>sattvayoga</s>), taken up by the wisdom born of the paired meditation of <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s> on the aspects up to all three omnisciences, is the definition of the application indicated here. For the application of the path of accumulation (<s>sambhāramārga</s>) indicated by 'with difficulty and over a long time he awakens' is included here.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
viṃśatiḥ prayogāṇāṃ bhedā bhavanti /
tatra svarūpataḥ pañca pramedāḥ, yathā - rūpādiṣu niḥsvabhāvatayā anavasthānaprayogaḥ, ayoga eva teṣu prayogo bhavatītyayogaprayogaḥ, rūpāditathatāgambhīratayā pratiṣṭhānānupalabdhyarthena sarvajñatādhikāre gambhīraprayogaḥ, rūpādiduravagāhatayā prakṛtyanāvilārthena mārgajñatādhikāre duravagāhaprayogaḥ, rūpādyapramāṇatayā paryantānupalambhārthena sarvākārajñatādhikāre apramāṇaprayoga iti /
children.translated_text: (b) Division (<s>bheda</s>). There are twenty divisions of applications. Among these, from the perspective of their nature, there are five types: (1) the application of non-abiding (<s>anavasthānaprayoga</s>) in form and the like through [their] essencelessness; (2) the application of non-application (<s>ayogaprayoga</s>), meaning that [true] application to them is precisely non-application; (3) the profound application (<s>gambhīraprayoga</s>), pertaining to the domain of omniscience, for the purpose of the non-apprehension of any basis due to the profundity of the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of form and the like; (4) the unfathomable application (<s>duravagāhaprayoga</s>), pertaining to the domain of path-knowledge, for the purpose of natural non-turbidity due to the unfathomability of form and the like; (5) the immeasurable application (<s>apramāṇaprayoga</s>), pertaining to the domain of the knowledge of all aspects, for the purpose of the non-apprehension of any limit due to the immeasurability of form and the like.

children.text: pudgalāśrayadṛṣṭyā aṣṭau prayogāḥ / tathā hi - gambhīraśūnyatāyāmuttrasanajātīyasyādikarmikasya kṛcchacirābhisambodhaprayogaḥ, prayogamārgīyoṣmābhisamayādārabhya gambhīradharmatāyāmuttrāso na bhavati, na ca svapne 'pi ṣaṭpāramitācaryāsu dūrībhāva iti vyākaraṇalābhaprayogaḥ, mūrdhābhisamayādārabhya dharmatādhigamaviṣayakeṇa cirābhyāsena avinivartanīyaprayogaḥ, kṣāntimārabhya upāyakauśalena dharmatādhigamadṛḍhatayā śrāvakapratyekabuddhantarāyikadharmavarjanāt niryāṇaprayogaḥ, agradharmābhisamayamārabhya stambādyanupalambhāt mahāsamudrasyābhyāsannatvamiva satatabhāvanādipratipattyā nirantaraprayogabalena dharmaṃdhātoḥ sākṣāddarśanasyābhyāsannatvaniścaya iti nirantaraprayogaḥ, sarvajñatāhetūnāṃ abhinavānāsravadharmāṇāmādhāratvapratipatterāsannābhisambodhaprayogaḥ, kṣipraṃ dharmaṃkāyaphalābhinirvartanāt kṣiprābhisambodhaprayogaḥ, dharmacakrapravartanādikaṃ parārthaprayoga iti /
children.translated_text: From the perspective of persons, there are eight applications. Namely: (1) the application of difficult and prolonged awakening (<s>kṛcchracirābhisambodhaprayoga</s>) of the beginner (<s>ādikarmika</s>) who is of the type that is frightened by the profound emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>); (2) the application of receiving prediction (<s>vyākaraṇalābhaprayoga</s>), from the heat stage (<s>uṣmābhisamaya</s>) of the preparatory path, where there is no longer fear regarding the profound <s>dharmatā</s>, and even in dreams one does not depart from the practice of the six <s>pāramitās</s>; (3) the irreversible application (<s>avinivartanīyaprayoga</s>), from the peak stage (<s>mūrdhābhisamaya</s>), through long practice in the domain of the realization of <s>dharmatā</s>; (4) the application of deliverance (<s>niryāṇaprayoga</s>), from the patience stage (<s>kṣānti</s>), through skillful means and firmness of the realization of <s>dharmatā</s>, avoiding the hindering <s>dharmas</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>; (5) the uninterrupted application (<s>nirantaraprayoga</s>), from the supreme mundane quality stage (<s>agradharmābhisamaya</s>), through the non-apprehension of obstructions and the like, with the certainty that the direct seeing of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is near through continuous application — like approaching a great ocean through constant practice; (6) the application close to awakening (<s>āsannābhisambodhaprayoga</s>), through the realization of being the foundation of fresh uncontaminated <s>dharmas</s> that are the causes of omniscience; (7) the application of swift awakening (<s>kṣiprābhisambodhaprayoga</s>), through quickly producing the fruit of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>; (8) the application of others' benefit (<s>parārthaprayoga</s>), such as turning the wheel of the <s>Dharma</s> and the like.

children.text: prajñāpāramitābhāvanāpāripūryupāyadṛṣṭyā catvāraḥ prayogāḥ / tadyathā paramārthato guṇadoṣāṇāṃ vṛddhiparihāṇyadarśanena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caraṇānujñānāt avṛddhyaparihāṇiprayogaḥ, paramārthato dharmādharmāderanupalambhapratipattyā dharmādharmādyanupalambhaprayogaḥ, dharmadhāturūpatvena rūpādyacintyamiti acintyaprayogaḥ, dharmadhāturūpatvāt rūpāditannimittatatsvabhāvādiṣu vikalpābhāvād avikalpaprayoga iti /
children.translated_text: From the perspective of methods for completing the cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, there are four applications: (1) the application of non-increase and non-decrease (<s>avṛddhyaparihāṇiprayoga</s>), through the permission to practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> by the view that ultimately there is no increase or decrease of qualities and faults; (2) the application of non-apprehension of <s>dharma</s> and non-<s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmādharmādyanupalambhaprayoga</s>), through the practice of non-apprehension of <s>dharma</s>, non-<s>dharma</s>, and the like, ultimately; (3) the inconceivable application (<s>acintyaprayoga</s>), because form and the like, being of the nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, are inconceivable; (4) the application of non-conceptualization (<s>avikalpaprayoga</s>), because form and the like, being of the nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, are free from conceptual elaboration regarding their signs, their nature, and so forth.

children.text: prayogaphaladṛṣṭyā dvau prayogau / tathā hi - srota-āpattyādyanuttarasamyaksambodhiphalaratnapradāyakatvāt phalaratnadānaprayogaḥ, kleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇahetutvena viśuddhiprayoga iti dvau /
children.translated_text: From the perspective of the fruit of application, there are two applications: (1) the application of giving the jewel of fruit (<s>phalaratnadānaprayoga</s>), because it bestows the fruit-jewels of stream-entry and so forth up to unsurpassed perfect awakening; (2) the application of purification (<s>viśuddhiprayoga</s>), because it is the cause for the abandonment of the afflictive and cognitive obscurations (<s>kleśajñeyāvaraṇa</s>).

children.text: kṣiprabhāvanādṛṣṭyā ekaḥ prayogaḥ, yathā dharmataiṣā yasmānmahāratnānāṃ bahavo 'ntarāyāḥ sambhavanti, tasmāt paramaratnasvabhāvāyā mātuḥ saṃvatsareṇa bahvantarāyatve 'pi likhanaṃ śīghrameveti avadhiprayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: From the perspective of swift cultivation, there is one application: the limit-application (<s>avadhiprayoga</s>) — since many obstacles arise for great jewels, the writing of the mother [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>], whose nature is the supreme jewel, should be done swiftly even though there are many obstacles within a year; such is the nature of the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text:
3. guṇāḥ
guṇānāṃ lakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre kārikārdhenopadarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: 3. Qualities (<s>guṇa</s>). All the characteristics and so forth of the qualities are shown in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in half a verse. Namely:

children.text: mārāṇāṃ śaktihānyādiścaturdaśavidho guṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: the destruction of the power of <s>Māras</s> and the rest — [these are] the fourteen qualities.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
prayogāṇāṃ bhāvanābalena adhigataprāśastyaṃ guṇānāṃ lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of qualities is: the excellence attained through the power of the meditation on the practices.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
guṇānāṃ caturdaśa bhedā bhavanti / tathā hi - pāramitāyāṃ udgṛhyamāṇāyāṃ mārakṛtavighnāḥ tathāgatānubhāvena vyāhanyanta iti māraśaktivyāghātaguṇaḥ, prayogamaulapṛṣṭhāvasthāsu tathāgatasamanvāharaṇalābhāt buddhasamanvāhārajñātatvaguṇaḥ, tathāgatajñānadarśanalābhāt buddhapratyakṣīkaraṇaguṇaḥ, tathāgatānāṃ samīpībhavanalābhena samyaksambodhyāsannībhāvaguṇaḥ, mahānuśaṃsalābhāt mahārthatādiguṇaḥ, tathāgatakṛtyakaraṇād deśanirūpaṇāguṇalābhena deśanirūpaṇaguṇaḥ, pratipakṣadharmaparipūraṇalābhāt sarvānāsravadharmaparipūriguṇaḥ, sarvākārajñatākathākathanalābhena kathāpuruṣatāguṇaḥ, tathāgatasānāthyakaraṇalābhena abhedyatāguṇaḥ, mahodāraprītisampādanāt asādhāraṇakuśalamūlotpattiguṇaḥ, pratijñānumodanalābhe kramaṇa prayogābhyāsāt pratijñāyāthārthyasampādanaguṇaḥ, gambhīrodārārthādhimokṣeṇa udāraphalaparigrahaṇaguṇaḥ, satvārthakaraṇasāmarthyalābhena sattvārthapratipattiguṇaḥ, avikalaprajñāpāramitāprāpakakuśalamūlasamanvāgame prayogābhyāsena niyatilābhaguṇaśceti caturdaśa guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are fourteen divisions of qualities. Namely: the quality of destroying <s>Māra</s>'s power — because when the <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) is being taken up, the obstacles created by <s>Māra</s> are repelled through the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; the quality of being known through the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s sustained attention — because of obtaining the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s sustained attention during the stages of preparation, main practice, and subsequent [practice]; the quality of direct perception of the <s>Buddha</s> — because of obtaining the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s vision of knowledge; the quality of proximity to perfect complete awakening (<s>samyaksambodhi</s>) — because of obtaining nearness to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>; the quality of great purpose and the like — because of obtaining great benefit; the quality of delineation of regions — because of obtaining the quality of delineation of regions through performing the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s function; the quality of completing all uncontaminated <s>dharmas</s> — because of obtaining the completion of the antidote <s>dharmas</s>; the quality of being a speaker of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects) — because of obtaining the ability to discourse on <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>; the quality of indestructibility — because of obtaining the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s protection; the quality of arising of uncommon roots of merit — because of accomplishing a great and magnificent joy; the quality of accomplishing the truthfulness of one's pledges — because of practice and habituation in sequence upon obtaining the approval of one's pledges; the quality of receiving magnificent fruit — because of conviction in the profound and magnificent meaning; the quality of practice for the benefit of beings — because of obtaining the capacity for accomplishing the welfare of beings; and the quality of obtaining certainty (<s>niyati</s>) — through practice and habituation when one possesses the roots of merit that lead to the unimpaired <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — thus there are fourteen qualities.

children.text:
4. doṣāḥ
prayogāṇāṃ doṣā abhisamayālaṅkāre kārikārdhena upadarśitāḥ / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
4. Faults
The faults of the practices are displayed in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through half a verse. Namely:

children.text: doṣāśca ṣaḍ viboddhavyāścaturbhirdaśakaiḥ saha //
children.translated_text: And the faults should be understood as six [groups] together with four sets of ten.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
prayogotpattisthitiprakarṣagatīnāmantarāyakarā vighnā eva doṣā iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of faults is: those obstacles that hinder the arising, stability, culmination, and progress of the practices.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
ṣaṭcatvāriṃśad doṣāṇāṃ bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are forty-six divisions of faults.

children.text: prathamaṃ daśakam /
children.translated_text: The first set of ten:

children.text: kṛcchraprāptiḥ (cireṇa mātari pratibhānam), atyāśupratibhānatā, kāyadauṣṭhulyam, cittadauṣṭhulyam, ayogavihitasvādhyāyāditā, vaimukhyanimittagrāhitā, hetubhraṃśaḥ, praṇītāsvādabhraṃśaḥ, uttamayānabhraṃśaḥ, uddeśabhraṃśaśceti daśa /
children.translated_text: Difficulty of attainment (slow cognition of the Mother [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]), excessive quickness of cognition, bodily unfitness (<s>kāyadauṣṭhulya</s>), mental unfitness (<s>cittadauṣṭhulya</s>), engaging in improper recitation and study and the like, grasping signs of aversion (<s>vaimukhya</s>), loss of the cause, loss of the taste of the sublime, loss of the supreme vehicle, and loss of the purpose — these are ten.

children.text:
dvitīya daśakam
hetuphalasambandhabhraṃśaḥ, niruttarasthānabhraśaḥ, bahuvidhaviṣayavikalpapratibhānotpādaḥ, akṣaralikhanābhiniveśaḥ, abhāvābhiniveśaḥ, akṣarābhiniveśaḥ, anakṣarābhiniveśaḥ, janapadādimanaskāraḥ, lābhasatkāraślokāsvādanam, amārgopāyakauśalamārgaṇañceti daśa /
children.translated_text:
The second set of ten:
Loss of the connection between cause and effect, loss of the unsurpassed station, arising of cognition with manifold object-conceptualization, clinging to the writing of syllables, clinging to non-existence, clinging to syllables, clinging to non-syllables, mental attention to regions and the like, savoring gain, honor, and fame, and seeking the path of non-means as if it were skillful means — these are ten.

children.text: amī viśatiḥ doṣāḥ pāramitāyāṃ pravṛttasya yogino 'ntarāyakarāḥ pratipāditāḥ / samprati punaḥ pravṛttipūrvikā visāmagrī nirucyate /
children.translated_text: These twenty faults are set forth as obstacles for the <s>yogin</s> (practitioner) who is engaged in the <s>pāramitā</s>. Now, furthermore, the disharmony that precedes engagement is explained.

children.text:
tṛtīyaṃ daśakam
chandakilāsavaidhuryam (ayaṃ hi śrotāvaktroḥ doṣaḥ), chandaviṣayabhedavaidhuryam (ayamapi tathā), alpecchatānalpecchatāvaidhuryam, dhūtaguṇayogāyogau, kalyāṇākalyāṇadharmatvam, tyāgamātsaryam, dānāgrahaṇam, uddhaṭitajñavipañcitajñatvam, sūtrādidharmābhijñānabhijñatvam, ṣaṭpāramitāsamanvāgamāsamanvāgamāviti daśa /
children.translated_text:
The third set of ten:
Disparity of desire and laziness (this is a fault of both the listener and the speaker), disparity of the objects of desire (this too is likewise), the disparity of having and not having few desires, the possession or non-possession of ascetic qualities (<s>dhūtaguṇa</s>), having wholesome or unwholesome <s>dharma</s>-nature, generosity and miserliness, giving and non-acceptance, being one with superficial knowledge versus one with discerning knowledge, knowledge or non-knowledge of the <s>Dharma</s> of <s>sūtras</s> and the like, and being endowed or not endowed with the six <s>pāramitās</s> — these are ten.

children.text:
caturthaṃ daśakam
upāyakauśalānupāyakauśale, dhāraṇīpratilambhāpratilambhau, likhitukāmatā 'likhitukāmate, vigatāvigatakāmādichandattve ceti catvāri; upāyagativaimukhyam, sugatigamanasaumanasyamiti dve: śrotāvaktroḥ kasyacid ekākiparṣadabhiratiḥ, anubandhakāmānavakāśadānatvam, āmiṣakiñcitkābhilāṣatadadātukāmatā, jīvitāntarāyānantarāyadiggamanamiti catvāri ceti daśa /
children.translated_text:
The fourth set of ten:
Skill and non-skill in means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>), obtaining and not obtaining <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention), the desire and non-desire to write, and the possession and non-possession of desire for sensual pleasures and the like — [these are] four; aversion to the path of skillful means and delight in going to happy rebirths — [these are] two; on the part of either the listener or the speaker, delight in being alone in the assembly, giving opportunity to followers, craving for material things and trifles and the desire to give them, and going in the direction of dangers to life and other dangers — [these are] four; thus [in total] ten.

children.text:
avaśiṣṭadoṣaṣaṭkam
durbhikṣadiggamanāgamanam, caurādyākulitadiggamanāgamanam, kulāvalokanadaurmanasyamiti trīṇi, mārabhedaprayogaḥ, prativarṇikopasaṃhāraḥ (kṛtrimapratipādanam), ayathāviṣayaspṛhotpādanamityaparāṇi trīṇi ceti ṣaṭ / ityevaṃ ṣaṭcatvāriṃśad doṣā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
The remaining group of six faults:
Going to and coming from regions of famine, going to and coming from regions beset by thieves and the like, mental distress from examining families — these are three; the stratagem of <s>Māra</s>'s splitting [the community], approaching the counterfeit (false instruction), and the arising of desire for inappropriate objects — these are another three; thus there are six. In this way, there are forty-six faults.

children.text:
5. lakṣaṇāni saṃkṣepeṇa
lakṣaṇasya pratipādanam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā kṛtam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
5. Characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), in brief
The presentation of characteristics is made in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through a single verse. Namely:

children.text: lakṣyate yena tajjñeyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ trividhaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: That by which [the practice] is characterized should be known as the characteristic; and that is threefold:

children.text: jñānaṃ viśeṣaḥ kāritraṃ svabhāvo yaśca lakṣyate //
children.translated_text: knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>), function (<s>kāritra</s>), and essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) — which is characterized [by these].

children.text: vistareṇa tu lakṣaṇānāṃ pratipādanam abhisamayālaṅkāre aṣṭādaśabhiḥ kārikabhiḥ samyag vihitam /
children.translated_text: In detail, however, the presentation of characteristics is properly carried out in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through eighteen verses.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
svaśaktyā prayogasvarūpasyopalakṣakaḥ sattvayogo mārgaṃpāramitāprayogalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of the characteristic of the <s>mārgapāramitā</s> (perfection of the path) practice is: a mental engagement of a continuum (<s>sattvayoga</s>) that, by its own power, characterizes the essential nature of the practice.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
prayogāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ karaṇasādhanaparigraheṇa jñāna-viśeṣa-kāritrasvarūpam, karmasādhanaparigraheṇa svabhāvātmakamiti lakṣaṇaṃ caturvidhaṃ boddhavyam /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
The characteristic of the practices should be understood as fourfold: having the nature of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>), and function (<s>kāritra</s>) — through the inclusion of the instrument [of accomplishment]; and having the nature of essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) — through the inclusion of the action [of accomplishment].

children.text: tatra jñānalakṣaṇāni aṣṭacatvāriṃśat, viśeṣalakṣaṇāni ṣoḍaśa, kāritralakṣaṇāni ekādaśa svabhāvalakṣaṇāni ṣoḍaśa ceti lakṣaṇānāṃ bhedā vistareṇa ekanavatiḥ bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Therein, there are forty-eight knowledge-characteristics, sixteen distinction-characteristics, eleven function-characteristics, and sixteen essential-nature-characteristics — thus in detail, the divisions of characteristics number ninety-one.

children.text:
(a) jñānalakṣaṇāni aṣṭacatvāriṃśad
jñanalakṣaṇānāṃ sarveṣāṃ vistareṇa pratipādanam abhisamayālaṅkāre navabhiḥ kārikābhiḥ suspaṣṭaṃ vihitam /
children.translated_text:
(a) The forty-eight knowledge-characteristics
The complete detailed presentation of all knowledge-characteristics is clearly set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through nine verses.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
mahākaruṇāśūnyatāvalambitaprajñāviśiṣṭenopāyakauśalenopāttaḥ sattvayogo lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition is: a mental engagement of a continuum taken up by skillful means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>), distinguished by wisdom that relies on great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) and emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>).

children.text: kleśaliṅgādayo vakṣyamāṇāḥ svabhāvā eva eteṣāṃ upalakṣakāḥ /
children.translated_text: The forthcoming natures beginning with the sign of affliction (<s>kleśaliṅga</s>) and so on are the characterizers of these.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
aṣṭacatvāriṃśad jñānalakṣaṇānyapi triṣu vyākhyātāni / tathā hi - sarvajñatāsaṃgṛhītāni jñānalakṣaṇāni ṣoḍaśa, mārgajñatāsaṃgṛhītāni jñānalakṣaṇāni ṣoḍaśa, sarvākārajñatāsaṃgṛhītāni jñānalakṣaṇāni ṣoḍaśa ceti tridhā bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
The forty-eight knowledge-characteristics are also explained under three [categories]. Namely: sixteen knowledge-characteristics comprised within <s>sarvajñatā</s> (knowledge of all [bases]), sixteen knowledge-characteristics comprised within <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the paths), and sixteen knowledge-characteristics comprised within <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects) — thus the division is threefold.

children.text: sarvajñatāsaṃgṛhītāni jñānalakṣaṇāni ṣoḍaśa
children.translated_text: The sixteen knowledge-characteristics comprised within <s>sarvajñatā</s>:

children.text: tathāgatanirvṛttijñānam, lokālujyatājñānam, sarvasattvacittacaritajñānam, ciattasaṃkṣepajñānam, cittavikṣepajñānam, cittākṣayākārajñānam, sarāgādicittajñānam, vigatarāgādicittajñānam, vipulacittajñānam, mahadgatacittajñānam apramāṇacittajñānam, anidarśanacittajñānam adṛśyacittajñānam, cittonmiñjitādijñānam, unmiñjitāditathatākārajñānam, tathāgatatathatāvabodhatatparasamākhyānaprajñapanajñānaṃ ceti ṣoḍaśa / tathoktam abhisamayālaṅkāre -
children.translated_text: Knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation), knowledge of the world's unshakability, knowledge of the mental conduct of all beings, knowledge of the contraction of mind, knowledge of the distraction of mind, knowledge of the inexhaustible aspect of mind, knowledge of mind with attachment (<s>sarāga</s>) and the like, knowledge of mind free from attachment (<s>vigatarāga</s>) and the like, knowledge of the vast mind, knowledge of the great mind, knowledge of the immeasurable mind, knowledge of the invisible (<s>anidarśana</s>) mind, knowledge of the unseen (<s>adṛśya</s>) mind, knowledge of the opening and the like of the mind, knowledge of the suchness-aspect (<s>tathatākāra</s>) of the opening and the like, and knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s awakening to suchness and the explanation thereof to others — these are sixteen. As stated in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>:

children.text: tathāgatasya nirvṛtau loke cālujyanātmake /
children.translated_text: Regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s cessation (<s>nirvṛti</s>) and the world's unshakable nature,

children.text: sattvānāṃ cittacaryāsu tatsaṃkṣepe bahirgatau //
children.translated_text: the mental conduct of beings, its contraction, and its outward going,

children.text: akṣayākāratāyāṃ ca sarāgādau pravistṛte /
children.translated_text: the inexhaustible aspect, [mind] with attachment and the like, the vast,

children.text: mahadgate 'pramāṇe ca vijñāne cānidarśane //
children.translated_text: the great, the immeasurable, and consciousness that is invisible (<s>anidarśana</s>),

children.text: adṛśyacittajñāne ca tadunmiñjādisaṃjñakam /
children.translated_text: and knowledge of the unseen mind, and that called 'the opening of that' and the like,

children.text: punastathattākāreṇa te ṣāṃ jñānamattaḥ param //
children.translated_text: again with the aspect of suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), the knowledge of them beyond that,

children.text: tathatāyāṃ munerbodhatatparākhyānamityayam /
children.translated_text: the awakening of the Sage to suchness and the explanation thereof to others —

children.text: sarvajñatādhikāreṇa jñānalakṣaṇasaṃgrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: this is the collection of knowledge-characteristics under the heading of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (knowledge of all [bases]).

children.text: mārgajñatāsaṃgṛhītāni jñānalakṣaṇāni ṣoḍaśa
children.translated_text: The sixteen knowledge-characteristics comprised within <s>mārgajñatā</s>:

children.text: śūnyatājñānam, animittajñānam, apraṇihitajñānam, paramārthato 'nutpādajñānam, anirodhajñānam, ādiśabdenāsaṃkleśajñānam, avyavadānajñānam, abhāvajñānam, svabhāvajñānam, aniśritajñānam, ākāśalakṣaṇajñānamiti ṣaṭ saṃgṛhīttāni; dharmatā 'vikopanajñānam, asaṃskārajñānam, avikalpajñānam, prabhedajñānam, alakṣaṇajñānamiti ṣoḍaśa / tathā coktam abhisamayālaṅkāre -
children.translated_text: Knowledge of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), knowledge of the signless (<s>animitta</s>), knowledge of the wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>), knowledge of non-origination (<s>anutpāda</s>) ultimately, knowledge of non-cessation (<s>anirodha</s>), knowledge of non-affliction (<s>asaṃkleśa</s>) by way of the word 'ādi' (and so forth), knowledge of non-purification (<s>avyavadāna</s>), knowledge of non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>), knowledge of own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), knowledge of the unsupported (<s>aniśrita</s>), knowledge of the nature of space (<s>ākāśalakṣaṇa</s>) — six thus included; knowledge of the inviolability of <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality), knowledge of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskāra</s>), knowledge of the non-conceptual (<s>avikalpa</s>), knowledge of distinction (<s>prabheda</s>), and knowledge of the characteristicless (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>) — these are sixteen. As stated in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>:

children.text: śūnyatve sānimitte ca praṇidhānavivarjite /
children.translated_text: Regarding emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), the signless (<s>animitta</s>), and that devoid of aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>),

children.text: anutpādānirodhādau dharmatāyā akopane //
children.translated_text: non-origination (<s>anutpāda</s>), non-cessation (<s>anirodha</s>), and the rest, and the inviolability of <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality),

children.text: asaṃskāre 'vikalpe ca prabhedālakṣaṇatvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskāra</s>), the non-conceptual (<s>avikalpa</s>), and in [the pair of] distinction (<s>prabheda</s>) and characteristiclessness (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>) —

children.text: mārgajñatādhikāreṇa jñānalakṣaṇamiṣyate //
children.translated_text: under the heading of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the paths), the knowledge-characteristic is held [to be thus].

children.text: sarvākārajñatāsaṃgṛhītāni jñānalakṣaṇāni ṣoḍaśa
children.translated_text: The sixteen knowledge-characteristics comprised within <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects):

children.text: tathāgatasvadharmopaniśrayavihārajñānam, satkārajñānam, gurukārajñānam, mānanājñānam, pūjanājñānam, paramārthato 'kṛtakajñānam, sarvatragajñānam, adṛṣṭārthadarśakajñānam, lokaśūnyatākārajñānam, lokaśūnyatāsūcakajñānam, lokaśūnyatājñāpakajñānam, lokaśūnyatādarśakajñānam, paramārthato 'cintyatādeśanājñānam, paramārthataprapañcaśāntatājñānam, svabhāvasiddhalokanirodhajñānam, lokasaṃjñānirodhajñānamiti ṣoḍaśa / tathā coktam abhisamayālaṅkāre -
children.translated_text: The knowledge of dwelling in reliance upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s own <s>dharma</s>, the knowledge of honor (<s>satkāra</s>), the knowledge of respect (<s>gurukāra</s>), the knowledge of reverence (<s>mānanā</s>), the knowledge of worship (<s>pūjanā</s>), the knowledge of the uncreated in the ultimate sense, the knowledge that pervades everything, the knowledge that reveals unseen meanings, the knowledge of the aspect of the emptiness of the world, the knowledge that indicates the emptiness of the world, the knowledge that makes known the emptiness of the world, the knowledge that shows the emptiness of the world, the knowledge that teaches inconceivability in the ultimate sense, the knowledge of the quiescence of conceptual proliferation in the ultimate sense, the knowledge of the cessation of the world established by its own nature, and the knowledge of the cessation of worldly designations — [these are] sixteen. As stated in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>:

children.text: svadharmamupaniśritya vihāre tasya sakṛtau /
children.translated_text: In reliance upon one's own <s>dharma</s>, in dwelling therein, in honor,

children.text: gurutve mānanāyāṃ ca tatpūjā 'kṛtakatvayoḥ //
children.translated_text: in respect, in reverence, and in worship and uncreatedness,

children.text: sarvatra vṛttimajjñānamadṛṣṭasya ca darśakam /
children.translated_text: the knowledge that operates everywhere, and that which reveals the unseen,

children.text: lokasya śūnyatākārasūcakajñāpakākṣagam //
children.translated_text: that which indicates, makes known, and perceives the aspect of the emptiness of the world,

children.text: acintyaśāntatādarśi lokasaṃjñānirodhi ca /
children.translated_text: that which sees inconceivability and quiescence, and that which brings about the cessation of worldly designations —

children.text: jñānalakṣaṇamityuktaṃ sarvākārajñātānaye //
children.translated_text: this is declared to be the characteristic of knowledge according to the system of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects).

children.text: (ā) viśeṣalakṣaṇāni ṣoḍaśa
children.translated_text: (D) The sixteen special characteristics (<s>viśeṣalakṣaṇa</s>)

children.text: viśeṣalakṣaṇānāṃ ṣoḍaśānāṃ lakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre samyagupadarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: The definition and so forth of the sixteen special characteristics are all properly displayed in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Namely:

children.text: acintyādiviśeṣeṇa viśiṣṭaiḥ satyagocaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Distinguished by the special qualities of inconceivability and so on, with truth as their domain,

children.text: viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ ṣaḍbhirdaśabhiścoditaṃ kṣaṇaiḥ //
children.translated_text: the special characteristic is set forth through six and ten moments.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
acintyādiviśeṣaṇairviśiṣṭaṃ sattvajñānaṃ prayogāṇāṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The knowledge of a continuum distinguished by the special qualities of inconceivability and so on is the special characteristic of the practices.

children.text: athavā - hainayānikaprayogebhyo bodhisattvaprayogāṇāṃ vaiśiṣṭyamupalakṣayantīti viśeṣalakṣaṇāni / kleśaliṅgādayaḥ ṣoḍaśa svabhāvā eteṣāṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇānāmupalakṣakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively: they are called special characteristics because they characterize the distinction (<s>vaiśiṣṭya</s>) of <s>bodhisattva</s> practices from <s>Hīnayāna</s> practices. The sixteen natures beginning with separation from the signs of afflictions are the markers of these special characteristics.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
māhāyānīyadarśanamārgīyakṣāntijñānakṣaṇāni ṣoḍhaśa śrāvakapratyekabuddhadarśanamārgasambaddhakṣāntijñānakṣaṇebhyo viśiṣṭatarāṇīti ṣoḍaśa bhedā bhavanti / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
The sixteen <s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) moments of the Mahāyāna path of seeing are superior to the acceptance and knowledge moments associated with the paths of seeing of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> — thus there are sixteen divisions. Namely:

children.text: duḥkhasatyālambanāni catuḥkṣaṇasaṃgṛhītāni kṣāntijñānāni kramaśaḥ acintyaviśeṣaḥ atulyaviśeṣaḥ, aprameyaviśeṣaḥ, asaṃkhyeyaviśeṣaśceti catvāro bhedāḥ /
children.translated_text: The acceptances and knowledges taking suffering-truth (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>) as their object, comprised within four moments, are respectively: the distinction of inconceivability (<s>acintya</s>), the distinction of incomparability (<s>atulya</s>), the distinction of immeasurability (<s>aprameya</s>), and the distinction of innumerability (<s>asaṃkhyeya</s>) — thus four divisions.

children.text: samudayasatyālambanāni catuḥkṣaṇasaṃgṛhītāni kṣāntijñānāni yathākramaṃ sarvāryapudgalasaṃgrahaviśeṣaḥ, puruṣaviśeṣavedanīyatāviśeṣaḥ śrāvakādyasādhāratāviśeṣaḥ, śrāvakādibhyaḥ kṣiprābhijñatāviśeṣaśceti catvāro bhedāḥ /
children.translated_text: The acceptances and knowledges taking origination-truth (<s>samudayasatya</s>) as their object, comprised within four moments, are respectively: the distinction of including all noble persons, the distinction of being experienced by [only] special persons, the distinction of being uncommon to <s>śrāvakas</s> and others, and the distinction of swifter realization than <s>śrāvakas</s> and others — thus four divisions.

children.text: nirodhasatyālambanāni catuḥkṣaṇasaṃgṛhītāni kṣāntijñānāni yathākramaṃ anyūnāpūrṇatāviśeṣaḥ, tīvrapratipattiviśeṣaḥ, samudāgamaviśeṣaḥ, ālambanaviśeṣaśceti catvāro bhedāḥ /
children.translated_text: The acceptances and knowledges taking cessation-truth (<s>nirodhasatya</s>) as their object, comprised within four moments, are respectively: the distinction of being neither deficient nor excessive, the distinction of intense practice, the distinction of attainment (<s>samudāgama</s>), and the distinction of object (<s>ālambana</s>) — thus four divisions.

children.text: mārgasatyālambanāni catuḥkṣaṇasaṃgṛhītāni kṣāntijñānāni yathākramaṃ ādhāraviśeṣaḥ, sākalyaviśeṣaḥ, samparigrahaviśeṣaḥ, anāsvādaviśeṣaśceti catvāro bhedāḥ /
children.translated_text: The acceptances and knowledges taking path-truth (<s>mārgasatya</s>) as their object, comprised within four moments, are respectively: the distinction of basis (<s>ādhāra</s>), the distinction of completeness (<s>sākalya</s>), the distinction of embracing (<s>samparigraha</s>), and the distinction of non-relishing (<s>anāsvāda</s>) — thus four divisions.

children.text: iti ṣoḍaśātmakaḥ duḥkhādisatyakṣaṇānāṃ viśeṣaḥ, yena śrāvakādimārgebhyo bodhisattvādīnāṃ mārgajñatādidvaye viśeṣamārgo viśiṣyate / tathā coktam abhisamayālaṅkāre -
children.translated_text: Thus the sixteenfold distinction of the moments of the truths beginning with suffering — by which the path of distinction of <s>bodhisattvas</s> and others is distinguished from the paths of <s>śrāvakas</s> and others in the two [knowledges] of <s>mārgajñatā</s> and so on. As stated in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>:

children.text: acintyātulyate meyasaṃkhyayoḥ samatikramau /
children.translated_text: Transcendence of inconceivability and incomparability, of the measurable and the numerable,

children.text: sarvāryasaṃgraho vijñavedyāsādhāraṇajñate //
children.translated_text: inclusion of all noble ones, being experienced by the wise, uncommonness, and the [swift] knowledge,

children.text: kṣiprajñānyūnapūrṇatve pratipatsamudāgamau /
children.translated_text: swiftness of knowledge, neither deficiency nor excess, practice and attainment,

children.text: ālambanaṃ ca sādhāraṃ sākalyaṃ samparigrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: object, commonality, completeness, embracing,

children.text: anāsvādaśca vijñeyo viśeṣaḥ ṣoḍaśātmakaḥ /
children.translated_text: and non-relishing — the sixteenfold distinction should be known,

children.text: viśeṣamārgo mārgebhyo yenānyebhyo viśiṣyate //
children.translated_text: the path of distinction by which [this path] is distinguished from other paths.

children.text: (i) kāritralakṣaṇāni ekādaśa
children.translated_text: (E) The eleven activity-characteristics (<s>kāritralakṣaṇa</s>)

children.text: kāritrāṇāṃ lakṣaṇādikaṃ abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kārikābhyāṃ samyagāveditam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: The definition and so forth of activities are properly made known in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through two verses. Namely:

children.text: hitaṃ sukhaṃ ca trāṇaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ layanaṃ nṛṇām /
children.translated_text: Benefit, happiness, protection, refuge, shelter for beings,

children.text: parāyaṇaṃ ca dvīpaṃ ca pariṇāyakasaṃjñakam //
children.translated_text: final resort, island, and that called 'leader' (<s>pariṇāyaka</s>),

children.text: anābhogaṃ tribhiryānaiḥ phalāsākṣātkriyātmakam /
children.translated_text: effortless, having the nature of the actualization of the fruit through the three vehicles,

children.text: paścimaṃ gatikāritramidaṃ kāritralakṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: and the final one — this is the activity-characteristic pertaining to destiny (<s>gati</s>).

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
hitasukhatrāṇādiprativiśiṣṭajñānaiḥ sattvaprayogāḥ parārthasampādanasādhanaiḥ yojyanta iti tāni kāritralakṣaṇānyucyante / kleśaliṅgādayaḥ ṣoḍaśa svabhāvāḥ kāritrāṇāmupalakṣakā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The practices for sentient beings, which are to be conjoined with the means of accomplishing others' welfare through knowledges distinguished by benefit, happiness, protection, and so on — these are called activity-characteristics. The sixteen natures beginning with separation from the signs of afflictions are the markers of activities.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
kāritrāṇāṃ ekādaśa bhedā bhavanti / tatra sarvajñatāyāḥ trīṇi, mārgajñatāyāḥ sapta, sarvākārajñatāyā ekamiti ekādaśa kāritrāṇi bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are eleven divisions of activities. Among these, three pertain to <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), seven to <s>mārgajñatā</s> (path-knowledge), and one to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) — thus eleven activities.

children.text: sarvajñatākāritrāṇi trīṇi
children.translated_text: Three activities of <s>sarvajñatā</s>:

children.text: sarvasattvānāṃ anāgatamokṣasukhopasaṃhārārthena hitakāritram, lokasya duḥkhadaurmanasyādīni prahāya aihikasukhopasaṃhāreṇa sukhakāritram, duḥkharahitāvipākadharmatāyāṃ sthāpanāt trāṇakāritramiti trīṇi /
children.translated_text: The activity of benefit, for the purpose of bringing future liberation and happiness to all sentient beings; the activity of happiness, through bringing happiness in this life by removing the sufferings and mental distresses of the world; and the activity of protection, through establishing [beings] in the state of dharmatā whose fruition is free from suffering — thus three.

children.text: mārgajñatākāritrāṇi sapta
children.translated_text: Seven activities of <s>mārgajñatā</s>:

children.text: ātyantikahitopasaṃhārārthena śaraṇakāritram, duḥkhahetunivartanārthena layanakāritram, saṃsāranirvāṇasamatopasampādanārthena parāyaṇakāritram, svaparārthādhigamādhārabhāvopasaṃhārāt dvīpakāritram, parārthapratipattyupasaṃhārāt pariṇāyakakāritram, anābhogapravṛttasattvārthopasaṃhārāt anābhogakāritram, yānatrayaniryāṇattatphalāsākṣātkaraṇakāritramiti sapta /
children.translated_text: The activity of refuge, for the purpose of bringing ultimate benefit; the activity of shelter (<s>layana</s>), for the purpose of averting the causes of suffering; the activity of final resort (<s>parāyaṇa</s>), for the purpose of bringing about the equality of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>; the activity of island (<s>dvīpa</s>), through bringing about the state of being a basis for the attainment of one's own and others' welfare; the activity of leadership (<s>pariṇāyaka</s>), through bringing about the practice for others' welfare; the activity of effortlessness (<s>anābhoga</s>), through accomplishing the welfare of sentient beings without deliberate effort; and the activity of actualizing the fruit of emergence through the three vehicles — thus seven.

children.text: sarvākārajñatākāritram ekam
children.translated_text: One activity of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>:

children.text: sarvākārajñatayā sarvadharmadaiśikatvena sarvākārajñatāyā ekameva gatikāritram /
