children.translated_text: Through <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects), being the guide to all <s>dharmas</s>, there is exactly one activity of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, namely the activity pertaining to destiny (<s>gati</s>).

children.text: kāritrākārairevaṃ yathāvat sarvajñatātrayasya prayogā lakṣyanta iti kāritralakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: The practices of the three kinds of omniscience are duly characterized through the modes of activity — this is the activity-characteristic.

children.text:
(u) svabhāvalakṣaṇāni ṣoḍaśa
eteṣāṃ svabhāvalakṣaṇānāṃ svarūpapratipādanam abhisamayālaṅkāre tisṛbhiḥ kārikābhiḥ samyag vihitam /
children.translated_text:
(F) The sixteen nature-characteristics (<s>svabhāvalakṣaṇa</s>)
The presentation of the nature of these sixteen nature-characteristics is properly set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through three verses.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
uparinirdiṣṭaṃ prayogalakṣaṇameva eteṣāmapi lakṣaṇaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The practice-characteristic stated above is the definition of these as well.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
svabhāvānāṃ ṣoḍaśa bhedā bhavanti / tatra sarvajñatāyāḥ svabhāvāḥ catvāraḥ, mārgajñatāyāḥ, svabhāvāḥ pañca, sarvākārajñatāyāḥ svabhāvāḥ sapteti ṣoḍaśa bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are sixteen divisions of natures. Among these, four are natures of <s>sarvajñatā</s>, five are natures of <s>mārgajñatā</s>, and seven are natures of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> — thus sixteen.

children.text:
sarvajñatāsvabhāvāścatvāraḥ
rāgādiviviktasvabhāvatvena kleśavivekasvabhāvaḥ, rāgādiliṅgakāyādidauṣṭhulyaviviktasvabhāvatvena kleśaliṅgavivekasvabhāvaḥ rāgādinimittāyoniśomanasikāraviviktasvabhāvatvena kleśanimittaviviktasvabhāvaḥ rāgārāgadveṣādveṣamohāmohaviviktasvabhāvatvena vipakṣapratipakṣavivekasvabhāva iti catvāraḥ /
children.translated_text:
Four natures of <s>sarvajñatā</s>:
The nature of separation from afflictions (<s>kleśaviveka</s>), being of a nature separated from desire and the rest; the nature of separation from the signs of afflictions (<s>kleśaliṅgaviveka</s>), being of a nature separated from the bodily and other rigidities that are signs of desire and the rest; the nature of separation from the causes of afflictions (<s>kleśanimittavivikta</s>), being of a nature separated from improper mental attention (<s>ayoniśomanasikāra</s>) which is the cause of desire and the rest; and the nature of separation from opponent and antidote (<s>vipakṣapratipakṣaviveka</s>), being of a nature separated from desire and non-desire, aversion and non-aversion, delusion and non-delusion — thus four.

children.text:
mārgajñatāsvabhāvāḥ pañca
paramārthāsatsarvasattvaparinirvāpaṇaduṣkarasaṃnāhatvena duṣkarasvabhāvaḥ, anya (śrāvakādi-) yānāpātalakṣaṇa aikāntikasvabhāvaḥ, uttamaścirasādhya uddeśasvabhāvaḥ, bhāvyabhāvakabhāvanānupalambhāt anupalambhasvabhāvaḥ, samastabhāvābhiniveśaniṣedhād anabhiniveśasvabhāva iti pañca /
children.translated_text:
Five natures of <s>mārgajñatā</s>:
The nature of difficulty (<s>duṣkara</s>), through donning the difficult armor of bringing all sentient beings — who are ultimately non-existent — to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; the nature of exclusivity (<s>aikāntika</s>), characterized by not falling into other vehicles such as those of <s>śrāvakas</s>; the nature of purpose (<s>uddeśa</s>), being supreme and long to accomplish; the nature of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>), since that which is to be cultivated, the cultivator, and the cultivation are not apprehended; and the nature of non-attachment (<s>anabhiniveśa</s>), through the prohibition of attachment to all existents — thus five.

children.text:
sarvākārajñatāsvabhāvāḥ sapta
sarvajñatāmārgajñatāsaṃgṛhītavastuviśeṣālambanasvabhāvaḥ, lokapratipattigrahaṇādiviparītanirdeśāt sarvalokavipratyanīkasvabhāvaḥ, sarvatra rūpādau jñānadharmasyāpratighātitvād apratighātasvabhāvaḥ, jñānajñeyasamatayā sarvapratiṣṭhānupalambhārthena apadasvabhāvaḥ, tathatayā agatisvabhāvaḥ, rūpādisarvadharmāṇāṃ tattvenānutpannatvāt ajātisvabhāvaḥ, bhāvābhāvādisvabhāvatrayānupalambhāt tathatānupalambhasvabhāva iti sapta /
children.translated_text:
Seven natures of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>:
The nature of having as its object the special entities included in <s>sarvajñatā</s> and <s>mārgajñatā</s>; the nature of being contrary to the entire world (<s>sarvalokavipratyanīka</s>), due to its teaching being contrary to worldly understanding of practice and so on; the nature of non-obstruction (<s>apratighāta</s>), because the <s>dharma</s> of knowledge is unobstructed with respect to all things such as form; the nature of being without foundation (<s>apada</s>), in the sense of non-apprehension of any foundation through the equality of knowledge and the knowable; the nature of being without destination (<s>agati</s>), due to <s>tathatā</s> (suchness); the nature of being without arising (<s>ajāti</s>), because all <s>dharmas</s> such as form are in reality unborn; and the nature of non-apprehension of <s>tathatā</s>, due to the non-apprehension of the three natures of existence, non-existence, and so on — thus seven.

children.text: ityevaṃ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ svabhāvairyathāvat trisarvajñatāprayogā lakṣyanta iti svabhāvalakṣaṇāni / tathā coktam abhisamayālaṅkāre -
children.translated_text: Thus the practices of the three kinds of omniscience are duly characterized through sixteen natures — these are the nature-characteristics. As stated in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>:

children.text: kleśaliṅganimittānāṃ vipakṣapratipakṣayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Separation from afflictions, their signs, and their causes,

children.text: viveko duṣkaraikāntāvuddeśo 'nupalambhakaḥ //
children.translated_text: and from opponent and antidote; difficulty and exclusivity; purpose and non-apprehension;

children.text: niṣiddhābhiniveśaśca yaścālambanasaṃjñakaḥ /
children.translated_text: the prohibition of attachment, and that called 'object',

children.text: vipratyayo 'vidhātī ca so 'padāgatyajātikaḥ //
children.translated_text: contrariety and non-obstruction, and [that which is] without foundation, without destination, and without arising,

children.text: tathatā 'nupalambhaśca svabhāvaḥ ṣoḍaśātmakaḥ /
children.translated_text: and non-apprehension of <s>tathatā</s> — the sixteenfold nature,

children.text: lakṣīva lakṣyate ceti caturthaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ matam //
children.translated_text: [by which], like a target, [the three knowledges] are characterized — this is considered the fourth characteristic.

children.text: ityevaṃ sāmānyena ekatra kṛtāni ekanavatiḥ lakṣaṇāni bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Thus, gathered together in general, there are ninety-one characteristics.

children.text:
6. mokṣabhāgīyam
asya sarvaṃ lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā pratipāditam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
6. <s>Mokṣabhāgīya</s> (portion conducive to liberation)
The entire definition and so forth of this is set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through one verse. Namely:

children.text: animittapradānādisamudāgamakauśalam /
children.translated_text: Skill in the attainment of signlessness (<s>animitta</s>), generosity (<s>pradāna</s>), and the rest,

children.text: sarvākārāvabodhe 'smin mokṣabhāgīyamiṣyate //
children.translated_text: In this realization of all aspects, [that which] is held to belong to the liberation-share (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>).

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
animittālambanajñānākāreṇa dānādyārabhya sarvākārajñatāparyantaṃ svasantāne samudāgame kauśalalakṣaṇo dharmābhisamaya evātra mokṣabhāgīyamiti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The realization of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmābhisamaya</s>) having the character of skillfulness in the arising in one's own continuum, from giving (<s>dāna</s>) and so on up to omniscience (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), with the aspect of knowledge whose object is the signless (<s>animitta</s>) — this very [realization] is here called the 'liberation-share.' This is its definition.

children.text:
(kha) paryāyaḥ
māhāyāniko dharmābhisamayaḥ, māhāyānikaṃ mokṣabhāgīyam, māhāyānikaḥ sambhāramārga iti paryāyāḥ /
children.translated_text:
(b) Synonyms.
The <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization of <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> liberation-share, and the <s>Mahāyāna</s> path of accumulation (<s>sambhāramārga</s>) — these are synonyms.

children.text:
(ga) nirvacanam
mokṣo 'tra kleśavisaṃyogaviśeṣaḥ, tadbhāge (pakṣe) pātitvāt mokṣabhāgīyam / athavā - tadbhāge hitatvāt mokṣabhāgīyam /
children.translated_text:
(c) Etymology.
'Liberation' (<s>mokṣa</s>) here means the special disjunction from afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). Because it falls on the side (<s>bhāga</s>) of that [liberation], it is a 'liberation-share.' Alternatively, because it is beneficial to the side of that [liberation], it is a 'liberation-share.'

children.text:
(gha) bhedaḥ
avasthātaḥ mṛdurmadhyo 'dhimātraśceto trayo 'sya bhedāḥ / svarūpataḥ śrutamayaṃ cintāmayaṃ bhāvanāmayamiti trividhaṃ mokṣabhāgīyamiṣṭam /
children.translated_text:
(d) Classification.
According to stages [of development], there are three divisions: mild, medium, and intense. In terms of its own nature, the liberation-share is held to be threefold: arising from hearing (<s>śrutamaya</s>), arising from reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>), and arising from cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>).

children.text:
(ṅa) avadhiḥ
sambhāramārgeṃ kevalamidaṃ bhavatīti jñeyam / cittotpādasamakālamevotpadya svasantāne yāvanna śraddhādipañcendriyotpādastāvadasya vyāptirbhavati /
children.translated_text:
(e) Scope.
This should be known as existing only on the path of accumulation (<s>sambhāramārga</s>). It arises simultaneously with the generation of the awakening mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>), and its extent lasts until the arising of the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>) such as faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and so on in one's own continuum.

children.text:
(ca) liṅgāni
saṃsārādīnavān mokṣaguṇāṃśa śrāvaṃ śrāvaṃ romaharṣodgamāśrupātādayo bhavanti, cittādīnatvaṃ nirbhayatvamityādīni liṅgāni /
children.translated_text:
(f) Signs.
Signs [of having attained this] include: upon hearing repeatedly about the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> and the qualities of liberation, goosebumps arise, tears fall, and so on; gentleness of mind, fearlessness, and so on are the signs.

children.text:
7. nirvedhabhāgīyam
asya lakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre savistaraṃ pratipāditam /
children.translated_text:
7. The aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>).
Its entire definition and so on are set forth extensively in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
upāyaviśiṣṭasattvasya arthābhisamayo māhāyānikanirvedhabhāgīyasya lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The realization of the meaning (<s>arthābhisamaya</s>) of a being distinguished by means (<s>upāya</s>) is the definition of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> aid to penetration.

children.text:
(kha) paribhāṣā
darśanaheyānāṃ savāsanakleśānāṃ nirvedhakatvena darśanamārgapakṣe pātitvāt, tadbhāgahitatvād vā nirvedhabhāgīyam /
children.translated_text:
(b) Terminology.
Because it penetrates (<s>nirvedhaka</s>) the afflictions with their latent tendencies (<s>savāsana</s>) that are to be abandoned on the path of seeing, and falls on the side of the path of seeing, or because it is beneficial to the side of that [path of seeing], it is called an 'aid to penetration.'

children.text:
(ga) bhedaḥ
nirvedhabhāgīyasya dvādaśa bhedā bhavanti / prathamaṃ ūṣmā, mūrdhā, kṣāntiḥ, agradharmaśceti catvāro bhedāḥ / eṣu caturṣu pratyekaṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedena trividha iti dvādaśa bhedā bhavati / tathā coktam abhisamayālaṅkāre -
children.translated_text:
(c) Classification.
The aids to penetration have twelve divisions. First, the four divisions of heat (<s>ūṣman</s>), summit (<s>mūrdhan</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), and supreme <s>dharma</s> (<s>agradharma</s>). Each of these four is threefold through the division into mild, medium, and intense...

children.text: ālambanaṃ sarvasattvā ūṣmaṇāmiha śasyate /
children.translated_text: The object of the heat [stage] is held here to be all sentient beings;

children.text: samacittādirākārasteṣveva daśadhoditaḥ //
children.translated_text: the aspect, such as equal-mindedness and so on, is stated to be tenfold toward them.

children.text: svayaṃ pāpānnivṛttasya dānādyeṣu sthitasya ca /
children.translated_text: Of one who has himself turned away from evil and abides in giving and so on,

children.text: tayorniyojanānyeṣāṃ varṇavādānukūlate //
children.translated_text: the engagement of others in those [practices] accords with praising [their] virtues.

children.text: mūrdhagaṃ svaparādhāraṃ satyajñānaṃ tathā kṣamā /
children.translated_text: The summit is the support of self and others; likewise knowledge of the truths is patience;

children.text: tathāgradharmā vijñeyāḥ sattvānāṃ pācanādibhiḥ //
children.translated_text: and the supreme <s>dharmas</s> should be known through the maturing of beings and so on.

children.text:
(gha) avadhiḥ
śūnyatālambanātmikāṃ vidarśanāprāptimārabhya yāvanna darśanamārgaprāptistāvadasyāvadhirbhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
(d) Scope.
Its scope extends from the attainment of insight (<s>vidarśanā</s>) that has emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) as its object, until the attainment of the path of seeing.

children.text:
8. avaivartiko gaṇaḥ
avaivartikabodhisattvasaṃghasya svarūpaṃ ekayā kārikayā abhisamayālaṅkāre proktam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
8. The non-regressing assembly (<s>avaivartika gaṇa</s>).
The nature of the assembly of non-regressing <s>bodhisattvas</s> is stated in one verse in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Namely:

children.text: nirvedhāṅgānyupādāya darśanābhyāsamārgayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Taking the aids to penetration [as the starting point], on the paths of seeing and cultivation,

children.text: ye bodhisattvā vartante so 'trāvaivartiko gaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who engage [in practice] — that is here the non-regressing assembly.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
rūpādinivṛttinirvicikitsādyākāraiḥ viṃśatiprakāraiḥ nirvedhabhāgīyasthānām avaivartikalakṣaṇaṃ jñeyam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The characteristics of non-regression for those abiding in the aids to penetration should be known through twenty modes such as the turning away from form and so on, freedom from doubt, and so on.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
nirvedhabhāgīyaprayogamārgasthaḥ, kṣāntijñānasaṃgṛhītadarśanamārgasthaḥ, paraśca prābandhikabhāvanāmārgastha iti trividho bhavati avaivartikabodhisattvasaṃgha iti trayo 'sya bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
The non-regressing <s>bodhisattva</s> assembly is threefold: those abiding on the path of preparation at the aids to penetration stage, those abiding on the path of seeing included within patience-knowledge, and further those abiding on the continuous path of cultivation. These are the three...

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
prayogamārgīyoṣmābhisamayamārabhya antimakṣaṇāvasthitabodhisattvāvasthāparyantamasya sīmā bhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope.
Its limit extends from the heat realization on the path of preparation up to the <s>bodhisattva</s> stage abiding at the final moment.

children.text:
9. bhavaśāntyoḥ samatā
asya samatāprayogasya lakṣaṇādim abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā pratipāditam / tathā hi -
svapnopamatvād dharmāṇāṃ bhavaśāntyorakalpanā /
children.translated_text: Because <s>dharmas</s> are like a dream, there is no conceptualization of existence and quiescence;

children.text: karmābhāvādicodyānāṃ parihārā yathoditāḥ //
children.translated_text: the refutations of objections such as the non-existence of <s>karma</s> (action) are as stated.

9. Equality of existence and quiescence (<s>bhavaśāntyoḥ samatā</s>).
The definition and so on of this practice of equality are set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in one verse. Namely:

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
pṛṣṭhalabdhāvasthāyāmapi sattāgrāhakavikalpaparikṣayāt śauddhabhūmikaṃ jñānaṃ bhavaśamasamatāprayogasya lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The knowledge belonging to the pure stages (<s>śuddhabhūmi</s>), arising even in the post-attainment state (<s>pṛṣṭhalabdha</s>) from the exhaustion of the conceptualization that grasps at [real] existence of beings — this is the definition of the practice of equality of existence and quiescence.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
tisṛṇāṃ śuddhabhūmīnāṃ trīṇi jñānānyevāsya trayo bhedāḥ /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
The three knowledges of the three pure stages are the three divisions of this [practice].

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
aṣṭamīṃ bhūmimārabhya antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvāvasthāparyantamasya sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope.
Its limit extends from the eighth stage up to the <s>bodhisattva</s> stage abiding at the final moment.

children.text:
10. kṣetraśuddhiprayogaḥ
prayogastāsya lakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā 'bhihitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
10. The practice of purification of the field (<s>kṣetraśuddhi</s>).
The entire definition and so on of this practice are stated in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in one verse. Namely:

children.text: sattvalokasya yā 'śuddhistasyāḥ śuddhyupahārataḥ /
children.translated_text: That which is the impurity of the world of sentient beings — through the offering of its purification,

children.text: tathā bhājanalokasya buddhakṣetrasya śuddhatā //
children.translated_text: and likewise [the impurity of] the receptacle world — [this constitutes] the purity of the Buddha-field.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
praṇidhānādikuśalamūlabalena svabuddhakṣetraṃ sattvabhājanalokātmakaṃ pariśodhitukāmasya śauddhabhūmikāni jñānānyeva kṣetraśuddhiprayogasya lakṣaṇāni /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The knowledges belonging to the pure stages of one who wishes to purify one's own Buddha-field, consisting of the world of sentient beings and the receptacle world, through the power of roots of virtue such as aspirational vows (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) — these are the defining characteristics of the practice of field-purification.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
svabuddhakṣetrasya bhājanalokaśuddhiprayogaḥ sattvalokaśuddhiprayogaśceti dvau bhedau /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
There are two divisions: the practice of purifying the receptacle world of one's own Buddha-field, and the practice of purifying the sentient-being world.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
tisṛṣu śuddhabhūmiṣvayaṃ prayogo bhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope.
This practice occurs on the three pure stages.

children.text:
11. upāyakauśalam
asyopāyakauśalaprayogasya svarūpādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre dvābhyāṃ kārikābhyāmupadarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
11. Skillful means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>).
The nature and so on of this practice of skillful means are shown in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in two verses. Namely:

children.text: viṣayo 'sya prayogaśca śātravāṇāmatikramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Its object and practice, the transcending of hostile [factors],

children.text: apratiṣṭho yathāvedhasādhāraṇalakṣaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: non-abiding, and the character of being common according to capacity,

children.text: asakto 'nupalambhaśca nimittapraṇidhikṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: non-attachment, non-apprehension, being free from signs and aspirations,

children.text: talliṅgaṃ cāpramāṇaṃ ca daśadhopāyakauśalam //
children.translated_text: its marks, and being immeasurable — skillful means is tenfold.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
manasikāraparivarjanena nirābhogakarmasampādanasamarthāni jñānāni upāyakauśalātmakānīti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
Knowledges that are capable of accomplishing action effortlessly (<s>nirābhoga</s>) through the relinquishment of mental engagement (<s>manasikāra</s>) — these have the nature of skillful means. This is the definition.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
upāyakauśalasya daśa bhedā bhavanti / yathā - āntarāyikadharmasamatikramaṇena devādimārātikramaḥ, vibhāvitasarvadharmasamatvena apratiṣṭhitavihāraḥ, praṇidhānasamṛddhyā yathāvedhaṃ parārthakaraṇam, svabhyastasarvaduṣkaratvena asādhāraṇaḥ, śukladharmaviśuddhyā sarvadharmasyāgrahaṇam, śūnyatāvimokṣamukhatvena anupalambhaḥ, animittavimokṣamukhatvena animittaḥ, apraṇihitavimokṣamukhatvena apraṇidhānam, praśnapūrvakāvaivartikadharmakathanena avaivartikaliṅgam, sarvaviṣayajñānatvena apramāṇamiti daśa upāyakauśalaprayogā iti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
Skillful means has ten divisions, namely: transcending <s>Māra</s> and others such as gods through overcoming obstructive <s>dharmas</s>; non-abiding dwelling through having realized the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>; through the success of aspirational vows...

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
aṣṭamīṃ bhūmimārabhya antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvāvasthāparyantamasma sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope.
Its limit extends from the eighth stage up to the <s>bodhisattva</s> stage abiding at the final moment.

children.text: // iti sarvākārābhisambodhopalakṣakā ekādaśa dharmāḥ //
children.translated_text: // Thus the eleven <s>dharmas</s> that characterize the realization of all aspects (<s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s>). //

children.text: (ā) Mūrdhābhisamayopalakṣakā aṣṭau dharmāḥ
children.translated_text: (IV) The eight <s>dharmas</s> that characterize the peak realization (<s>mūrdhābhisamaya</s>):

children.text: 1. liṅgam (ūṣmā mūrdhaprayogaḥ), 2. vivṛddhiḥ (mūrdhā mūrdhaprayogaḥ), 3. nirūḍhiḥ (kṣāntiḥ mūrdhaprayogaḥ) , 4. cittasaṃsthitiḥ (agradharmaḥ mūrdhaprayogaḥ) , 5. darśanamārgaḥ (mūrdhaprayoga), 6. bhāvanāmārgaḥ (mūrdhaprayogaḥ), 7. ānantaryasamādhiḥ (mūrdhaprayogaḥ), 8. vipratipattiḥ (mūrdhaprayogaḥ) , ityaṣṭau dharmā mūrdhābhisamayamupalakṣayantīti abhisamayālaṅkāre pratipāditam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: 1. Sign (<s>liṅga</s>) (heat as the peak practice), 2. Increase (<s>vivṛddhi</s>) (summit as peak practice), 3. Stability (<s>nirūḍhi</s>) (patience as peak practice), 4. Mental abiding (<s>cittasaṃsthiti</s>) (supreme <s>dharma</s> as peak practice), 5. Path of seeing (as peak practice)...

children.text: liṅgaṃ tasya vivṛddhiśca nirūḍhiścittasaṃsthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: The sign, its increase, stability, and mental abiding,

children.text: caturdhā ca vikalpasya pratipakṣaścaturvidhaḥ //
children.translated_text: and the fourfold antidote to the fourfold conceptualization,

children.text: pratyekaṃ darśanākhye ca bhāvanākhye ca vartmani /
children.translated_text: each on the path called 'seeing' and on the path called 'cultivation,'

children.text: ānantaryasamādhiśca saha vipratipattibhiḥ //
children.translated_text: and the uninterrupted concentration (<s>ānantaryasamādhi</s>) together with the divergent [views] —

children.text: mūrdhābhisamayaḥ /
children.translated_text: [this constitutes] the peak realization (<s>mūrdhābhisamaya</s>).

children.text:
1. liṅgam (ūṣmā mūrdhaprayogaḥ)
asyoṣmaṇo mūrdhaprayogasya svarūpam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayopadarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
1. Sign (<s>liṅga</s>) (heat as the peak practice).
The nature of this heat as peak practice is shown in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in one verse. Namely:

children.text: svapnāntare 'pi svapnābhasarvadharmekṣaṇādikam /
children.translated_text: Even in a dream, the seeing of all <s>dharmas</s> as dream-like and so on —

children.text: mūrdhaprāptasya yogasya liṅgaṃ dvādaśadhā matam //
children.translated_text: the sign of the <s>yoga</s> that has attained the peak is considered to be twelvefold.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
svapne 'pi sarvadharmāṇāṃ svapnābhatvadarśanādiṣu dvādaśaliṅgeṣu anyatamasya prāptyā vyavasthāpitaḥ prathamo nirvedhabhāgīya ūṣmā mūrdhaprayoga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The first aid to penetration — heat as peak practice — is established through the attainment of any one of the twelve signs, such as seeing all <s>dharmas</s> as dream-like even in dreams. This is its definition.

children.text: (kha) mṛdu-madhyādhimātrabhedena trayo 'sya bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: (b) Through the division into mild, medium, and intense, it has three divisions.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
nairātmyālambanāyā vidarśanāyāḥ prāptimārabhya bhūmiprāptiparyantamasya sīmā bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope.
Its limit extends from the attainment of insight (<s>vidarśanā</s>) that has selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) as its object up to the attainment of the stages.

children.text:
2. vivṛddhiḥ (mūrdhā mūrdhaprayogaḥ)
asya mūrdhākhyasya mūrdhaprayogasya lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā paridīpitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
2. Increase (<s>vivṛddhi</s>) (summit as the peak practice).
The definition and so on of this peak practice called 'summit' are illuminated in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> in one verse. Namely:

children.text: jambudvopajaneyattābuddhapūjāśubhādikām / upamāṃ bahudhā kṛtvā vivṛddhiḥ ṣoḍaśātmikā //
children.translated_text: Making manifold comparisons of being born in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, worship of the <s>Buddha</s>, meritorious deeds, and so forth — the increase is sixteenfold.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
puṇyavivṛddhyādiṣoḍaśavivṛddhīnāṃ pūrṇatayā māhāyāniko dvitīyo nirvedhabhāgīyo mūrdhā mūrdhaprayoga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>mūrdhan</s> (peak) peak-practice is: the second <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (factor conducive to penetration) of the Mahāyāna, [so called] through the completion of the sixteen increases beginning with the increase of merit.

children.text: ayaṃ mūrdhā mūrdhaprayogaḥ mahāyānaprayogamārgīyo mūrdhaprayogaśceti samānārthakau /
children.translated_text: This <s>mūrdhan</s> peak-practice and the Mahāyāna <s>prayogamārga</s> (path of preparation) peak-practice of <s>mūrdhan</s> are synonymous.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedena trayo 'sya bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are three divisions of this through the subdivision into mild, middling, and supreme.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
māhāyānikasya prayogamārgīyamūrdhaprayogasya yathāvadhistathaivāsyāpi jñātavyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The scope of this should be known as the same as that of the Mahāyāna <s>prayogamārga</s> peak-practice of <s>mūrdhan</s>.

children.text:
3. nirūḍhiḥ (kṣāntiḥ mūrdhaprayogaḥ)
asya nirūḍhyākhyamūrdhaprayogasya sarvaṃ lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayopavarṇitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
3. <s>Nirūḍhi</s> (<s>kṣānti</s> peak-practice)
The entire definition and so forth of this peak-practice called <s>nirūḍhi</s> (firmness) is described in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through one verse. Namely:

children.text: trisarvajñatvadharmāṇāṃ paripūriranuttarā /
children.translated_text: The unsurpassed fulfillment of the <s>dharmas</s> of the three kinds of omniscience (<s>trisarvajñatva</s>),

children.text: aparityaktasattvārthā nirūḍhirabhidhīyate //
children.translated_text: without abandoning the welfare of sentient beings — this is declared to be <s>nirūḍhi</s> (firmness).

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
samyagupāyakauśalabalena nirvikalpādhigamāvasthāyāṃ mahākaruṇādisammukhībhāvena yathoktasarvākārajñatāditrisarvajñatādharmāṇāṃ (cittotpādādīnāṃ) / anuttarā paripūriḥ nirūḍhyākhyastṛtīyo nirvedhabhāgīyaḥ kṣāntimūrdhaprayoga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>nirūḍhi</s> — the third <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>, the <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) peak-practice — is: the unsurpassed fulfillment of the <s>dharmas</s> of the three kinds of omniscience beginning with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> as previously described (i.e., <s>cittotpāda</s> and so forth), through the power of correct skillful means, in the state of non-conceptual realization, while bringing to the forefront great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) and the like.

children.text: ayaṃ kṣāntyākhyo mūrdhaprayogaḥ māhāyānikaḥ prayogamārgīyakṣāntiprayogaśceti dvau samānārthakau /
children.translated_text: This peak-practice called <s>kṣānti</s> and the Mahāyāna <s>prayogamārga</s> <s>kṣānti</s> practice are synonymous.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
mṛmumadhyādhimātrabhedenāsya kṣāntyākhyamūrdhaprayogasya trayo bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are three divisions of this peak-practice called <s>kṣānti</s> through the subdivision into mild, middling, and supreme.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
yathā māhāyānikāyāḥ prayogamārgīyāyāḥ kṣānteravadhistathā asyāpi prayogasyāvadhirjñātavyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The scope of this practice should be known as the same as that of the Mahāyāna <s>prayogamārga</s> <s>kṣānti</s> (patience).

children.text:
4. cittasaṃsthitiḥ (agradharmaḥ mūrdhaprayogaḥ)
asya agradharmākhyasya mūrdhaprayogasya lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā pratipāditam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
4. <s>Cittasaṃsthiti</s> (<s>agradharma</s> peak-practice)
The definition and so forth of this peak-practice called <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma) is set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through one verse. Namely:

children.text: caturdvīpakasāhasradvitrisāhasrakopamaḥ /
children.translated_text: With the simile of the four continents, the first thousand, the second thousand, and the third thousand [world-systems],

children.text: kṛtvā puṇyabahutvena samādhiḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
children.translated_text: this <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is proclaimed through the abundance of merit.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
darśanamārgotpādasamarthā pramāṇātikrāntapuṇyabahutvena samādhilakṣaṇā (sthirībhāvalakṣaṇā) cittasaṃsthitiścaturthanirvedhabhāgīyo 'gradharmo mūrdhaprayoga iti lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>cittasaṃsthiti</s> — the fourth <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>, the <s>agradharma</s> peak-practice — is: that which has the characteristic of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), i.e., the characteristic of stability, through the abundance of merit that surpasses all measure, and which is capable of generating the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>).

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedena trayo 'sya prayogasya bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are three divisions of this practice through the subdivision into mild, middling, and supreme.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
māhāyānikasya prayogamārgīyāgradharmasya yathā avadhistathaivāsyāpi jñātavyaḥ /
etāni ca liṅgādīni yathākramamūṣmādicaturnirvedhabhāgīyasvarūpāṇi veditavyāni /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The scope of this should be known as the same as that of the Mahāyāna <s>prayogamārga agradharma</s>.
And these signs (<s>liṅga</s>) and so forth should be understood as the respective natures of the four <s>nirvedhabhāgīyas</s> beginning with <s>ūṣma</s> (heat).

children.text:
5. darśanamārgaḥ (mūrdhaprayogaḥ)
asya darśanamārgākhyasya mūrdhaprayogasya lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre savistaraṃ aṣṭādaśabhiḥ kārikābhiḥ pratipāditam /
children.translated_text:
5. The path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s> peak-practice)
The definition and so forth of this peak-practice called the path of seeing is set forth extensively in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through eighteen verses.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
darśanaheyāyāḥ sattāgrāhikāyā dṛṣṭeḥ pratipakṣabhāvena vyavasthāpito māhāyānikaḥ satyābhisamayo darśanamārgākhyo mūrdhaprayoga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of the peak-practice called the path of seeing is: a Mahāyāna realization of truth (<s>satyābhisamaya</s>), established as the antidote to the view that grasps at real existence (<s>sattāgrāhikā dṛṣṭi</s>), which is to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaheya</s>).

children.text: ayaṃ darśanamārgākhyo mūrdhaprayogaḥ māhāyāniko darśanamārgaśca paryāyau /
children.translated_text: This peak-practice called the path of seeing and the Mahāyāna path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) are synonymous.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
heyadṛṣṭyā darśanaprahātavyānāṃ caturṇāṃ vikalpānāṃ catvāraḥ pratipakṣā iti catvāro 'sya prabhedā bhavanti / samāhitaḥ pṛṣṭhalabdhaśceti dvāvapi bhedau /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
From the perspective of what is to be abandoned, there are four antidotes to the four conceptualizations to be abandoned by seeing — thus four divisions. There are also two divisions: meditative equipoise (<s>samāhita</s>) and subsequent attainment (<s>pṛṣṭhalabdha</s>).

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
māhāyānikasya darśanamārgasya avadhivat asyāpyavadhirbhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The scope of this is the same as that of the Mahāyāna path of seeing.

children.text:
6. bhāvanāmārgaḥ (mūrdhaprayogaḥ)
asya bhāvanāmārgākhyasya mūrdhaprayogasya sarvaṃ lakṣaṇādikam abhisamayālaṅkāre navabhiḥ kārikābhiḥ savistaramabhihitam /
children.translated_text:
6. The path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s> peak-practice)
The entire definition and so forth of this peak-practice called the path of meditation is extensively set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through nine verses.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
trisarvajñatāparigṛhītayā prakarṣaprāptaprajñayopāttānāṃ bhāvanāprahātavyavikalpapratipakṣāṇāṃ dṛṣṭyā vyavasthāpito māhāyāniko 'nvabhisamayaḥ bhāvanāmārgākhyo mūrdhaprayoga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of the peak-practice called the path of meditation is: a Mahāyāna subsequent realization (<s>anvabhisamaya</s>), established from the perspective of the antidotes to the conceptualizations to be abandoned by meditation (<s>bhāvanāprahātavya</s>), taken up by the wisdom that has reached excellence (<s>prakarṣaprāptaprajñā</s>) embraced by the three kinds of omniscience.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
bhāvanāheyānāṃ navānāṃ vikalpānāṃ sākṣāt pratipakṣabhūtā navānantaryamārgāḥ, nava ca vimuktimārgā iti aṣṭādaśa asya bhāvanāmārgākhyasya mūrdhaprayogasya bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are eighteen divisions of this peak-practice called the path of meditation: nine <s>ānantaryamārgas</s> (uninterrupted paths) that are the direct antidotes to the nine conceptualizations to be abandoned by meditation, and nine <s>vimuktimārgas</s> (paths of liberation).

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
prathamāṃ bhūmimārabhya daśamīṃ bhūmiṃ yāvadasya sīmā bhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
Its boundary extends from the first stage (<s>bhūmi</s>) up to the tenth stage.

children.text:
7. ānantaryaṃsamādhiḥ (mūrdhaprayogaḥ)
buddhatvaprāpteravyavahito yaḥ pūrvasamanantaraḥ samādhiḥ, so 'tra ānantaryasamādhiḥ / asya lakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvaṃ svarūpam abhisamayālaṅkāre tisṛbhiḥ kārikābhiḥ samyak pratipāditam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
7. <s>Ānantaryasamādhi</s> (uninterrupted concentration peak-practice)
The <s>samādhi</s> that is the immediately preceding condition, without any intervening [state], before the attainment of Buddhahood — that is the <s>ānantaryasamādhi</s> (uninterrupted concentration) here. The entire definition and so forth of its essential nature is properly set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through three verses. Namely:

children.text: trisāhasrajanaṃ śiṣyakhaḍgādhigamasampadi /
children.translated_text: Having established the beings of the <s>trisāhasra</s> (triple-thousand [world-system]) in the attainment of the realization of disciples (<s>śiṣya</s>) and solitary realizers (<s>khaḍga</s>),

children.text: bodhisattvasya ca nyāme pratiṣṭhāpya śubhopamāḥ //
children.translated_text: and of the <s>bodhisattva</s> in the definite state (<s>nyāma</s>), with comparisons of merit,

children.text: kṛtvā puṇyabahutvena buddhatvāpteranantaraḥ /
children.translated_text: through the abundance of merit, immediately before the attainment of Buddhahood —

children.text: ānantaryasamādhiḥ sa sarvākārajñatā ca tat //
children.translated_text: that is the <s>ānantaryasamādhi</s> (uninterrupted concentration), and that is <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects).

children.text: ālambanamabhāvo 'sya smṛtiścādhipatirmataḥ /
children.translated_text: Its object is non-existence, and mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) is considered its governing factor (<s>adhipati</s>);

children.text: ākāraḥ śāntatā cātra //
children.translated_text: its aspect is quiescence (<s>śāntatā</s>) herein.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
trisarvajñatāsaṃgṛhītaprakarṣaprāptaprajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāḥ phalabhūtasya sarvākārajñatāvipākasya avyavahitatvena sākṣādutpādakaḥ paryantayogaḥ ānantaryasamādhyākhyo mūrdhaprayoga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of the peak-practice called the <s>ānantaryasamādhi</s> is: the final yoga (<s>paryantayoga</s>) that directly produces — without any intervening [state] — the fruition of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) as the result of cultivating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> that has reached excellence and is embraced by the three kinds of omniscience.

children.text: ayaṃ ānantaryasamādhiḥ mūrdhaprayogaḥ, antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvasya jñānamityanarthāntaram /
children.translated_text: This <s>ānantaryasamādhi</s> peak-practice is synonymous with the knowledge of the <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding at the final moment.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
ekakṣaṇikāścatvāraḥ prayoga evāsya catvāro bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
The four practices that occur in a single moment (<s>ekakṣaṇika</s>) are the four divisions of this.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
ayaṃ prayogaḥ kevalaṃ antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvāvasthāyāmeva bhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
This practice exists only at the stage of the <s>bodhisattva</s> abiding at the final moment.

children.text:
8. vipratipattiḥ (mūrdhaprayogaḥ)
aviditopāyakauśalānāṃ pravādināṃ nānācodyamukhaparamparāprasarpipyo vipratipattiayo 'tra nirākarttavyā bhavantīti tāsāṃ vipratipattīnāṃ sarvaṃ lakṣaṇādikaṃ svarūpam abhisamayālaṅkāre tisṛbhiḥ kārikābhiḥ savistaraṃ samyak pratipāditam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
8. <s>Vipratipatti</s> (erroneous views as peak-practice)
The erroneous views that spread through various chains of objections by proponents who do not know skillful means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>) — these are the <s>vipratipattis</s> that must be refuted here. The entire definition and so forth of these erroneous views is extensively and properly set forth in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through three verses. Namely:

children.text: ālambanopapattau ca tatsvabhāvāvadhāraṇe /
children.translated_text: Regarding the object (<s>ālambana</s>) and its arising, and the ascertainment of its essential nature,

children.text: sarvākārajñatājñāne paramārthe sasaṃvṛtau //
children.translated_text: regarding the knowledge of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, regarding the ultimate truth together with conventional [truth],

children.text: prayoge triṣu ratneṣu sopāye samaye muneḥ /
children.translated_text: regarding practice, regarding the three jewels (<s>ratna</s>), regarding skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), regarding the realization of the Sage,

children.text: viparyāse samārge ca pratipakṣavipakṣayoḥ //
children.translated_text: regarding the perversion (<s>viparyāsa</s>), regarding the path, and regarding the antidote and the adverse factor,

children.text: lakṣaṇe bhāvanāyāṃ ca matā vipratittayaḥ /
children.translated_text: regarding the characteristic and regarding meditation — the erroneous views are considered

children.text: sarvākārajñatādhārā ṣoḍhā daśa ca vādinām //
children.translated_text: [to be] based on <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, sixteenfold and tenfold, of the proponents.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
saṃvṛtiparamārthasatyayordvayoḥ svabhāvata ekatvalakṣaṇayoḥ agrahaṇarūpāḥ sammukhībhūtavikalpāḥ tadbījāni vā nirākarttavyā vipratipattaya iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of the erroneous views (<s>vipratipatti</s>) to be refuted is: manifest conceptualizations, or their seeds, that have the form of non-apprehension of the two truths — conventional and ultimate — each having the characteristic of oneness in its own nature.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
vipratipattīnāṃ ṣoḍaśa bhedā bhavanti / tathā hi - saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtadhātvorabhāvatvena ālambanopapattauḥ sarvathā nīrūpatvād ālambanasvabhāvadhāraṇe, bhāvābhāvānupalambhena sarvākārajñatājñāne, tathatāsvabhāvatvena saṃvṛttiparamārthasatyadvaye, dānādyanupalambhena prayoge, boddhavyābhāvād buddharatne, nāmadheyamātratvād dharmaratne, rūpādyālambanapratiṣedhāt saṃgharatne, dānādyanulambhena upāyakauśale, bhāvābhāvobhyarūpādhigamapratiṣeghāt tathāgatābhisamaye, prapañcavyavasthāpitānityāditvena nityādiviparyāse, vibhāvitamārgaphalāsākṣātkaraṇena mārge, hānopādānābhāvena vipakṣe pratipakṣe ca, dharmyabhāvād dharmalakṣaṇe, svasāmānyalakṣaṇānupapattyā bhāvanāyāṃ ceti sarvākārajñatādhiṣṭhānāḥ saṃśayarūpāḥ ṣoḍaśa vipratipattayo bhavanti / tāḥ yathāsambhavamubhayasatyāśritopāyakauśalena nirākṛtya samyak sarvathā niścayamutpādya kalyāṇakāmaiḥ bodhisattvairānantaryasamādhiradhigantavyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are sixteen divisions of erroneous views. Namely: regarding the arising of the object (<s>ālambanopapatti</s>), due to the non-existence of the conditioned and unconditioned realms; regarding the ascertainment of the nature of the object, due to being completely formless; regarding the knowledge of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, through the non-apprehension of existence and non-existence; regarding the two truths — conventional and ultimate, due to having the nature of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness); regarding practice, through the non-apprehension of generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and the rest; regarding the <s>Buddha</s> jewel, due to the non-existence of anything to be awakened to; regarding the <s>Dharma</s> jewel, due to being mere designation; regarding the <s>Saṅgha</s> jewel, through the negation of objects such as form; regarding skillful means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>), through the non-apprehension of generosity and the rest; regarding the realization of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through the negation of the realization of the forms of existence, non-existence, and both; regarding the perversion (<s>viparyāsa</s>) of impermanence and the rest established through conceptual proliferation; regarding the path, through the actualization of the fruit of the cultivated path; regarding the adverse factor and the antidote, due to the absence of abandonment and adoption; regarding the characteristic of <s>dharmas</s>, due to the non-existence of the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer); and regarding meditation, due to the impossibility of specific and general characteristics — thus there are sixteen erroneous views in the form of doubts, based on <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Having refuted these through skillful means that relies on both truths, and having generated complete certainty in all respects, <s>bodhisattvas</s> who desire the good should realize the <s>ānantaryasamādhi</s> (uninterrupted concentration).

children.text: etāsu kalpanātmikā vipratipattayo mukhyāḥ, yāśca prasaṅgamukhenoktāstā gauṇā iti mantavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Among these, the erroneous views that are conceptual in nature are primary, while those stated through the method of consequence (<s>prasaṅga</s>) should be understood as secondary.

children.text: etāḥ ṣoḍaśāpi vipratipattayo kalpanātmikā śabdātmikā ceti dvayorantarbhavanti /
children.translated_text: These sixteen erroneous views are all subsumed under two: those of a conceptual nature and those of a verbal nature.

children.text: dvayoḥ satyayorekamālambya yadaparaṃ nirākaroti tad abhiniveśātmakaṃ jñānameva kalpanātmikā vipratipattiḥ /
children.translated_text: That knowledge which, grasping one of the two truths, negates the other — being of the nature of attachment (<s>abhiniveśa</s>) — that itself is the erroneous view of a conceptual nature.

children.text: dvayoḥ satyayorekaṃ nimittīkṛtya yā aparaṃ nirākaroti sā vāk śabdātmikā vipratipattiaravaseyā /
children.translated_text: Speech consisting of words, which, taking one of the two truths as the basis, refutes the other — that is the ground of conflicting understanding that is to be removed.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
mārge 'praveśādārabhya aśuddhasaptabhūmiparyantamāsāṃ vipratipattīnāṃ sīmā bhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
(c) Limit.
From prior to entry onto the path up to the seventh impure <s>bhūmi</s> (ground) — that is the boundary of these conflicting understandings.

children.text: // iti mūrdhābhisamayopalakṣakā aṣṭau dharmāḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [are explained] the eight <s>dharmas</s> that are indicators of the summit realization (<s>mūrdhābhisamaya</s>).

children.text: (i) ānupūrvikābhisamayopalakṣakāḥ trayodaśa dharmāḥ
children.translated_text: (iv) The thirteen <s>dharmas</s> that are indicators of the sequential realization (<s>ānupūrvikābhisamaya</s>).

children.text: ānupūrvikābhisamayasya svarūpanirdeśaḥ abhisamayālaṅkāre saṃkṣepataḥ kārikāśena kṛtaḥ / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: The essential description of the sequential realization has been briefly accomplished in a half-verse in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Thus:

children.text: tredhā daśadhā cānupūrvikaḥ
children.translated_text: 'The sequential [realization] is threefold and tenfold.'

children.text: vistaratastu tasya lakṣaṇādikamanayā ekayā kārikayopanyastam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: In detail, its characteristics and the like have been presented in one verse. Thus:

children.text: dānena prajñayā yāvad buddhādau smṛtibhiśca sā /
children.translated_text: 'Through giving, wisdom, up to the recollections of the <s>Buddha</s> and the like,

children.text: dharmābhāvasvabhāvenetyanupūrvakriyā matā //
children.translated_text: and through the nature of the non-existence of <s>dharmas</s> — the sequential practice is considered [to be such].'

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
sarvākārajñatāditrisarvajñatākārān adhigatān anupūrvīkṛtya prajñābhāvanayopāttaḥ sattvayogaḥ ānupūrvikaprayoga iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The engagement of beings [in the path], which is taken up through the cultivation of wisdom by sequentially [reviewing] the realized aspects of the three types of omniscience beginning with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) — the sequential practice (<s>ānupūrvikaprayoga</s>) is so defined.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
dānādiṣaṭpāramitāparipūraṇena (ṣaṭ), buddha-dharma-saṃgha-śīla-tyāga-devatā-nāmanusmaraṇena (ṣaṭ) , rūpādisarvadharmābhāve svabhāvāvabodhena (ekaḥ) yo 'dhigamaḥ sa ānupūrvikābhisamayastrayodaśavidha ityasya trayodaśa bhedā bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
Through the fulfillment of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) such as giving and the like (six); through the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Saṅgha</s>, moral discipline, generosity, and deities (six); and through the understanding of the nature of the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s> such as form and the like (one) — the realization that constitutes these is the thirteenfold sequential realization. Thus, there are thirteen divisions.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
sambhāramārgamārabhya ekakṣaṇābhisambodhāt samanantarapūrvakṣaṇaparyantamasya sīmā bhavatīti /
children.translated_text:
(c) Limit.
From the path of accumulation (<s>sambhāramārga</s>) up to the moment immediately preceding the single-moment awakening (<s>ekakṣaṇābhisambodha</s>) — that is its boundary.

children.text: // iti ānupūrvikābhisamayopalakṣakāḥ trayodaśaḥ dharmāḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [are explained] the thirteen <s>dharmas</s> that are indicators of the sequential realization.

children.text: (ī) ekakṣaṇābhisambodhābhisamayopalakṣakāḥ catvāro dharmāḥ
children.translated_text: (v) The four <s>dharmas</s> that are indicators of the single-moment complete awakening realization (<s>ekakṣaṇābhisambodhābhisamaya</s>).

children.text: ekakṣaṇābhisambodhasya svarūpanirdeśaḥ abhisamayālaṅkāre kārikārdhena saṃkṣepataḥ kṛtaḥ / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: The essential description of the single-moment complete awakening has been briefly accomplished in a half-verse in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Thus:

children.text: ekakṣaṇābhisambodho lakṣaṇena caturvidhaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'The single-moment complete awakening is fourfold by its characteristics.'

children.text: vistaratastu saptamādhikāre draṣṭavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In detail, it should be seen in the seventh chapter.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
adhigatatrisarvajñatākāreṣu svabhyastasteṣāmeva kṣaṇenaikenādhigamarūpaḥ paryantayogaḥ ekakṣaṇābhisambodha iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The final practice (<s>paryantayoga</s>), which takes the form of realization in a single moment of those very aspects of the three types of omniscience that have been realized and repeatedly practiced — this is the definition of single-moment complete awakening.

children.text: ekakṣaṇaprayogaḥ, antimakṣaṇabodhisattvīyajñānam, ānantaryamūrdhaprayogaḥ ityanarthāntaram /
children.translated_text: The single-moment practice, the knowledge of the <s>bodhisattva</s> at the final moment, and the summit practice of the uninterrupted [path] — these are synonymous terms.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
svarūpataḥ ekavidha eva ekakṣaṇābhisambodho lakṣaṇena (vyāvṛtyā) caturvidho bhavati, yathā - avipākalakṣaṇaḥ, vipākalakṣaṇaḥ alakṣaṇalakṣaṇaḥ, advayalakṣaṇaśceti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
In its essential nature, the single-moment complete awakening is of one type only, but by its characteristics (exclusions) it is fourfold, namely: the characteristic of non-maturation (<s>avipākalakṣaṇa</s>), the characteristic of maturation (<s>vipākalakṣaṇa</s>), the characteristic of non-characteristic (<s>alakṣaṇalakṣaṇa</s>), and the characteristic of non-duality (<s>advayalakṣaṇa</s>).

children.text:
(ya) avipākalakṣaṇaḥ
asya sarvaṃ svarūpam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā parīdīpitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
(i) The characteristic of non-maturation.
Its entire nature has been illuminated in one verse in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Thus:

children.text: anāsravāṇāṃ sarveṣāmekaikenāpi saṃgrahāt /
children.translated_text: 'Because each single [uncontaminated dharma] includes all the uncontaminated [dharmas],

children.text: ekakṣaṇāvabodho 'yaṃ jñeyo dānādinā muneḥ //
children.translated_text: this single-moment awakening of the Sage should be known through giving and the like.'

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
ekakṣaṇadānādijñānena anāsravadānādyaśītyanuvyañjanalakṣaṇānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ saṃgraheṇa bodhisattvasya avabodharūpaḥ paryantayogaḥ avipākānāsravasarvadharmaikakṣaṇalakṣaṇo bhavatīti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The final practice, taking the form of the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s awakening through the inclusion — by the single-moment knowledge of giving and the like — of [all] uncontaminated <s>dharmas</s> characterized by giving and the like, the eighty minor marks, and so forth: this has the characteristic of the single-moment [realization] of all uncontaminated <s>dharmas</s> in the non-maturation [state].

children.text: (ra) vipākalakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: (ii) The characteristic of maturation.

children.text: asya sarvaṃ svarūpam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā samyagabhihitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: Its entire nature has been properly stated in one verse in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Thus:

children.text: vipākadharmatāvasthā sarvaśuklamayī yadā /
children.translated_text: 'When the maturation state of <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality), consisting entirely of the pure,

children.text: prajñāpāramitā jātā jñānamekakṣaṇe tadā //
children.translated_text: has arisen as <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, then that is knowledge in a single moment.'

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
yadā bodhisattvasya pratipakṣabhāvanayā sarvavipakṣakalaṅkāpagamena sakalavyavadānapakṣavipākadharmatāvasthā śuklasvabhāvā jātā, tadā ekasminneva kṣaṇe vipākāvasthāprāptānām anāsravadharmāṇāṃ bodhāt jñānaṃ (prajñāpāramitā) vipākadharmatāvasthānāsravadharmaikakṣaṇalakṣaṇo bhavati, ityevakṣaṇābhisambodho dvitīyaḥ / ayaṃ vipākaḥ aṣṭamabhūmerūrdhvaṃ bhavatīti jñeyam /
(la) alakṣaṇalakṣaṇaḥ
asya svarūpādikaṃ sarvam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā suspaṣṭamupavarṇitam / tathā hi -
svapnopameṣu dharmeṣu sthitvā dānādicaryayā /
alakṣaṇatvaṃ dharmāṇāṃ kṣaṇenaikena vindati /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
When, through the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s cultivation of the antidote, through the removal of the stain of all adversaries, the maturation state of the entire purification aspect has arisen as pure in nature — then, the knowledge (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>) arising from the awakening to uncontaminated <s>dharmas</s> that have attained the maturation state in that single moment has the characteristic of the maturation of <s>dharmatā</s>.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
pūrvaṃ svapnopamasarvadharmābhyāsena sambhāradvayamanubhūya adhigamāvasthāyāṃ svapnasvabhāveṣu sarvadharmeṣu upādānaskandhādiṣu sthitvā dānādiṣaṭpāramitāpratipattyā dānādirūpanirūpaṇākāreṇa alakṣaṇāḥ sarvadharmā iti saṃkleśavyavadānarūpāṇāṃ sarvadharmāṇāmekenaiva kṣaṇena alakṣaṇatvaṃ jānāti, ityevam alakṣaṇa sarvadharmaikakṣaṇalakṣaṇo bhavatīti ekakṣaṇābhisambodhastṛtīyaḥ /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
Having previously experienced the twofold accumulation [of merit and knowledge] through the practice of all <s>dharmas</s> as dream-like, and in the state of realization, abiding in all <s>dharmas</s> of dream-like nature such as the aggregates of clinging and the like, through the practice of the six <s>pāramitās</s> of giving and the like, in the aspect of examining [whether] giving and the like [have] form — [the understanding that] all <s>dharmas</s> are without marks, in the form of affliction and purification,

children.text:
(va) advayalakṣaṇaḥ
asyādvayalakṣaṇasya svarūpam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā spaṣṭamupadarśitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
(iv) The characteristic of non-duality.
The nature of this characteristic of non-duality has been clearly shown in one verse in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Thus:

children.text: svapnaṃ taddarśinaṃ caiva dvayayogena nekṣate /
children.translated_text: 'The dream and its perceiver — these it does not regard through the connection of duality;

children.text: dharmāṇāmadvayai tattvaṃ kṣaṇenaikena paśyati //
children.translated_text: the non-dual reality of <s>dharmas</s> it perceives in a single moment.'

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
nirantaradīrghakāladvayapratibhāsaprahāṇābhyāsasātmībhāvād unmīlitadvayapratibhāsavāsano yadā bodhisattvo grāhyagrāhakayogena svapnaṃ grāhyaṃ svapnadarśinaṃ grāhakaṃ nekṣate, tadā sarve 'pyevaṃdharmāṇo dharmā iti dharmāṇāmadvayaṃ tattvamekenaiva kṣaṇena paśyati, ityevam advayalakṣaṇasarvadharmaikakṣaṇalakṣaṇo bhavatyekakṣaṇābhisambodhaścaturthaḥ /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
When, through the habitual practice of abandoning the appearance of duality over a long, uninterrupted time, having become accustomed to it, the <s>bodhisattva</s> whose latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the appearance of duality have been unveiled does not regard the dream — the apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>) — and the dream-perceiver — the apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>) — through the connection of duality, then all <s>dharmas</s> being of this very nature — the non-dual reality of <s>dharmas</s>

children.text:
(kha) nirvacanam
eka ityantimaḥ, kṣaṇamiti samayaḥ, abhirityābhimukhyam, samiti samyak, aya ityadhigama ityevaṃ antimakāle dānādisarvānāsravadharmāṇāmaviparītaḥ samyak prativedhaḥ ekakṣaṇābhisambodha ityucyate /
children.translated_text:
(b) Etymology.
'<s>Eka</s>' means final; '<s>kṣaṇa</s>' means moment; '<s>abhi</s>' means facing; '<s>sam</s>' means correctly; '<s>aya</s>' means realization. Thus, the correct, unerring penetration of all uncontaminated <s>dharmas</s> such as giving and the like at the final moment is called '<s>ekakṣaṇābhisambodha</s>' (single-moment complete awakening).

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
samastānāṃ caturlakṣaṇānāmavadhiḥ antimakṣaṇasthabodhisattvīyāvasthāyāmeva bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Limit.
The limit of all four characteristics falls precisely in the state of the <s>bodhisattva</s> at the final moment.

children.text: // iti ekakṣaṇābhisambodhābhisamayasya aṣṭau dharmāḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [are explained] the eight <s>dharmas</s> of the single-moment complete awakening realization.

children.text: 3. Dharmakāyopalakṣakāścatvāro dharmāḥ
children.translated_text: 3. The four <s>dharmas</s> that are indicators of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body).

children.text: vipākabhūtasya dharmakāyasya saṃkṣiptanirdeśaḥ abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā paridīpitaḥ / tathā hi -
children.translated_text: The condensed description of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> as the matured result has been illuminated in one verse in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Thus:

children.text: svābhāvikaḥ sasāmbhogo nairmāṇiko 'parastathāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>svābhāvika</s> (natural), together with the <s>sāmbhoga</s> (enjoyment), the <s>nairmāṇika</s> (emanation), and the other likewise —

children.text: dharmakāyaḥ sakāritraścaturdhā samudīritaḥ //
children.translated_text: the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, together with its activity, is proclaimed to be fourfold.'

children.text: vistṛtanirdeśastu aṣṭamādhikāre catvāriṃśatkārikābhirvihitaḥ / tatra dharmakāyasya lakṣaṇādikaṃ sarvaṃ svarūpamupavarṇitam /

(ka) lakṣaṇam
sambhāradvayasaṃcayabalena prāptāḥ paryantaguṇā eva phalabhūto dharmakāya iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The ultimate qualities attained through the power of the accumulation of the twofold accumulation [of merit and knowledge], which constitute the result — this is the definition of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
catvāro 'sya bhedā bhavanti, yathā - svabhāvakāyaḥ, jñānadharmakāyaḥ, sambhogakāyaḥ, nirmāṇakāyaśceti catvāraḥ /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
There are four divisions, namely: the <s>svabhāvakāya</s> (nature body), the <s>jñānadharmakāya</s> (knowledge truth-body), the <s>sambhogakāya</s> (enjoyment body), and the <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation body).

children.text:
1. svabhāvakāyaḥ
asya svābhāvikakāyasyopapādanam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā kṛtam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
1. The <s>svabhāvakāya</s> (nature body).
The establishment of this natural body has been accomplished in one verse in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>. Thus:

children.text: sarvākārāṃ viśuddhiṃ ye dharmāḥ prāptā nirāsravāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those uncontaminated <s>dharmas</s> that have attained complete purification in all aspects —

children.text: svābhāviko muneḥ kāyasteṣāṃ prakṛtilakṣaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: the natural body of the Sage has the characteristic of their fundamental nature.'

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
prakṛtyāgantukamalaviśuddhidvayalakṣaṇaḥ paryantadhāturanutpādarūpaḥ svabhāvakāya iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The ultimate element (<s>paryantadhātu</s>), of the nature of non-origination, characterized by the twofold purity of natural purity and purity from adventitious defilements — this is the definition of the <s>svabhāvakāya</s>.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
prakṛtiviśuddhaḥ āgantukaviśuddhaśceti dvau bhedau /
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
The naturally pure and the adventitiously pure — these are the two divisions.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
svabhāvakāyaḥ kevalaṃ buddhabhūmāveva bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Limit.
The <s>svabhāvakāya</s> exists exclusively on the <s>Buddha</s>-ground.

children.text:
2. jñānadharmakāyaḥ
asya jñānakāyasya svarūpam abhisamayālaṅkāre pañcabhiḥ kārikābhirupadarśitam /
children.translated_text:
2. The <s>jñānadharmakāya</s> (knowledge truth-body).
The nature of this knowledge body has been shown in five verses in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
yāvajjñānaṃ yathāvajjñānaṃ cāpekṣya sākṣātkāri paryantajñāna jñānadharmakāya iti lakṣaṇam / jñānadharmakāyaḥ sarvajñajñānaṃ cetyanarthāntaram /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition.
The ultimate knowledge (<s>paryantajñāna</s>) that directly realizes [reality] in terms of 'as much as' (<s>yāvat</s>) knowledge and 'as it is' (<s>yathāvat</s>) knowledge — this is the definition of the <s>jñānadharmakāya</s>. The <s>jñānadharmakāya</s> and the knowledge of the omniscient (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>) are synonymous.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
buddhabhūmau anāsravajñānānāmekaviṃśatiḥ jñānavargā evāsya ekaviṃśatiḥ prabhedāḥ / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
(b) Classification.
On the <s>Buddha</s>-ground, the twenty-one classes of uncontaminated knowledge are the twenty-one subdivisions of this [<s>jñānadharmakāya</s>]. Thus:

children.text:
(1) smṛtyupasthānādyārabhya āryāṣṭāṅgamārgaparyantā saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣāḥ, (2) catvāryapramāṇāni maitryādicaturbrahmavihārāḥ, (3) aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ, (4) navasamāpattayaḥ, (5) kṛtsnāyatanāni daśa (6) aṣṭau abhibhvāyatanāni, (7) araṇāsamādhiḥ, (8) praṇidhijñānam, (9) ṣaḍabhijñāḥ, (10)catasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ, (11) āśrayālambanacittajñānapariśuddhaya iti cataśraḥ śuddhayaḥ, (12) daśa vaśitāḥ, (13) daśa balāni, (14) catvāri vaiśāradyāni, (15) trīṇi arakṣaṇāni, (16) trīṇi smṛtyupasthānāni, (17) asammoṣadharmatā, (18) kleśajñeyāvaraṇānuśayarūpabījaprahāṇāt vāsanāsamudghātaḥ, (19) sakalajanahitāśayatā mahākaruṇā, (20) aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmāḥ, (21) sarvākārajñatāditrisarvajñatā /
tathā coktam abhisamayālaṅkāre -
children.translated_text:
(1) The thirty-seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>), from the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) up to the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>); (2) the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), namely the four divine abidings (<s>brahmavihāra</s>) beginning with loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>); (3) the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>); (4) the nine attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>); (5) ten totality-bases (<s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>); (6) eight bases of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>); (7) the <s>araṇāsamādhi</s> (concentration of non-conflict); (8) <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> (aspiration-knowledge); (9) the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>); (10) the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>); (11) the four purifications (<s>śuddhi</s>), namely the purifications of basis (<s>āśraya</s>), object (<s>ālambana</s>), mind (<s>citta</s>), and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>); (12) the ten masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>); (13) the ten powers (<s>bala</s>); (14) the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>); (15) the three non-guardednesses (<s>arakṣaṇa</s>); (16) the three foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>); (17) the nature of non-forgetfulness (<s>asammoṣadharmatā</s>); (18) the eradication of latent impressions (<s>vāsanāsamudghāta</s>), through the abandonment of the seeds in the form of latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) of the obstructions of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>); (19) great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), the intention for the welfare of all people; (20) the eighteen distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-qualities (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>); (21) the three knowledges (<s>trisarvajñatā</s>) beginning with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects).
As stated in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>:

children.text: bodhipakṣāpramāṇāni vimokṣā anupūrvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>), the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), in sequence,

children.text: navātmikā samāpattiḥ kṛtsnaṃ daśavidhātmakam //
children.translated_text: the ninefold attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>), the totality (<s>kṛtsna</s>) of tenfold nature,

children.text: abhibhvāyatanānyaṣṭaprakārāṇi prabhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: the bases of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>) of eight kinds by division,

children.text: araṇā praṇidhijñānamabhijñāḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>araṇā</s> (non-conflict [concentration]), <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> (aspiration-knowledge), the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>),

children.text: sarvākārāścatasro 'tha śuddhayo vaśitā daśa /
children.translated_text: all aspects, and then the four purifications (<s>śuddhi</s>), the ten masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>),

children.text: balāni daśa catvāri vaiśāradyānyarakṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: the ten powers (<s>bala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the non-guardedness (<s>arakṣaṇa</s>)

children.text: trividhaṃ smṛtyupasthānaṃ tridhā 'saṃmoṣadharmatā /
children.translated_text: threefold, the threefold foundation of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the nature of non-forgetfulness (<s>asammoṣadharmatā</s>),

children.text: vāsanāyāḥ samudghāto mahatī karuṇā jane //
children.translated_text: the eradication of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), great compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) toward beings,

children.text: āveṇikā munereva dharmā ye 'ṣṭādaśeritāḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>dharmas</s> that are distinctive (<s>āveṇika</s>) of the Sage alone, stated as eighteen,

children.text: sarvākārajñatā ceti dharmākāyo 'bhidhīyate //
children.translated_text: and <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects) — [all these together] are called the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth body).

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
buddhabhūmāveva jñānadharmakāyo bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The <s>jñānadharmakāya</s> (knowledge truth body) exists only at the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage).

children.text:
3. sambhogakāyaḥ
sambhogakāyasya svarūpavarṇanam abhisamayālaṅkāre ekayā kārikayā kṛtam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
3. <s>Sambhogakāya</s> (enjoyment body)
The description of the essential nature of the <s>sambhogakāya</s> is made in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through a single verse. Namely:

children.text: dvātriṃśallakṣaṇāśītivyañjanātmā munerayam /
children.translated_text: Consisting of the thirty-two marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) and eighty minor marks (<s>vyañjana</s>), this [body] of the Sage

children.text: sāmbhogiko mataḥ kāyo mahāyānopabhogataḥ //
children.translated_text: is considered the <s>sāmbhogika</s> (enjoyment) body, due to the enjoyment of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
sthānakāyaparivāradharmakālākhyaiḥ pañcabhirviniyatairvirśiṣṭaḥ kāyaḥ sambhogakāya iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of the <s>sambhogakāya</s> is: a body distinguished by five certainties called place (<s>sthāna</s>), body (<s>kāya</s>), retinue (<s>parivāra</s>), <s>dharma</s>, and time (<s>kāla</s>).

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
mahāsambhogakāyaḥ kaniṣṭhasambhogakāyaśceti bhedadvayamabhidhānadṛṣṭyā kartuṃ śakyate / tatra mahāsambhogakāyaḥ akaniṣṭhabhaumikaḥ sambhogakāya ityanarthāntaram / tathaiva kaniṣṭhasambhogakāyaḥ akaniṣṭhabhaumikau nirmāṇakāyaścetyanarthāntaram /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
Two divisions can be made from the perspective of designation: the great <s>sambhogakāya</s> and the minor <s>sambhogakāya</s>. Of these, the great <s>sambhogakāya</s> is synonymous with the <s>sambhogakāya</s> belonging to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> level. Likewise, the minor <s>sambhogakāya</s> is synonymous with both the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>-level [bodies] and the <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation body).

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
ayaṃ sambhogakāyo buddhabhūmau akaniṣṭhaghanavyūhakṣetre eva kevalaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
This <s>sambhogakāya</s> exists exclusively at the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage), only in the <s>Akaniṣṭhaghanavyūhakṣetra</s> (Akaniṣṭha Dense Array buddha-field).

children.text:
4. nirmāṇakāyaḥ
kāyasyāsya nairmāṇikasya svarūpam abhisamayālaṅkāre kārikayā ekayā samyagupavarṇitam / tathā hi -
children.translated_text:
4. <s>Nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation body)
The essential nature of this <s>nairmāṇika</s> (emanation) body is properly described in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through a single verse. Namely:

children.text: karoti yena citrāṇi hitāni jagataḥ samam /
children.translated_text: By which he performs various beneficial [deeds] equally for the world,

children.text: ā bhavāt so 'nupacchinnaḥ kāyo nairmāṇiko muneḥ //
children.translated_text: uninterrupted until [the end of] existence — that is the <s>nairmāṇika</s> (emanation) body of the Sage.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
pañcabhirviniyatairvirahitaḥ paryantarūpakāyo nirmāṇakāya iti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of the <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> is: the ultimate <s>rūpakāya</s> (form body) that is devoid of the five certainties.

children.text: yena śākyamunitathāgatādirūpeṇa āsaṃsāraṃ sarvalokadhātuṣu sattvānāṃ samīhitamarthaṃ samaṃ karoti, asau kāyaḥ prabandhatayā anuparato nairmāṇiko buddhasya bhagavataḥ sarvabālajanasādhāraṇaścaturtho 'vasātavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the form of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> and the like, it equally accomplishes the desired purpose of beings in all world-realms for as long as <s>saṃsāra</s> [lasts]. This body, being continuous and unceasing, is the <s>nairmāṇika</s> (emanation body) of the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, the fourth [body], common to all ordinary beings.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
nirmāṇakāyasya trayo bhedā bhavanti, yathā - uttamanirmāṇakāyaḥ, śailpikanirmāṇakāyaḥ, nairyāṇikanirmāṇakāyaśceti /
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
There are three divisions of the <s>nirmāṇakāya</s>: the supreme <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (<s>uttamanirmāṇakāya</s>), the artisan <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (<s>śailpikanirmāṇakāya</s>), and the birth <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (<s>nairyāṇikanirmāṇakāya</s>).

children.text: buddhakāritrāṇi
children.translated_text: The activities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhakāritrāṇi</s>)

children.text: imāni bhagavato vicitrāṇi kāritrāṇi abhisamayālaṅkāre saptabhiḥ kārikābhirvistaraśo nirdiṣṭāni /
children.translated_text: These various activities of the <s>Bhagavān</s> are indicated in detail in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s> through seven verses.

children.text:
(ka) lakṣaṇam
svasantatisthasarvākārajñatādhipatyenodayamāsāditāḥ śuklā guṇā eva buddhakāritrāṇīti lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text:
(a) Definition
The definition of <s>Buddha</s>-activities is: the wholesome qualities that have arisen through the mastery of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects) abiding in one's own continuum.

children.text:
(kha) bhedaḥ
gatipraśamanakāritrata ārabhya nirvāṇaniveśanaparyantaṃ saptaviṃśatiḥ karmāṇyevāsya saptaviṃśatiḥ prabhedā bhavanti / yathoktamabhisamayālaṅkāre saptaviṃśatiḥ karitrāṇi -
children.translated_text:
(b) Divisions
From the activity of pacifying the [lower] destinies up to the activity of establishing [beings] in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, there are twenty-seven activities, and these constitute the twenty-seven divisions. As stated in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, the twenty-seven activities are:

children.text: tathā karmāpyanucchinnamasyāsaṃsāramiṣyate /
children.translated_text: Likewise, its activity is considered uninterrupted throughout <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: gatīnāṃ śamanaṃ karmaṃ saṃgrahe ca caturvidhe //
children.translated_text: The activity of pacifying the [lower] destinies, and in the fourfold means of attraction (<s>saṃgraha</s>),

children.text: niveśanaṃ sasaṃkleśe vyavadānāvabodhane /
children.translated_text: establishing [beings] in that which is afflicted (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and in the awakening to purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>),

children.text: sattvānāmarthayāthātmye ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu ca //
children.translated_text: in the true nature of the welfare of beings, and in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),

children.text: buddhamārge prakṛtyaiva śūnyatāyāṃ dvayakṣaye /
children.translated_text: in the <s>Buddha</s>-path, in the emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) that is by nature [present], in the extinction of duality,

children.text: saṃkete 'nupalambhe ca paripāke ca dehinām //
children.translated_text: in convention (<s>saṃketa</s>), in non-apprehension, and in the ripening (<s>paripāka</s>) of embodied beings,

children.text: bodhisattvasya mārgo 'bhiniveśasya nivāraṇe /
children.translated_text: in the path of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, in the prevention of clinging (<s>abhiniveśa</s>),

children.text: bodhiprāptau jinakṣetraviśuddhau niyatiṃ prati //
children.translated_text: in the attainment of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), in the purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field (<s>jinakṣetra</s>), in relation to certainty (<s>niyati</s>),

children.text: aprameye ca sattvārthe buddhasevādike guṇe /
children.translated_text: and in the immeasurable welfare of beings, in qualities such as attending upon <s>Buddhas</s> and the like,

children.text: bodheraṅgeṣvanāśe ca karmaṇāṃ satyadarśane //
children.translated_text: in the limbs of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), in the indestructibility of actions, in the seeing of truth,

children.text: viparyāsaprahāṇe ca tadavastukatānaye /
children.translated_text: in the abandonment of perversions (<s>viparyāsa</s>) and in the principle of the insubstantiality of those [perversions],

children.text: vyavadāne sasambhāre saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛte prati //
children.translated_text: in purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) together with the accumulations (<s>sambhāra</s>), with respect to the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>),

children.text: vyatibhedāparijñāne nirvāṇe va niveśanam /
children.translated_text: in the comprehension of non-differentiation, and the establishing [of beings] in <s>nirvāṇa</s> —

children.text: dharmakāyasya karmedaṃ saptaviṃśatidhā matam //
children.translated_text: this activity of the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth body) is considered to be twenty-sevenfold.

children.text:
(ga) avadhiḥ
mārge 'praveśādārabhya buddhabhūmiparyantamasyāvadhirbhavati /
children.translated_text:
(c) Scope
The scope of this extends from [the time of] non-entry into the path up to the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage).

children.text:
(gha) vaiśiṣṭyam
vineyajanakarmānusāraṃ bhagavataḥ kāyavāṅmanaḥkāritrāṇi ākāśavad atyudārāṇi, nadīdhārāvad avicchinnāni, samudrataraṅgavat kālānatikramaṇalakṣaṇāni, cintāmaṇikalpavṛkṣādivad anābhogarūpāṇi bhavanti /
children.translated_text:
(d) Distinction
The <s>Bhagavān</s>'s activities of body, speech, and mind, in accordance with the actions of those to be trained (<s>vineyajana</s>), are supremely magnificent like space, uninterrupted like the current of a river, of the nature of not transgressing time like the waves of the ocean, and effortless in nature like a wish-fulfilling gem or a wish-fulfilling tree.

children.text:
(ṅa) avadhiḥ
vineyajanapratibhāsabhāk saptaviṃśatiprakāraṃ karma avicchinnatayā āsaṃsāraṃ pravartate /
children.translated_text:
(e) Scope
The twenty-seven types of activity, appearing to those to be trained, operate uninterruptedly throughout <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: // iti dharmakāyopakṣakāścatvāro dharmāḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus the four <s>dharmas</s> characterizing the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth body).

children.text: pariṇāmanā
children.translated_text: Dedication (<s>pariṇāmanā</s>)

children.text: prajñāpāramitopalakṣakāṇāṃ sarvākārajñātādyaṣṭānām, aṣṭapadārthopalakṣakāṇāṃ ca saptateḥ padārthānāṃ prakāśakamidaṃ subhāṣitaṃ jagadguroḥ maitreyanāthasya mukhānniḥ-sṛtasyāgamasya caturdikṣuḥ prasārāya lokasya ca sanmārgārohaṇāya prabhavediti pariṇāmanā / ācāryaharibhadravacanena tu -
children.translated_text: May this excellent discourse, which illuminates the eight [topics] beginning with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge of all aspects) that characterize the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and the seventy topics that characterize the eight [main] topics — [this discourse] having issued from the mouth of <s>Maitreyanātha</s>, the teacher of the world — spread in the four directions for the world's ascent to the true path. This is the dedication. In the words of <s>Ācārya Haribhadra</s>, however:

children.text:
tathyātathyavibhāgayuktivikalajñānodayātsaṃvṛtau
saṃsārārṇavapaṅkamagnamanasī jātāḥ sadā dehinaḥ / sarve 'mī jananīnibandhanakṛtād bījānmayāptācchubhāt sarvākāravarā bhavantu niyataṃ kāyatrayaprāpiṇaḥ //
children.translated_text:
In conventional [truth], due to the arising of knowledge deficient in the reasoning that discriminates between the true and the false,
embodied beings have always been with their minds sunk in the mire of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
May all of these, through the wholesome seed obtained by me from the bond of the mother [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>],
certainly become those who attain the three bodies (<s>kāyatraya</s>), supreme in all aspects.

children.text: iti śam om
children.translated_text: Thus, may there be peace. <s>Oṃ</s>.
